breakdown: Two-panel vertical split on a shared marble background, 1:1-ish crop. Left: young woman with wet, greasy, flattened hair, neutral-to-glum expression — the wrong state. Right: same-role woman with voluminous curled hair holding the cream-white electric spray comb (button and indicator visible) up to her hair — the resolved state with the product as the visible explanation. Argument structure is wrong-state vs answer in one glance, i.e. job=pain, device=split, closest to the --mirror shape because the right side is a person in the corrected state with the product secondary-to-prominent. It deviates from the base skeleton by three softenings that look deliberate for a beauty vertical: no X/check badges, no grayscale on the wrong side, and the product held mid-use. G4 still holds (right side brighter, airier); G5 holds (both photographic, same background and lighting register); G7 holds (hand-held comb in a plausible use moment). Hypothesis for curation: a 'soft/beauty' presentation register where hard judgment marks (badges, grayscale) would cheapen an aesthetic category — one observation, no action until the >=3 evidence threshold. Likely a real listing/ad image of the actual product; useful later as a reference for the product's face, though not a clean packshot.

Single photographic frame, zero graphic overlays, wide-ish crop. A woman in her 30s-40s in pajama bottoms and a t-shirt stands at a bathroom counter looking directly into the lens with drawn brows and a pressed, frustrated mouth — restrained everyday frustration, not theatrical pain. Symptom evidence per the G9 hierarchy: rank 1, the frizzy tangled hair itself; rank 3, the pink comb still in her raised hand as the failed tool; plus one hand pulling a strand. Environment is a lived-in bathroom with toothbrush cup, toothpaste tubes, towels and plants — real clutter signaling a disrupted morning routine. A mirror behind her shows her from the back, doubling the symptom evidence exactly as the optional [MIRROR] slot prescribes. Light is even, bright, flat daylight; palette desaturated neutrals; no red anywhere; nothing signals advertising and no product is present. This is a clean match for 01-pain-scene --confront with every v1.1 slot satisfied — it appears to be the very seed exemplar that produced the --confront variant (seed conversation.md), now formally ledgered as its first evidence. Rendering style suggests it is itself AI-generated, which does not affect its value as a structural exemplar.

No comparison, no person, no symptom — it exhibits rather than argues, sitting on the step-3 tier beside ghostbody (inside the body) and spec-split (component combat). Blue/cyan dominance reads as correct-mechanism under G3; the copper-orange traces are decorative but sit in tension with G3's orange=wrong-pressure if reused as signal. In-image text present (spec label) — a claim and a model-weakness both; the library version of this type must externalize numbers. G7 exempt (technical render register). Likely sourced from the product's own listing gallery.

deviations.observed: no person as subject — only a wary hand entering frame; the indicted OBJECT (old wall outlet with exposed tangled wires) is the protagonist

The argument is not 'recognize your felt pain' (no person, no symptom on a body) but 'look at what the old way actually involves' — indicting an object in daily life, which is job=cause, delivered through the documentary scene device (job cause + device scene has no existing type; 02-cause-anatomy is its illustrated sibling). G9 logic transfers: the hazard is physical fact in frame, the hand carries hesitation, no red signal graphics needed — the exposed copper does the work. Low-key cinematic grade, lived-in grime, nothing staged-looking; G7 passes (a mid-repair moment anyone recognizes). Fits the advertorial 'old way' beat before a no-wiring product answer. First exemplar for candidate 02-cause-scene. Product domain context: mist air cooler funnel (traditional AC installation pain).

deviations.observed: invisible force (electrical arc/interference) visualized as a bright teal glowing arc with concentric rings and purple sparks composited over a photographic wall cavity — a graphic-FX layer on a real scene; no existing device covers this (flagged: new device value `aura` would need a vocabulary gate)

Proposed as 02-cause-aura with the new device value flagged for the vocabulary gate — per governance this record accumulates evidence and changes nothing until reviewed. G3 tension: teal/cyan is used here for DANGER, colliding with blue=correct in the library palette — any adopted skeleton must flip the hazard color to red/orange. One exemplar; the aesthetic skews dramatic and may read as fearmongering on marketplace channels — advertorial-leaning. Product domain: mist air cooler funnel.

breakdown: Single cinematic frame, no overlays: a man in his 50s crouches in a dark basement beside two aged breaker panels, a single bare bulb overhead, pipes and joists in shadow. His face is turned to the lens with a drained, troubled expression — restrained, not theatrical — landing this as gaze=confront. Symptom evidence per G9: the environment itself is the evidence (old panels, sticker-covered doors, bare-bulb infrastructure), rank-1 on-object condition; his posture (elbow on knee, hand slack) carries resignation. Low-key warm key from the bulb, deep shadow across most of the frame, desaturated amber-grey grade, film-still character — everything else matches 01-pain-scene cleanly. The one structural surprise is the gaze/light pairing: current variant definitions bundle confront with flat daylight, but this image demonstrates confront+low-key working (the basement is where the problem lives; daylight would be false). Logged as a deviation for the >=2/3 rule — if it recurs, the patch is to decouple gaze and light into independent axes rather than variant bundles. G7 passes; no red, no product. Product domain: mist air cooler funnel.

Recorded under in-use for the lit-state evidence, with the mode boundary noted for drafting (in-use may need a 'powered' sub-branch rather than a fourth mode). Job=social, device=snapshot; authenticity texture is maximal — underexposure, color cast and noise would all be faults in a commercial register and are credentials here. deviations.observed: tenth exemplar, at-rest (held) mode: the drive held up over a grey couch with its USB cable coiled beside and a tablet at the frame edge — third distinct room for one product, live proof of the set-diversity law

Mode is at-rest in its held execution (showing the thing to the camera rather than using it); the coiled cable plays the single-anchor role. Job=social, device=snapshot; hand as incidental limb; low, honest light. Same reviewer family as r8-r9 for source counting. Ratio 5:3, low-res review thumbnail. Fifth distinct source family for the candidate — the furniture-mover vertical, richly known to the ledger through its commercial composites (batch 2026-08-10-G) and now grounded by its first real-UGC record; with five families across five verticals, the §6.3 distinct-sources requirement is substantively met, leaving the router-confusion test and a rendered worked example as the candidate's open criteria. deviations.observed: twelfth exemplar, in-use mode: the red lever's roller head wedged under a white dresser leg mid-lift on wood flooring — the tool photographed at its exact working moment by its owner

deviations.observed: dark moody tech grade throughout — the skeleton's register is warm lifestyle photography; this execution trades warmth for gadget-noir while keeping every structural law

breakdown: Vertical three-panel stack, thin gutters, no numbers, no arrows, no text: top, hands plug the coiled black cable into a phone held close; middle, the slim probe snakes into an open wall cavity between studs and insulation, its LED tip lit; bottom, the phone lies landscape showing the live camera view from inside a wet drain pipe. The order reads by action alone — connect, insert, see — and the final panel closes on the payoff rather than mechanics, exactly the sequence device's law set. Job=use answering will-I-manage for a phone endoscope, the product class whose whole anxiety is operation. The phone screens are diegetic UI (G6 scope) — the drain view IS the product's output, and the production law applies to any generated execution: screen content composited, never model-drawn. G8 is honored in the middle panel (the LED tip visibly lit in the dark cavity — the emitting module shown active). The single deviation is register: a dark technical grade against the type's warm-lifestyle line — structural laws all hold, so this is execution dialect worth tracking, not a variant. Camera drifts naturally between panels (handheld ✓). Ratio ~10:13, inside the 4:5 family. Hands render clean. Product domain: phone endoscope camera — new vertical for the ledger.

deviations.observed: FIFTH exemplar (5/5): the entire x-ray runs in the product's brand ORANGE — amber ghost shell, glowing amber internals — against the candidate's navy-and-cyan palette lock, and in G3 tension (orange = wrong-pressure); one observation, below any patch threshold, logged for the palette-lock evidence base

a white circular inset top-right repeats the see-through view at wider framing (both wheels + neon triangle brace glow) — second exemplar carrying a companion cell beside the single-subject core (after sha256:6735f5…)

breakdown: Extreme close 3D render of the ab-roller's wheel with its shell gone translucent: the internal rebound SPRING COIL and hub spokes rendered solid and glowing inside the amber ghost drum, every wire of the coil resolved; top-right, a rounded white inset shows the double-wheel assembly see-through at wider scale, a neon triangle tracing the elbow-support brace between the wheels. The argument is strict mechanism: WHY the roller assists the return stroke — a spring inside stores the push and gives it back — justified by showing the inside of the intact object, which is the xray candidate's exact definition (product translucent, internals solid; it exhibits, it does not compare). This is the FIFTH distinct exemplar from a fifth product vertical (spray comb, optical drive, electric cutter, mini chopper, now ab roller) — the §6.3 exemplar count is met. Register returns to the majority form (full 3D see-through render; 4 of 5 now, the photo-overlay form stays a 1/3 variant observation). The palette deviation matters: brand-orange x-ray inverts the draft's navy/cyan lock and grazes G3 (orange = wrong pressure) — as one observation it changes nothing, but the promoted type's palette-lock line should expect brand-colored market executions and hold the line. No text, no people; the inset's neon triangle is annotation-glow, sanctioned-adjacent. Ratio 1:1. Product domain: ab roller with elbow support — new vertical.

deviations.observed: second exemplar for the explode candidate (2/5), in a new execution: the exploded view lives INSIDE a circular inset — six material layers of the wheel fanned like a book, each swatch textured — over a packshot base, not as the full frame

the fanned layers carry small numbered digits 1-6 — overlay numerals on the image; production law applies (composite in post), and the candidate's skeleton must decide whether layer indices are ever generated

The argument is a construction census: what the wheel is MADE of, layer by layer — job=spec argued by inventory, which is the explode candidate's exact logic (batch 2026-08-11-B, exemplar 1: the speaker puck full-frame explode). The execution differs structurally: explode-as-inset over a packshot rather than explode-as-frame — the candidate's skeleton will need a framing decision (full-frame | inset) the way relief-hero parameterizes insets. Same product family as the xray exemplar this batch — one campaign feeding two step-3 candidates with two different interiors (spring mechanism vs material stack), a tidy demonstration that xray answers WHY and explode answers WHAT. Under G3 the palette is brand-orange plus neutral swatches, no signal claim. Ratio 1:1. Product domain: ab roller with elbow support.

deviations.observed: fourth exemplar (4/5): the band runs along the BOTTOM as six circular muscle-map badges (torso/arm diagrams with orange-lit zones) — band content mode #4, TARGETED MUSCLES, and the first band rendered as ILLUSTRATION against a photographic hero
the hero zone is itself a diptych — product packshot with phone mounted (left) against a sunlit bare-midriff torso (right) — rather than one scene

breakdown: Composite tile: upper two-thirds pairs the orange ab roller (a phone clipped to its bracket playing a workout video) with a separate sunlit shot of a lean bare midriff in a pink sports bra; along the bottom run six dark circular badges, each a line-drawn body diagram with a muscle group lit orange — abs, obliques, shoulders, back, arms, legs. Two structural strains are the payload: the band is illustrated while the hero is photographic — the register-mix failure symptom-rail's G5 law exists to prevent, now observed on the positive-polarity side too — and the band count is six, double the legibility law's three. The hero's diptych construction (product | aspiration body) is persuasion shorthand, not scene logic — closer to collage than hero, and the aspiration torso quietly imports a body-result claim that G9 would demand evidence for. The phone-on-product is diegetic screen content (composite in post per production law). Ratio 1:1. Product domain: ab roller with elbow support — third image of the family this batch.

deviations.observed: third exemplar (3/5) inverts the candidate's framing: the MACRO lives in a circular inset (the rotating clamp dial, magnified, with a drawn blue rotation arrow) while the product beauty shot dominates — macro-as-inset, and the magnified subject is a MECHANISM detail, not material texture

breakdown: Marketplace tile on a stylized ice-and-snow backdrop: the white handheld clip fan angled hero-size, its fan face frosted with droplets, LED readout showing 199, power ring visible; bottom-left, a circular magnifier inset zooms the underside clamp with its knurled adjustment dial, a drawn blue arrow tracing the dial's rotation. The argument family is component-level quality and feature proof — job=spec — but this third exemplar stretches the macro candidate on two axes at once: framing (the magnification is an inset on a packshot, not the dominant frame — the same inversion the explode candidate logged this batch) and subject (a working mechanism with an operation arrow, not a material surface). Drafting will have to rule whether 03-spec-macro means texture-as-argument narrowly (then this is a different callout genre) or magnification-as-argument broadly (then framing and subject are slot parameters); recorded against macro as the nearest magnification candidate, with the scope question flagged rather than resolved. The 199 readout is diegetic device UI; the rotation arrow is overlay annotation; the ice field is a declared visual metaphor for cold — G7 does not bind graphic-register backdrops, but the metaphor imports a cooling-power claim no physics in-frame supports. Ratio 1:1. Product domain: handheld/clip portable fan — the store's cooling vertical, second product.

deviations.observed: the waistband cell carries drawn pale-blue airflow lines curving into the lifted shirt — a graphic overlay inside a device defined as overlay-free collage

breakdown: Clean 2x2 photographic grid of the lilac clip fan across four personas and mounts: a laughing baby in a stroller with the fan clipped to the bumper bar; a visor-wearing hiker with it clipped to a backpack strap; a cyclist's handlebars with the fan band-mounted; a runner's waistband with the fan clipped blowing up into her lifted shirt, airflow drawn as pale blue lines. Persona breadth is the argument — from infant to athlete, stroller to bicycle — with the mount system as the connective tissue: every cell restates clip-anywhere, so use-versatility rides inside persona casting (a cleaner fusion than the drill-compatibility grid managed, since people stay present). All four cells photographic, product visible above the 15% floor everywhere, personas differ maximally (the baby cell is the widest casting reach in the ledger), grades cohere within tolerance. One deviation: the drawn airflow in the waistband cell — an overlay on the overlay-free device, and a borderline G8 case: moving air is invisible, so the lines annotate a real but unseeable output; under the no-invented-effects reading they are annotation, not fabrication, but they still break the grid's own law. Ratio 1:1, commercial register, no text. Product domain: handheld/clip portable fan — second image of the product this batch.

deviations.observed: third exemplar (3/5), the full-frame execution again: the mini camera's parts float in a vertical exploded stack — clear top shell with red-ringed lens module, populated PCB, gold-foil battery cell, black lower case with USB-C — over a circuit-board canvas with cyan traces

The canvas language — dark engineering field, dim circuit traces — is shared vocabulary with the promoted xray aesthetic, useful evidence that step-3 technical renders converge on one house register. The lens ring's red glow is the device's real recording indicator, not a pain signal — G3-neutral as product identity, worth one line in any future skeleton so red-ring optics do not get policed out. No text, no people, no invented modules apparent (lens, board, battery, shell — a plausible minimal census). Ratio 16:9. Product domain: mini security/body camera — new vertical for the ledger.

deviations.observed: the siphon hose is traced end-to-end by a running chain of small yellow spark-glints — an invented luminous effect on a product whose real output (diesel moving through a tube) is invisible; G8's do-not-invent clause is broken rather than its light-for-the-output clause

breakdown: Low-angle jobsite scene against clear sky: a man in a black hard hat stands on an aluminium ladder at the flank of a yellow excavator, holding a red-nozzled fuel gun into the machine's tank port, while a clear siphon hose runs down from his hands to a small pump unit seated on a blue plastic drum at the frame's foot. The sell is the relief state of refuelling heavy equipment without lifting jerry cans — job=relief, device=hero, commercial register, no inset, product visible at the working end of the hose. The single deviation is the effect layer: a chain of yellow sparkles chases along the whole length of the hose, and fuel flowing inside a translucent tube produces no light whatsoever. This is the cleanest invented-emission exemplar the ledger has: the type's negative already bans 'invented spray or mist' and G8 says do not invent an effect when nothing is visible, so the image documents exactly the failure those clauses exist to prevent. Useful as a teaching pair against the genuine-output exemplars (mist, foam, water). Otherwise conforming: no text, no badges, the ladder and drum are plausibly placed (G7 holds), palette is neutral yellow-blue with the sparkles as the only signal-adjacent colour, and G3 has no pain/relief claim to bind. Ratio 1:1 marketplace tile. Product domain: fuel transfer pump — new vertical for the ledger (eleventh).

deviations.observed: NEW device value `companion` (not in vocabulary — flagged): the product and its phone app shown TOGETHER in one frame, joined by drawn wifi arcs, the phone screen carrying the live multi-camera feed — the argument is the pairing itself, not a step sequence
a picture-in-picture thumbnail bottom-right repeats the whole scene at small scale — a self-referential inset with no informational job

breakdown: Car-interior composite: a hand holds a phone at the left showing the dashcam app with a large road view and four labelled sub-feeds (Front, Rear, Left, Right); at the right the three-lens dashcam sits suction-mounted on the windscreen above the dash, and blue wifi arcs drawn between them carry the connection. Bottom-right, a small rectangular thumbnail repeats the same scene in miniature. The argument is that the device and your phone are one system: pair it and the footage is in your hand — job=use in its will-I-manage sense, but the device is neither a step sequence (03-use-sequence) nor equal cells (03-use-grid candidate) nor a hero-plus-band (03-use-rail candidate). What defines it is the two-object pairing with a drawn connection between them, so it is proposed as a new device value `companion`, flagged for the taxonomy gate. First exemplar (1/5). Router-confusion note for the future draft: the nearest active type by job is 03-use-sequence, and the boundary is temporal — sequence shows steps in order, companion shows one persistent relationship. The phone screen is diegetic UI carrying the core claim, so the production law applies: composite the interface, never model-draw it (the sub-feed labels here are already soft). The self-referential thumbnail is pure decoration and would go into the candidate's negative list, not its skeleton. Blue arcs annotate a real but invisible signal (the same annotation-of-invisible-emission family as the NCV arcs and the wearable-puck arcs already in the ledger); under G3 blue reads mechanism, correctly. Ratio 1:1. Product domain: three-lens dashcam — new vertical (twelfth).

deviations.observed: the protagonist is an ANTAGONIST, not the buyer: a masked thief mid break-in, shot so the viewer watches the threat rather than recognising themselves in it — pain-scene's whole mechanism (self-recognition) is inverted
a white crosshair reticle locked on the thief plus a cyan translucent detection wedge sweeping from the car — surveillance-HUD graphics on a device family defined as zero-overlay

breakdown: Night scene in a dark garage: a masked man in a black beanie and gloves leans into a grey car's driver window with a slim tool, one hand on the glass; a large white crosshair reticle sits over his torso and a translucent cyan wedge sweeps from the car's mirror across him, reading as a camera's field of view catching him in the act. The image sells fear of a specific event rather than recognition of a lived symptom, which is why it will not sit on 01-pain-scene despite sharing step 1: pain-scene's law is that the viewer sees THEMSELVES (G9 physical evidence on the buyer's own body or objects), while this frames a third-party aggressor and asks the viewer to imagine the loss. That is a distinct argument structure worth its own name — proposed 01-pain-threat, first exemplar (1/5) — and it comes with a governance question the gate must answer before anything is drafted: fear-of-crime imagery is a persuasion register the library has never sanctioned, and a type that legitimises staged criminals invites exactly the theatre the fairness rules elsewhere forbid. The HUD overlays are the second structural break: scene-register types carry zero graphic layers by definition, and here the reticle and detection cone are doing the arguing. Register is cinematic-dark, the antagonist's face is deliberately unreadable, no text anywhere. Under G3 cyan reads mechanism (the camera's vision) rather than pain, and no red appears despite the threat framing — the palette is calmer than the content. Ratio 1:1. Product domain: dashcam / vehicle security camera — same vertical as the other two dashcam images this batch.

deviations.observed: the recall cell is FULL COLOUR and carries no desaturation and no red X — the past-state marking law is broken outright, so a crash photo floats unlabelled beside a night-driving hero
in place of a product view, a large golden shield-and-padlock emblem glows over the device — a trust glyph occupying the product-view layer

breakdown: Interior night-driving hero shot from the back seat: the three-lens dashcam is suction-mounted on the windscreen, tail lights and lane markings streaking ahead through the glass, the dashboard and seat backs framing the view. Top-left sits a rectangular inset of a two-car front-end collision in daylight, debris on the asphalt; over the dashcam itself floats a large amber shield emblem with a padlock. Job=relief (drive protected, the footage is being taken care of), device=hero, commercial register, and the inset is doing recall work — a reminder of the event you are insuring against. Two deviations carry the evidence. First, the recall cell breaks the type's central law: v1.5 requires the past state to be desaturated OR carry a red X, because an unmarked past cell reads as a result — and here a crash photo sits in full colour beside a calm hero, which at a glance can read as something the product caused rather than prevented. This is the first ledgered exemplar of that exact failure, and it is worth citing the next time the marking law is questioned. Second, the shield emblem occupies the Zone B slot without doing Zone B's job (revealing a hidden angle); it is a trust glyph, of the family the ledger has now seen several times (green checks, thumbs, verified badges) and which curation keeps excluding. Under G3 amber/gold sits outside the sanctioned signal set entirely — neither pain nor mechanism, purely a marketing warmth cue. No text. Ratio 1:1. Product domain: three-lens dashcam.

deviations.observed: fourth exemplar (4/5) and the first with NO product context at all: two extreme close-ups of the trainer's foot-pedal and grip stacked in one frame, dashed outlines and curved white arrows annotating how the pedal flexes and the grip rotates — construction detail argued by annotated macro rather than by resolved texture

breakdown: Two macro fragments on a pink studio ground: the upper two-thirds show the pedal cradle at very close range — grey ribbed footplate seated in a pink polymer arch, a dashed white outline tracing the arch's travel and a curved arrow at its hinge; the lower third shows the grey foam handgrip in extreme close-up with a second curved arrow wrapping it. Nothing else is in frame: no person, no whole product, no scene. The argument is construction quality at component scale — how the parts move and how they are built — which is job=spec, and the delivery is magnification, placing it on the 03-spec-macro candidate as a fourth exemplar. It also sharpens the scope question the candidate's 0.1 draft deliberately parked: exemplars 1-2 argue through RESOLVED TEXTURE with no annotation (gold carving disc, drill-shear gear teeth), exemplar 3 was macro-as-inset with a rotation arrow, and this one is annotated macro filling the whole frame. Two axes of variation now exist — framing (frame vs inset) and annotation (bare vs arrowed) — and the draft's SCOPE RULING currently admits only bare dominant-frame macro. Curation must either widen the type to macro-as-argument broadly, or split the annotated-callout genre off; this record is the third datapoint pushing that decision. The dashed outlines and arrows are overlay graphics the current negative list excludes ('no glow rims, badges, colour-coded highlights' — arrows are not yet named there, an omission worth closing). Brand-pink ground is decorative; under G3 nothing claims pain or mechanism. No text. Ratio 1:1. Product domain: pedal resistance rope trainer.

deviations.observed: money props ON the wrong panel — a heaped pile of gold coins and a cash sack composited into the top-left sky of the old-way half, with a red falling-arrow-and-coins motif on the answer half; the --oldway variant's negative list bans money props by name

breakdown: Wide 2:1 split down the centre. Left, desaturated near-monochrome: a man sits in a car at night in the rain holding a bulky legacy diagnostic tablet trailing a thick cable harness, reading a dense fault list, brow furrowed — with a large heap of gold coins and a money sack floating in the upper corner. Right, full colour: a hand holds the compact V529 battery tester with its bright icon menu beside an engine-bay battery, a circular inset above showing the OBD port it plugs into, and a red descending arrow with spilling coins low in the frame. The deviation is precise and already legislated against: v1.3's --oldway negative names 'money props, price-claim imagery' as observed-and-excluded market habits, and this image runs them on BOTH panels — cost-you-money on the left, saves-you-money on the right. Recorded as a variant-candidate rather than a match because the money layer is not decoration here, it is the argument: the split is being fought on price rather than on friction, which is a different persuasive claim from what --oldway describes. If a second and third exemplar arrive, curation faces a real choice — draft a --cost variant with rules for honest price imagery, or harden the ban. The right panel's circular OBD-port inset is a legitimate context detail; the red arrow is G3-consistent (red = the bad outcome). Screen text on both devices is diegetic. Product domain: OBD2 / battery tester — the vertical the GIF reference image came from.

Second exemplar (2/5), and it widens the device meaningfully: exemplar 1 was a bare packshot ringed by chips on marble, this one grafts the chip column onto a lifestyle half-frame, so the future skeleton must treat the base layer (packshot vs scene) as a parameter rather than fix it. The drawn arcs at the ear annotate sound, an invisible real emission — the same family as the wifi, ultrasonic and NCV arcs already ledgered, and G3-consistent in blue. Single photographic frame, 1200x942, zero graphic layers, zero typography, no inset, no panel divide and no product of ours in shot. Zones: a man in his forties fills the right half at a cluttered home-office desk, one hand resting on a laptop trackpad, the other pulling his damp collar away from his neck; the left third holds an old white oscillating desk fan with a ribbon tied to its cage; a blind-covered window fills the background centre and a shelf of binders and loose paperwork crowds the right edge. His grey-blue shirt carries visible sweat patches at the chest and shoulder, his brow is furrowed and he looks straight down the lens with drained irritation. The desk is deliberately untidy: stacked paper, an open handwritten notebook, a phone, a sweating glass of water, pens and tangled cables. Light is flat overcast daylight through the blinds, the palette is desaturated cool-neutral, and nothing in frame is rendered or composited. The argument is pure recognition - it sells nothing, explains nothing and resolves nothing, it only asks someone working in an overheated room to recognise themselves - so job=pain at funnel step 1, and device=scene, one cinematic frame with no rail, no split and no overlay. Evidence ranks well against G9: rank 1 is the sweat on shirt and skin, rank 3 is the failed tool, an old fan whose tied ribbon proves the airflow is too weak to matter; the expression is present but is not carrying the argument alone. Because he meets the lens over a daily-frustration problem, gaze reads confront rather than candid, matching the type's own wording. The 1.27:1 crop is outside the type's declared ratios, but ratio is an explicit runtime parameter and never identity, so it does not move the verdict off match. Strong: the fan-plus-ribbon detail indicts the incumbent solution without a word of copy. Weak: no product category is visible, so it can only run paired with a relief or proof image, exactly as the type's avoid_when says. Note for curation: a four-pointed sparkle glyph sits in the lower right, recorded in quality_flags as watermarked. It is a generator signature rather than a drawn mark, and it matches the artifact adapters/nano-banana.md Rule 7 still lists as unresolved - evidence that the glyph travels with whoever generated the image, seller included, not with our prompts.

Full-bleed photographic frame, 1024x1024, one scene, no panel divide, no inset, no typography, no graphic overlay. Zones: upper left, a white wall-mounted cooler high on the wall beside a curtained window, outlet grille angled down; centre, a broad plume of white vapour leaving the grille and drifting right across the frame; right, a woman in a grey knit top leaned back in a desk chair, eyes closed, chin lifted into the airflow with a relaxed half-smile. Foreground left: a pale wood desk with an open laptop, a sweating glass of iced water, a ceramic mug and a row of books; a potted plant on the windowsill, a bookshelf upper right. Warm daylight from the window backlights the vapour so it reads as substance rather than haze, which is exactly what G8 demands - the emission is the only proof the frame carries and the light is built for it. The argument is the state after buying: cool air on your own face in your own room with the product visible as the explanation, so job=relief at funnel step 6, device=hero. Register reads commercial - controlled warm light, tidy styling, no phone-photo cues, no handheld awkwardness - and inset_mode is none because the scene carries everything on its own. Colour semantics are neutral, no red/green encoding and no badges, so G3 is not engaged. The 1:1 crop sits outside the type's declared 2:1 and 4:5, but ratio is a runtime parameter, not identity. Strong: eyes-closed relief plus a visibly lit emission carries the whole argument without copy, and the iced glass reinforces the temperature claim diegetically. Weak: the plume is dense and white enough to read as steam, which is the one thing a cooling product must never suggest - the same fault already ledgered on an anchor image of this type, so it is now twice observed and worth a curation look.

deviations.observed: the indicted object is the incumbent APPLIANCE rather than a symptom on a person, and no person appears at all - reaching 01-pain-scene from here would require changing the job, which SPEC 3.1 makes a different type rather than a variant

breakdown: Single documentary photographic frame, 1024x1024, no people, no overlays, no typography, no panel structure. Subject zone: a white window-mounted air conditioner sits in the lower sash of an old timber window, grille and touch controls facing the room. The frame around it is the real subject: paint peeling away in sheets, bare grey wood exposed, three metal brackets screwed in crookedly, and slabs of yellow foam board jammed into the gap on the left where the unit does not fit. Supporting detail: a stained ceramic mug on the sill, a pale power cable running down the wall to a discoloured socket at lower right, a dark green curtain tied back at left, a packed wooden bookcase at right. Light is dull overcast daylight through dirty glass; the palette is muted, cool and low-contrast, with no styling anywhere. The argument indicts an object the viewer already owns - a window unit is invasive, ugly, and wrecks the frame it sits in - and it sells nothing, shows no alternative and offers no resolution. That makes the job cause rather than pain: the vocabulary defines cause as indicting a concrete thing in daily life while not being about the product, and here the indicted thing is the incumbent appliance. Device is scene, one cinematic frame with zero graphic layers. The variant rung fails by definition rather than by degree, so I escalated to new-candidate and propose 02-cause-scene, which needs no vocabulary additions - cause and scene both exist and step 2 is the correct prefix for job=cause. The same argument shape is already ledgered as a cluster under this id (grimy open outlet plate, rusted panel bank, scratched hardwood floor), and this is the first instance of it where the indicted object is a whole appliance rather than building fabric. Strong: the peeling frame and the crammed foam make the cost of the incumbent solution physical rather than asserted, which is what G9 asks of an object-only frame. Weak: with no alternative in frame it depends entirely on adjacent copy or a paired relief image, and a viewer whose own install is tidy may not recognise themselves. Note for curation: a four-pointed sparkle glyph sits in the lower right, recorded in quality_flags as watermarked. It is a generator signature rather than a drawn mark, and it matches the artifact adapters/nano-banana.md Rule 7 still lists as unresolved - evidence that the glyph travels with whoever generated the image, seller included, not with our prompts.

Three stacked full-width photographic panels, 1024x1024 overall, thin white gutters, no outer border, no numbers, no arrows, no text, no badges. Panel 1: two hands press a white adhesive mounting plate flat to a pale wall, with a pale wood desk edge and a window at frame left. Panel 2: one hand tips a clear jug of water into the open top tray of the unit, now mounted on that plate, a ceramic mug and a cream knit throw on the desk behind. Panel 3: an index finger presses a touch control on the unit's top edge while the other hand is held palm-up beneath the outlet inside a visible white vapour stream. The same cream sleeve, the same room, the same pale wood and the same warm light run through all three, so the panels read as one continuous session rather than three shoots. The argument is operational reassurance - mount it, fill it, switch it on - ordered as three action steps, which is job=use and device=sequence, stacked panels ordered by action steps, at funnel step 3. Framing varies slightly between panels in distance and angle rather than being pixel-locked, so camera_lock reads handheld, the only value this type declares. The 1:1 ratio is in the type's declared list. It obeys the type's hardest negative: ordering is carried by the actions themselves, with no step numbers and no arrows - the fault most market exemplars of this device commit and the one the ledger's rail-form exemplar committed. Hands at close range are the model-weakness class flagged in adapter Rule 5 and they resolve correctly in all three panels. Strong: panel 3 closes the loop by showing the output, so the sequence proves the thing works rather than only how to operate it. Weak: panel 1 shows the mounting plate alone with no product in frame, so at thumbnail size the first beat is ambiguous. Note for curation: a four-pointed sparkle glyph sits in the lower right, recorded in quality_flags as watermarked. It is a generator signature rather than a drawn mark, and it matches the artifact adapters/nano-banana.md Rule 7 still lists as unresolved - evidence that the glyph travels with whoever generated the image, seller included, not with our prompts.

Small dark technical render, 198x255 - a thumbnail, flagged low-res. Composition: a near-black field with faint blueprint and circuit hints holding one vertically exploded mechanical assembly. Read top to bottom: a chromed multi-lobed cap, a gap, a stacked ring assembly glowing cyan with an orange-copper winding band at its middle, another gap, then a lower housing shell; white vapour wisps and small glowing particles fill the gaps between the pieces. Colour is cold cyan with one warm accent where the windings sit; there is no person, no environment, no hand and no scale reference. The argument is component-level technology display: the parts are separated so the buyer can count what is inside, which is the exploded-parts form. No active type covers it. 03-mechanism-xray is the closest in aesthetic but requires the PRODUCT to be the translucent subject with solid internals inside a see-through skin, which an exploded stack is not; 03-spec-split, recorded here as nearest to match the existing cluster's convention, requires two panels and a comparison; ghostbody requires a body. The device explode exists in the vocabulary as reserved with exactly this gloss, so I propose 03-spec-explode with no vocabulary addition needed. IMPORTANT for curation, stated so it is not discovered later: this file carries no product identity at all - no brand, no recognisable device, no context - so it demonstrates the DEVICE's form without being a product argument for anything. It is a distinct source by the letter of SPEC 6.3(1) and would move 03-spec-explode from 3/5 toward promotion, so weigh it low deliberately. Strong: the glow and the vapour make the separation read as energy rather than as a parts catalogue. Weak: at this resolution the middle assembly is barely legible, which is why low-res is flagged.

deviations.observed: two translucent HUD panels packed with dense small UI text, miniature schematics and dial readouts flank the exploded stack - overlay text at scale, exactly what G6 bans and what G6's own scope note routes to post-composite; if this form is common in the market the staging draft must decide explicitly whether to ban it or composite it

breakdown: Wide dark technical render, roughly 800x445, on a near-black navy field with a faint blueprint dot-grid. Centre: a horizontally exploded mechanical assembly - gear clusters, bearing races, coil springs, bolts and a central glowing cyan point - spread along one horizontal axis. Flanking it left and right sit two translucent cyan HUD panels filled with dense small UI text, miniature schematics, dial readouts and bar charts. A faint repeated diagonal stock watermark crosses the middle of the frame and the filename carries a stock catalogue id, so this file is un-purchased stock inventory rather than a published listing image. The argument is the same exploded-parts form as the other explode candidate in this batch, plus one structural addition the registry has no rule for: paired data panels that turn the render into an instrument readout. Job reads spec and device reads explode, so the proposal is again 03-spec-explode; nearest active is recorded as 03-spec-split to match the cluster's convention, and 03-mechanism-xray fails for the same reason as before, since it needs a translucent product rather than a separated stack. There is no product identity, no scale and no context here either, and the visible watermark is positive evidence nobody ever shipped it as a listing image - so the same caveat applies and applies harder: weigh it low as a promotion exemplar under SPEC 6.3(1). Strong: it records how far the market pushes the explode device toward instrument aesthetics, which is real structural information for the staging draft. Weak: as evidence for this library it is a style reference rather than a product argument.

deviations.observed: the offset space is left EMPTY as a copy well for page headline text, where the type requires a layer to occupy it

breakdown: A pale seamless studio frame in a wide banner crop. The right two-fifths hold a woman cropped at the neck, in a pink top and jeans, one hand presenting a stand-up coffee pouch and the other holding a filled glass of iced coffee on the counter. The left three-fifths are empty pale grey. The argument is step-6 relief in commercial register: the product and the result it makes, held by a person, sold on ease and appetite rather than on a mechanism. Signature devices are the pouch face-on so the pack copy reads, the prepared drink beside it as the visible output, and the neck crop that keeps the model anonymous. Register is commercial: controlled light, deliberate negative space, no rim light. Camera is level and static at counter height. G1 is satisfiable — the pouch is the exact product, unretouched. G8 is honoured in spirit: the output, a made iced coffee, is present and is the second subject. The one structural break from 06-relief-hero is OFFSET: the type says the subject sits to one side AND a layer occupies that space, and here the space is deliberately blank because a page headline will be typeset over it. That is a real decision, not an accident — the whole left half is clean to a pixel. Strong: the drink makes the promise concrete. Broken from the library's view: nothing this type could render would use that empty half, so the frame is composed for a page rather than for itself.

A square lifestyle photograph of a seated woman's legs and forearms, a black woven fitness band on her wrist, hands resting on a raised knee against a rust-red wall. Over it sit three text layers: a circled check with HSA/FSA ELIGIBLE at the top right, a white rounded pill across the lower third reading that the band is eligible for reimbursement, and a small disclaimer line under it. The argument is not about the product's mechanism, result or audience — it is a payment-eligibility claim, a commerce administrative fact. Strip the text and what remains is a worn-product photograph with no claim at all: no symptom, no output, no before, no after. The photographic layer alone would be a weak 06-relief-hero missing its room and its argument. Register is commercial-lifestyle, camera close and level, colour is warm neutral with no signal hues, so G3 is not engaged. The reason for rejection is that the argument this image makes lives entirely in composited copy, and G6 bans text in every render this library produces; there is no single-pass type that could make it. Recorded rather than skipped because it is evidence about what direct-response product pages actually run: an eligibility badge over a stock lifestyle frame is a recurring device here.

deviations.observed: no product anywhere in frame; the RESULT — a calm pet in a lived-in home — carries the whole frame

breakdown: A circular-masked phone photograph looking down at a small white fluffy dog sitting on a patterned rug on a wooden floor. Around it: a plant pot, a blue quilted dog coat on a rack, a glass tub, a cable running across the boards, hard afternoon sun cutting from the left. It is the customer-photo texture exactly — imperfect framing, the dog's head turned away, the room photographed as found rather than tidied. The argument is step-5 social proof: a real buyer's home, offered as evidence that other people like this bought and used the thing. Register is ugc without qualification; camera is a phone held at chest height, no photographer's composition. No marks, no layers, no text; the circular mask is a page-furniture crop rather than a decision inside the image, which the ladder treats as a runtime parameter. Colour is uncontrolled daylight, so G3 is not engaged. The one structural break from 05-social-snapshot is that the type's skeleton opens with a PRODUCT REFERENCE and all three of its modes — in-use, at-rest, kit-flatlay — put the product in frame, while this image contains no product at all. What is being shown is the outcome, an unbothered animal in a normal house. Strong: the authenticity the type asks for is total. This is the second image in this batch with the same deviation.

deviations.observed: the owner is the SUBJECT and addresses the lens holding the product up, where all three modes make the person incidental — a forearm, two fingers, or nobody

breakdown: A vertical phone selfie in a back garden at golden hour: a woman in her fifties or sixties, brown hair, tan sweater, smiling straight into the lens, holding a pink-to-blue foil sachet up beside her face. Behind her a wooden fence, succulents, a patio chair and a tree with the sun flaring through. The argument is step-5 social proof in its most direct form — a named-looking real person vouching, with the pack held to camera so the brand reads. Register is ugc: phone optics, slight overexposure on the sky, no styling, the arm's-length geometry unmistakable. The product is the exact reference and is legible, satisfying G1. No marks, no layers, no text. Colour is uncontrolled daylight so G3 is not engaged. The structural break from 05-social-snapshot is single and clear: the type's three modes all specify that the person is visible only incidentally — a forearm, two fingers, or nobody — and here the person is the whole subject, facing the lens, presenting the product to it. That is a testimonial-to-camera device rather than a found snapshot. Strong: it carries trust the way a review video thumbnail does. Worth noting for curation: images 1 and 12 in this batch also present the product to the lens by hand, in commercial register, which suggests present-to-lens is a device the library has no home for at either register.

A rounded-corner card holding a video still: a bearded man in round glasses and a white lab coat over a black shirt, in a blurred laboratory with equipment behind him, looking directly at the lens mid-sentence. No product anywhere. The argument is authority endorsement — an expert whose credentials transfer to the claim, almost certainly paired on the page with a name, a title and a quote. Register is corporate-documentary; camera is a video frame at chest height with a long lens and shallow depth of field. There is no symptom, no mechanism, no before-and-after, no output. The library has no type for this and the absence is deliberate rather than an oversight: mapping/slot-rules.md carries an `author` role with every channel cell empty, added on 2026-08-18 specifically because no library type produces a portrait of a named person and because generating a face to sit under a real byline is a disclosure decision rather than an image one. Recording this as a new-candidate would propose exactly what that row declined. So it is rejected on the library's own recorded scope rather than on quality — the image is competent and the device is common. Evidence value: expert-portrait stills are a standing feature of direct-response pages and will keep appearing in this corpus.

deviations.observed: no product in frame at all, where the type requires it present in the scene as the reason

breakdown: A rounded-corner square: a young woman in a soft blue shirt holding a plain white mug in both hands, eyes closed, the faintest smile, in a bright out-of-focus kitchen. Shallow depth of field, window light from the left, warm skin, no styling flourish. The argument is step-6 relief: the moment of ease itself, sold as a feeling rather than a feature. Register is commercial-lifestyle but restrained; gaze is candid and closed, never on the lens, which is exactly what 06-relief-scene asks for. Camera is close, at the subject's level. No marks, no panels, no text, no layers. Colour is warm neutral with no signal hues, so G3 is not engaged, and the type is G3-exempt in any case. The single structural break is the PRODUCT slot: 06-relief-scene's purpose sentence is a photograph of a person letting go WITH THE PRODUCT THERE IN THE SCENE AS THE REASON, and here there is no product — the mug is unbranded and the source page sells a skin balm, so the mug is not even the category. Strong: the emotional read is immediate and it would sit under any headline. Broken: with no product and no symptom, the image makes no claim on its own; the page copy has to supply the entire argument, which is the failure mode the type's own PRODUCT slot exists to prevent.

deviations.observed: no product in frame; an owner's hand and the pet carry it, the result standing in for the thing sold

breakdown: A vertical phone photograph taken from standing height: a brindle-and-white bulldog lying on a wooden floor, an owner's hand reaching in from the bottom of the frame to cup its jowl, the dog looking up into the lens. Warm indoor light, a door frame at the edge, nothing staged. The argument is step-5 social proof from a review gallery — the filename carries a customer's first name and initial. Register is ugc completely: phone optics, tight vertical crop, a hand in shot because the owner is also the photographer. Camera is handheld, no composition beyond pointing. No marks, no layers, no text; colour is uncontrolled tungsten-ish interior light so G3 is not engaged. The structural break is the same one image 3 carries: 05-social-snapshot opens with PRODUCT REFERENCE and every one of its three modes places the product in frame, and this frame contains none. The subject is the pet — the outcome the supplement claims — with the owner's touch as the emotional anchor. Strong: it is unfakeable in exactly the way the type's purpose sentence asks for. Two independent observations of this same deviation now sit in this batch, which is the shape curation's evidence rule looks for.

A square off-white graphic. A bold green headline asks whether you are still stacking bottles; a subhead offers eleven clinically studied ingredients in one daily formula; a five-row bordered table lists single-ingredient categories against price ranges with the product's own price last; a white supplement bottle with two loose capsules sits at the right with a green roundel claiming a saving; a footnote qualifies the comparison. The argument is a cost comparison against the alternative of buying ingredients separately — a legitimate step-4 proof or comparison beat. But the argument is carried entirely by typography and a ruled table. The only photographic element is a standard packshot. G6 bans text, numerals and labels in every render this library produces, and there is no type whose skeleton could emit a price table; 03-spec-split is the nearest register and it compares specifications through images, not currency through rows. Register is clean editorial-commerce; colour is brand green on off-white, no signal hues, G3 not engaged. Rejected because the library cannot make it and should not learn to: a table is page content, not an image type. Evidence value is high all the same — price-comparison tables are a fixture of supplement direct-response pages and this corpus will contain many.

A close phone photograph looking down at bright green lawn grass, a white-and-periwinkle supplement canister lying on it, and a hand entering from the right holding a single capsule between two fingers just above the tube. Hard midday sun, slightly blown highlights on the cap, the grass texture filling every other part of the frame. The argument is step-5 social proof in the in-use mode: the owner has the product open and a dose in hand, in a real place, photographed by whoever is holding it. Register is ugc — phone optics, no fill, no styling, the shadow of the photographer's arm implied. Camera is a phone at arm's length pointing down. The product is the exact reference, front label legible, so G1 holds. The person is visible only incidentally, two fingers and a thumb, which is precisely what the type's mode definition specifies. No marks, no layers, no text. Colour is uncontrolled daylight, G3 not engaged. The only thing that differs from the type's scene sentence is that the place is a lawn rather than a room inside a home, and the ladder treats environment as a runtime parameter at level 1, so identity is unchanged. Strong: the capsule held up gives scale and dose in one gesture without any text. Clean match, no deviations.

deviations.observed: a blank seamless studio ground, where the type requires one real room filled to the edges and says never blank

breakdown: A wide crop of a grey-haired woman in a white shirt, framed from the nose down, holding a lavender capsule between finger and thumb at her lips, about to take it. Even soft commercial light, a plain pale grey seamless behind her, no props. The argument is the dose moment: this is what taking it looks like, and the model's age states the audience without a word. That is step-6 relief in commercial register, and the pose is operated and mid-action exactly as the type specifies. Camera is close and level; the crop that removes the eyes is a deliberate anonymity device that also keeps the capsule the only focal point. G1 holds — the capsule is the product and it is unmodified. No marks, no panels, no text, no inset. Colour is neutral with the capsule's lavender as the only saturated note, so G3's signal hues are untouched. The single structural break is SETTING: 06-relief-hero requires one real room filled to the edges and states plainly that it is never blank, because a blank ground is what makes an image read as an advertisement rather than a life. This ground is blank by design. Strong: the gesture is unambiguous and the age casting does real work. Broken from the type's view: with no room, there is no life for the relief to belong to.

deviations.observed: the subject is an ANIMAL, not a person; the library has no type whose subject slot admits one
a saturated green seamless studio ground rather than a real room

breakdown: A black-and-white border collie lying on a bright green seamless, head down, eating visible fresh food — grains, kale, orange squash — from a shallow white bowl. Hard studio key from the upper left throwing a defined shadow, colour ground fully saturated. The argument is acceptance as proof: the product works because the end user takes it willingly, and for pet categories the end user is the animal. Register is commercial and confident; camera is above and slightly forward, close enough that the food's texture is the second subject. G1 holds — the food is the product and it is shown as it really looks, which is the whole claim for fresh pet food. G8 is satisfied: the visible output is the meal itself. No marks, no text, no panels. Two structural decisions differ from 06-relief-hero at once, which is one more than a variant may carry: the subject is an animal where every relief and social type in the index specifies a person, and the setting is a coloured seamless where the type demands a real room. Because the subject slot is the one that cannot be reached from any existing type, this is recorded as a new candidate rather than a variant. Proposed id 06-relief-animal keeps job `relief` and introduces device `animal`, which is a new device value and is flagged as such. Image 15 in this batch is a second observation of an animal subject.

deviations.observed: a person on a pure white knockout ground, which no active type permits
colourway and size breadth argued in ONE frame by presenting the retail packs to the lens, rather than across grid cells

breakdown: A woman in a white t-shirt on a pure white knockout background, holding three carded retail packs of compression socks fanned in front of her face so only her eyes and hair show above them. Black, white and navy socks, each on an identical blue-and-white header card whose bullet copy is partly legible. The argument is breadth of choice: the range exists, here it is, and a human holds it so the scale and the friendliness come free. That is a step-3 spec argument about the product line rather than a step-5 social one — the woman is a model, not a buyer. Register is commercial e-commerce; camera is straight-on at chest height; the knockout is cut for compositing onto any page colour. G1 holds — the packs are the real retail units. No marks; the on-pack copy is product surface rather than added text, which G6's own scope note permits. Two decisions put it beyond a variant: no active type allows a person on a blank knockout, and no active type argues range in a single frame — 03-use-grid and 05-persona-grid both argue breadth across CELLS. Proposed id 03-spec-range keeps job `spec` and adds device `range`, a new device value, flagged. Strong: one frame does what a four-cell grid usually needs. Weak: hiding the face behind the product is a gimmick that will not survive repetition.

A brushed stainless handheld milk frother photographed on pure white: the motor body standing with its coiled whisk on a thin shaft, and its cylindrical cap standing separately to the left. Even soft studio light, no shadow of consequence, no context, no hand, no output. The argument is inventory: this is the object, here is what is in the box. There is no funnel step attached to it — no symptom, no mechanism, no comparison, no result, no audience. The classification template names raw product photos explicitly as a reject class, and this is the cleanest possible example of one. Register is catalogue packshot; camera is level, centred, long-lens flat. Colour is neutral metal on white, no signal hues, so G3 is not engaged and nothing in G1-G15 is tested by it. Recorded rather than skipped because the runbook requires exactly one record per batch image and because the volume of plain packshots in this corpus is itself evidence: a direct-response product page carries a large number of frames that argue nothing and exist to show the object, and the library is right not to model them.

deviations.observed: a SIGNAL EMANATION mark — concentric arcs radiating outward from the worn product — which no mark in this type's library covers

breakdown: A vertical frame of a grey-haired man outdoors at golden hour, in a dark linen shirt, fist resting against his chin, gazing off to the left, a black woven band on the wrist that is raised toward camera. Drawn over the photograph: five concentric thin arcs radiating outward from the band, and beneath them a composited readout — a heart glyph, the words Biological Age, a very large +5.2 Years, and a blue arrow chip reading Improving. The argument is proof of an invisible outcome, made visible by borrowing the interface's own language. Register is commercial-lifestyle; camera is close with a long lens, background thrown right out. G1 holds on the band. The stat block is page-composited text and G6 forbids it in any library render, but the arcs are different: they are drawn INTO the frame, anchored to the product, and they do the job a mark does — they say the device is sensing. 06-relief-hero's mark library is output, past, step, vs, hotspot and path, and none of them is an emanation from the product. That is the single structural break recorded here. Strong: the arcs make a silent device look active without any text at all. Note for curation: the same signal-emanation device would solve a problem several sensor products in this corpus share.

deviations.observed: the subject is an ANIMAL living the resolved state, where the type specifies a person
no product in the scene at all, where the type requires it present as the reason

breakdown: A vertical frame of a tan-and-white dog at full stretch running left to right across mown grass, caught in a panning shot so the animal is sharp and the ground is smeared into horizontal streaks. Low golden light from the right, no product, no person, no text. The argument is the outcome as pure energy: this is what your animal is like after. It is exactly the beat 06-relief-scene occupies — a subject living the resolved state, candid, in an ordinary place, never looking at the lens — with the subject slot filled by an animal. Register is commercial but shot like documentary; camera is a panning follow at the animal's height, and the motion blur is the device that makes vitality legible in a still. G3 is not engaged. Two structural decisions differ: the subject is an animal, and the product is absent where the type requires it in the scene as the reason. Two decisions exceed what a variant may carry, so this is a new candidate, and it is the second animal subject in this batch after image 11. Proposed id 06-relief-animal, job `relief`, new device value `animal`, flagged. Strong: the panning blur is a real technique and the library owns nothing like it. Weak on its own: with no product, the page copy carries the entire claim.

Roughly sixteen flat grey tablets scattered at varied angles across a white ground, each with a soft drop shadow, several cropped by the frame edge, arranged to thin out toward the lower right. No packaging, no hand, no context, no scale reference. The purpose is decorative: this is a texture asset cut for compositing behind or beside page copy, and the crop through the tablets at the edges makes that explicit — it is designed to bleed. There is no argument of any kind attached to it. Register is neutral studio; camera is directly overhead; lighting is even with a single soft key. Colour is greyscale, so G3 is not engaged. It fails the template's own test for an e-commerce product argument image on the plainest reading: nothing is being claimed. Recorded rather than skipped because the runbook requires one record per batch image, and because the count of pure decoration assets in this folder is a useful fact for whoever next scopes a batch from it — a naive to-do list will be heavy with them.

Four identical amber supplement bottles with black caps and white wrap labels, arranged two behind two in a shallow stack on a white ground with a soft cast shadow. The label reads as a women's hormone support formula. No person, no context, no output, no comparison. The argument is quantity — this is the multi-buy bundle you are being offered — which is an offer fact rather than a product argument, and the library's own slot-rules place the standard product shot and the CTA furniture outside its scope with empty cells. Register is catalogue packshot; camera is level and centred; light is a broad soft key with fill. G1 is trivially satisfied and nothing else in G1-G15 is engaged. This is a raw product photo under the template's reject class, differing from image 13 and image 20 only in that it repeats the same object four times to signify a deal. Evidence value: bundle packshots are one of the highest-frequency asset classes on direct-response pages and none of them will ever route to a library type, which is worth knowing before someone tries to widen the registry to cover them.

deviations.observed: one single scene rather than the grid of cells the persona job is currently only expressible in
no product in frame; the audience is identified by what they are doing, not by what they hold

breakdown: A horizontal frame shot over two people's shoulders — both heads thrown far out of focus in the extreme foreground, framing the picture like a soft vignette — onto a hand holding a printed ultrasound scan above a patterned bedspread. Warm domestic window light, shallow depth of field, no product anywhere. The argument is audience identification: this is who the product is for, stated by a life moment rather than by a demographic label. The library expresses that job only through 05-persona-grid, which argues breadth by putting several different people in several cells; here the same job is done by ONE scene with enough specificity that the reader either is that person or is not. Register is commercial-documentary; camera is behind and between the subjects, which is what makes the viewer a participant rather than an observer. No marks, no text, no panels. G3 is not engaged; G13 is not engaged as no minor is in frame. Two decisions separate it from the grid: the layout is a single frame, and no product appears. Proposed id 05-persona-scene keeps job `persona` and uses device `scene`, which already exists in the vocabulary via 06-relief-scene and 02-cause-scene, so no new vocabulary is required. Strong: the over-shoulder framing is doing real work. Weak: without the product the page copy must name the category.

A circular avatar roughly ninety pixels across: a person in navy scrubs holding a small long-haired puppy against their chest, in what reads as a clinic. At this size the face is a few dozen pixels, the puppy is a smudge, and no detail of the setting survives. The filename marks it as the avatar beside a veterinarian's quote. Its function is page furniture — the portrait chip that makes a testimonial look attributed — and it is the same class the library's own slot-rules `author` row places outside scope with every channel cell empty. It is also illegible at its delivered size, which the classification template names as its own reject condition. Register cannot be assessed; camera cannot be assessed; no rule from G1-G15 is testable against it. It entered this batch because the selection filter excluded filenames containing `avatar` and this file is named as a gallery item instead, which is a small lesson about filename-based scoping: a name is not evidence, and the only reliable way to know an asset is furniture is to open it. Recorded with a low-res quality flag.

A single white supplement bottle centred on a very pale grey ground, three-quarter lit from the front, its label fully legible: a brand mark, three green dots, the product name, a benefits line and a capsule count. Nothing else is in the frame — no hand, no context, no output, no second object. This is the hero packshot the product page uses in its gallery and its cart, and it argues nothing beyond existence and identity. The classification template names raw product photos as a reject class and this is the canonical instance. Register is catalogue; camera is level and centred with a long lens; lighting is a large soft key with a subtle gradient behind to separate the white bottle from the white ground, which is the one piece of craft in it. G1 is trivially satisfied; no other global rule is engaged. Third packshot in this batch of twenty after images 13 and 17. Taken together with the decoration scatter at image 16, four of these twenty images exist to show or decorate the object rather than to argue for it, which is a ratio worth carrying into the next batch's scoping.

An ultra-wide banner crop, roughly three to one, of a man's torso and arms after exercise: a towel over the near shoulder, sweat on the skin and the towel, the head cropped away entirely, the far hand holding a phone against a raised knee and the near wrist carrying a black woven fitness band with the brand mark legible on its clasp. Behind him a dim green wall and a bench, thrown well out of focus. The argument is step-6 relief in its quietest form: this is the moment the product belongs to, and the product is simply there being worn. Register is commercial — controlled warm key, deliberate shallow depth, nothing about the frame is accidental. Camera is level at seated height with a long lens. G1 holds: the band is the exact reference and is unmodified. No marks, no text, no panels, no inset, which 06-relief-hero permits explicitly through inset_mode `none` for the case where the scene carries the whole argument. SETTING is satisfied — a real space filled to the edges rather than a blank ground. The head crop is a cast and framing choice, which the ladder treats as a runtime parameter at level 1, and the extreme banner ratio is likewise a parameter even though it sits outside ADR-016's five. Strong: the sweat and the towel date the moment precisely without a word of copy. Clean match, no deviations.

deviations.observed: a photographic abundance still life standing for a historical dietary baseline, where the type is a two-panel 2D illustration of one structure
no product and no body structure anywhere; raw foods on a stone slab carry the whole claim

breakdown: A warm painterly still life on a rough stone slab in what reads as a cave mouth: chard and kale leaves, bunched herbs, purple and cream root vegetables, rainbow carrots, blackberries and raspberries, raw liver and a heart laid on a green leaf, lentils and mixed nuts spilling to the right. Directional warm light from the upper left, deep shadow behind. The filename marks it as the THEN half of a then-and-now pair about dietary fibre, so its argument is a historical baseline: this is what the diet used to contain, which sets up the deficiency the product corrects. That is a cause-family argument, made without a body and without the product. Register is commercial-editorial food photography; camera is level at table height. Colour is warm earth with no signal hues, so G3 is not engaged. The image is generated rather than photographed — the carrots merge into one another at their tips, several leaf edges dissolve, and the organ meats have no consistent surface — so it carries an ai-artifacts flag. Two decisions put it beyond a variant of 02-cause-anatomy: the medium is photographic rather than 2D illustration, and there is no structure under argument at all. Proposed 02-cause-stilllife keeps job `cause` and adds device `stilllife`, a new device value, flagged. Note for curation: this is one half of a pair the PAGE composes from two separate assets, which is a recurring shape in this corpus.

deviations.observed: the speaker is the whole subject, filling the frame and addressing the lens, where all three snapshot modes make the person incidental
the product is not identifiable; only its prepared result, a drink in a glass, is in shot

breakdown: A vertical video still, soft and slightly compressed: a blonde woman in clear-framed glasses drinking through a straw from a deep pink glass, in a bright kitchen with white cabinetry behind her. She fills most of the frame from the chest up and her attention is on or just beside the lens. The argument is step-5 social proof delivered as a talking testimonial — a person you are meant to believe, mid-sentence or mid-sip, in her own home. Register is ugc without qualification: phone optics, no fill light, video-still softness, no styling. Camera is a phone held at arm's length or propped. No marks, no layers, no text. Colour is uncontrolled interior daylight so G3 is not engaged. Two decisions separate it from 05-social-snapshot: the person is the subject rather than an incidental forearm or two fingers, and the product itself never appears — only the drink made from it. That combination is a person-fronted testimonial frame, and the library has no type for it at any register. Proposed 05-social-testimony, job `social` which already exists, device `testimony` which is new and flagged. Related evidence: batch A image 4 was recorded as a variant of 05-social-snapshot for the same device before the pattern was visible across products; curation should read the two together rather than as different findings.

deviations.observed: the subject is a raw INGREDIENT, not a region of the product; the type requires the magnified area be a true region of the reference product
a styled overhead still life at normal distance rather than an extreme close-up of a working surface

breakdown: A circular-cropped overhead still life: fresh rosemary sprigs fanned across a dull pewter plate on dark grey slate, lit hard from the upper left so the needles separate and the plate's rim catches a rim of light. The argument is composition and provenance — this named botanical is in the formula, and it is shown fresh and whole rather than as a powder. That is a step-3 spec argument made about an ingredient rather than about the product's own construction. Register is commercial food-editorial; camera is directly overhead; the circular mask is page furniture for an ingredient row, which is a runtime parameter. Colour is deep green on cool grey, no signal hues, G3 not engaged. There is no product and no body. 03-spec-macro is the nearest type by intent — it argues material quality at close range — but its PRODUCT REFERENCE requires the magnified region to be a true region of the reference product, and a rosemary sprig is not. Two decisions differ, so this is a new candidate rather than a variant. Proposed 03-spec-ingredient, job `spec` existing, device `ingredient` new and flagged. Images 5 and 16 in this batch are the second and third observations of the same type at different presentations.

deviations.observed: the subject is a raw dried ingredient, not a region of the product
a pure white knockout with no ground, cut for compositing anywhere on the page

breakdown: Five or six pieces of dried, pale brown root — the fibrous, slightly twisted form of an adaptogenic root such as ashwagandha or liquorice — arranged in a loose crossed pile on a pure white knockout with the faintest contact shadow. Nothing else in frame. The argument is the same one image 4 makes: this named ingredient is in the formula, shown in its recognisable raw state. Register is commercial catalogue; camera is level and close; lighting is broad and shadowless so the cut-out is clean. Colour is neutral tan on white, G3 not engaged. No product, no body, no marks, no text. Against 03-spec-macro the same two decisions differ as in image 4 — the subject is an ingredient rather than a region of the product, and the treatment is a catalogue cut-out rather than an extreme close-up of a working surface. The difference between this frame and image 4 is only the background treatment, styled slate versus white knockout, which the ladder treats as a runtime parameter at level 1, so these are two observations of ONE proposed type rather than two proposals. Second observation of 03-spec-ingredient. Worth noting for curation: an ingredient row on a supplement page typically carries six to twelve of these, so exemplars will accumulate fast.

deviations.observed: the speaker fills the frame and talks to the lens, where the type's three modes make the person incidental
no product anywhere in frame

breakdown: A vertical video still: a young woman with long brown hair in a dark linen shirt, mid-sentence, looking straight into the lens, against a plain warm wall with a snake plant at the right edge. Nothing else is in the frame — no product, no props, no text. The argument is step-5 social proof as pure testimony: the whole claim is carried by a person saying it, and the plain room signals that she is a customer rather than a spokesmodel. Register is ugc: flat available light, phone or webcam optics, mild softness, no colour grade. Camera is at eye height, close, static. No marks, no layers, no panels. G3 is not engaged and G13 is not engaged. Two decisions separate it from 05-social-snapshot: the person is the subject rather than an incidental limb, and no product appears at all, which every one of the type's three modes requires. Second observation in this batch of the person-fronted testimonial frame after image 3, and the third across both batches counting batch A image 4. Proposed 05-social-testimony, job `social`, new device `testimony`, flagged. Strong: it is the cheapest trust device on a direct-response page and this corpus is full of it. Weak for the library: with no product and no room, there is nothing for a type's slots to hold beyond a face, which is precisely why slot-rules keeps `author` empty — curation should decide whether this proposal collides with that decision.

The back panel of a white supplement carton stood upright on a pale blue ground with a hard diagonal shadow, and a vertical column of six pale yellow roundels down the right edge reading Vet Formulated, Non GMO, No Artificial Flavors, 3rd Party Tested, Made in Vermont and Great Taste, each with a small line icon. The panel itself carries a full Product Facts table, cautions, directions, storage and manufacturer address. The argument is transparency plus accreditation: read everything, and here are six third-party-ish assurances. The panel text is product surface, which G6's own scope note permits, but the six roundels are added graphics carrying added words, and they are what makes the image an argument rather than a packshot. Strip them and what remains is a back-of-pack photograph, which the template names as a raw product photo and rejects. Register is clean e-commerce studio; camera is level and centred; the shadow is the only styling. G3 is not engaged. Rejected because the library cannot make it: no type emits badge furniture, and G6 forbids the text that carries the claim. Recorded because trust-badge stacks are a fixture of this corpus and it is useful to know they will never route.

deviations.observed: the sequence is delivered as SEPARATE single-panel assets each carrying its own numbered step badge, where the type is three photographs stacked in one frame with the order read from the actions and no numbers of any kind

breakdown: An overhead flat-lay on a saturated cobalt ground: six or seven sealed pouches of fresh pet food in different colourways arranged around the frame edge, three white bowls holding the prepared meals, loose baked pieces scattered between them, and a large white-on-blue numbered badge reading 2 sitting at the bottom centre.
