The filename confirms it is step two of a how-it-works sequence. The argument is a step in an onboarding explanation — this is what arrives and what it looks like served. Register is commercial e-commerce; camera is directly overhead; light is broad and even with soft shadows. G1 holds on the packs. The single structural break from 03-use-sequence is its LAYOUT, and it is a deliberate one: the type specifies three photographs stacked one above another in a single frame, with no numbers, no step markers and no text of any kind, because the order is meant to be read from the actions themselves. Here the page composes the sequence from separate assets and supplies the ordering with a numeral baked into each one. That is exactly the device the type's law forbids, done anyway by a live page, which makes it worth a record rather than a dismissal. Strong: the flat-lay reads instantly at thumbnail size. Broken from the type's view: the numeral does the work the actions should do.

deviations.observed: near-duplicate of sha256:afd29ca653c25c5ac560b316ab4ed298bf3dcf316d8d3314005342273a79c2ed, recorded in batch 2026-08-31-A as a raw product photo; same bottle, same lighting design, differing only in crop scale and ground tone

breakdown: A single white supplement bottle centred on pure white, three-quarter lit, label fully legible with brand mark, three green dots, product name, benefits line and capsule count. It is the same product and effectively the same photograph as the bottle recorded in batch A from this product's gallery, differing only in crop scale and in the ground being pure white rather than a pale grey gradient. The filename marks it as a variant with the bottle omitted from some larger composition, which explains the tighter cut. The argument is identity and nothing more: no person, no context, no output, no comparison. Register is catalogue packshot; camera level and centred with a long lens; a single broad soft key. G1 is trivially satisfied and no other global rule is engaged. Recorded as a duplicate rather than a second reject so the ledger does not count one photograph twice as independent evidence, which is what SPEC section 6.2's evidence rule exists to prevent. The deviations field carries the earlier hash. Useful fact for scoping: the same packshot appears in this corpus at several crops under different filenames, so a to-do list built on hashes will still surface near-duplicates that only opening the file can catch.

deviations.observed: a composed brand flat-lay in hard styled sunlight, where the type's register is a real customer's phone photo and polish is its stated failure mode
a chosen textile surface arranged for the shot rather than one ordinary home photographed as found

breakdown: An overhead flat-lay on a woven blue, teal and cream diamond-patterned mat in hard directional sunlight: one white compression sock laid out full length with a mint cuff and the brand name printed on its sole, and beside it a navy pair still on its blue-and-white header card with the bullet copy legible. Strong diagonal shadows cross the frame. The argument is what you actually get — the product in the pack and out of it, at full length, so length and cuff are unambiguous. That is a step-3 spec argument about the physical article. Register is commercial: the mat is chosen, the light is used rather than accepted, the arrangement is deliberate. Camera is directly overhead. G1 holds. No marks, no added text; the header card's copy is product surface. 05-social-snapshot's kit-flatlay mode is the nearest structure in the index, but its register is explicitly a real buyer's phone photo and its purpose sentence states that polish is the failure mode, so a composed brand flat-lay cannot be a match or an axis value of it. Two decisions differ. Proposed 03-spec-flatlay, job `spec` existing, device `flatlay` new and flagged. Strong: laying the sock out flat beside the pack answers a real sizing doubt in one frame.

deviations.observed: a tight body-detail crop on a blank studio ground, where the type requires one person in one real room filled to the edges
no product in frame; the body zone where the result shows carries the whole argument

breakdown: A wide, tight studio crop of a flat abdomen from just below the ribs to the hip line, on a pale warm ground that is barely distinguishable from the skin. Even soft frontal light, fine skin texture and the faint vertical line above the navel left visible, no retouching gloss. No product, no clothing beyond the frame edges, no marks. The filename marks it as a difference claim, so the argument is the outcome shown on the body itself: this is what not being bloated looks like. That is step-6 relief with the product removed and the body zone isolated. Register is commercial; camera is level and close with a long lens; the crop deliberately removes any identity. Colour is warm neutral, no signal hues, G3 not engaged. Two decisions separate it from 06-relief-hero: the frame is a body detail on a blank ground rather than a person in a real room filled to the edges, and no product appears. Proposed 06-relief-detail, job `relief` existing, device `detail` new and flagged. Strong: it makes an invisible internal claim visible without a diagram or a mark, which is something no current relief type can do. Weak: with no before, the frame asserts rather than demonstrates, and 04-proof-lockedframe exists precisely because assertion is not proof.

deviations.observed: no product in the scene, where the type requires it present as the reason
a warm-boosted glamour grade and a posed repose, where the type demands a muted desaturated grade and a person mid-errand in an ordinary public place

breakdown: A wide banner crop of a woman lying back in long grass in a white sleeveless top, arms flung above her head, eyes closed, smiling, in strong low sunlight that rims her cheek and shoulder. No product, no props, no text. The argument is the emotional end state in its purest form: this is how you will feel, with nothing else asked of the frame. Register is commercial and consciously beautiful. Camera is above her, close, level with the grass. Colour is warm-boosted green and gold. 06-relief-scene is the nearest type by job and it breaks in three places at once: the product must be in the scene as the reason and is absent; the subject must be mid-errand in an ordinary public place someone would pass through, and lying in grass is neither; and the grade must be muted and desaturated and explicitly never warm-boosted, which this is. Three decisions is well past what a variant may carry. Proposed 06-relief-mood, job `relief` existing, device `mood` new and flagged. Related: batch A image 6, a woman with a mug and no product, was recorded as a single-deviation variant of the same type; this frame is the same family taken further, and curation should read them together. Weak on its own: without the product the page copy carries the entire claim.

A vertical lifestyle photograph of a middle-aged man outdoors in low sun, in a sleeveless top, seated with one hand raised and the fitness band on his wrist, looking down and away. Composited over the lower half is a large rounded glass-morphism card containing a red-to-green gauge arc, the label Chronic Illness, the figure 76 out of 100, a B-minus grade with a red down arrow, and four lines of body copy explaining rising visceral fat, resting heart rate, and drops in HRV, recovery and muscle mass. The argument is proof of an invisible risk, borrowed wholesale from the app's own interface. Register is commercial-lifestyle for the photograph and product UI for the overlay. The photographic layer alone would read as a competent 06-relief-hero, but it makes no claim by itself; everything that argues is text and a data gauge. G6 bans text, numerals and labels in every render this library produces, and no type emits a UI card. Third instance in this corpus of a data-overlay claim after batch A images 2 and 14, and unlike image 14 there is no mark drawn into the frame to record — the arcs there were anchored to the product, and this card simply sits on top. Rejected as unmakeable rather than as poor.

deviations.observed: a real thermographic instrument capture with its own false-colour LUT and scale bar, where every diagnostic type in the index is an illustration or a render
colour is the instrument's temperature scale rather than the library's semantics; red means hot, not wrong

breakdown: A thermogram of a human back seen from behind, the body isolated against black, rendered in the instrument's rainbow palette — violet and blue at the arms and flanks, orange across the shoulders and mid-back, and a vivid red column running the length of the lower spine. A vertical temperature scale bar from 19.7 to 28.4 sits at the right edge, and a timestamp with an operator name is burned into the bottom left. The argument is evidence of an invisible symptom, made visible by borrowing a medical imaging modality and its authority. Register is instrument capture, which no type in the index has: 02-cause-anatomy is a 2D illustration and 03-mechanism-xray is a 3D see-through render, and both are drawn. Camera is the device's own sensor, straight on. G3 is engaged and broken in an interesting way — red does mean the bad thing here, but by coincidence of the LUT rather than by the library's semantics, and the palette carries five more hues the library forbids. Two decisions differ. Proposed 04-proof-instrument, job `proof` existing, device `instrument` new and flagged. Note: this is a real capture, so a library type would be generating something that claims to be instrument output, which is a truthfulness question for curation and not only a craft one.

deviations.observed: breadth argued in ONE frame as a physical lineup, where every breadth type in the index argues it across separated grid cells
a pale seamless gradient studio ground rather than the real places a grid's cells require

breakdown: Five stand-up coffee pouches in five flavour colourways — orange, brown, blue, tan and yellow — arranged in a shallow arc on a pale lilac-to-white gradient, with two prepared iced coffees in glasses set among them and a stack of white lids at the right. Each pack faces forward so its flavour name and protein claim read. The argument is breadth of choice: the range exists and it is this wide. Register is commercial e-commerce; camera is level at product height; light is broad and even with a soft reflection under the ground line. G1 holds on all five packs. G8 is served by the two made drinks. No marks, no added text; on-pack copy is product surface. 03-use-grid is the nearest type by job but it argues breadth by giving each case its own cell in a photographic grid, in a real place per cell, with the camera changed between them; this frame argues the same thing by lining the objects up in one continuous studio space. Two decisions differ. Proposed 03-spec-range, job `spec`, device `range` new and flagged — and this is the SECOND observation of it in this corpus after batch A image 12, where the same lineup argument was made with a person holding three packs. Cast is a runtime parameter, so those are one type.

deviations.observed: the subject is a botanical growing in the ground, not a region of the product
a mid-distance natural-light plant photograph rather than an extreme close-up of a working surface

breakdown: A circular-cropped photograph of chaste tree in flower: several upright violet spikes of small densely packed blooms above narrow palmate green leaves, more of the same plant soft behind, an out-of-focus lawn at the bottom edge. Natural overcast-to-dappled daylight. The argument is provenance: the named botanical in the formula is a real plant that grows, shown alive rather than processed. Same job as images 4 and 5 in this batch — composition and origin — reached by a third presentation. Register is commercial-natural; camera is at plant height, mid-distance, shallow depth. The circular mask is page furniture for an ingredient row, a runtime parameter. Colour is violet and green, and violet is not one of G3's three signal hues, so G3 is not engaged. No product, no body, no marks, no text. The two decisions against 03-spec-macro are the same as in images 4 and 5: an ingredient rather than a region of the product, and a normal-distance frame rather than an extreme close-up. Third observation of 03-spec-ingredient in this batch. The three presentations seen so far — styled on a plate, cut out on white, growing in the ground — differ only in staging, which is a parameter, so the type would need a presentation axis rather than three variants.

deviations.observed: both people face the lens and give a shared thumbs-up, where the type requires an act passing between an advocate and a listener whose face is not visible
no product in frame at all, where the type makes it dominant

breakdown: A candid phone photograph inside a clinic: a visibly pregnant blonde woman in a navy and pink striped dress and a dark-haired practitioner in a grey jumper standing side by side, both smiling at the lens and both giving a thumbs-up, one hand resting on her upper arm. Behind them a wall densely covered with baby photographs and printed notices about acupuncture and fertility; to the right a desk with a card display. The argument is outcome plus authority in one frame — the practitioner and the person it worked for, in the room where it happened, with the wall of previous outcomes as corroboration. Register is ugc: on-camera flash, uneven white balance, no composition beyond standing them together. Camera is a phone at chest height. No product, no marks, no added text. 05-social-handoff is the nearest type — two people, step-5 social job — and it breaks twice: there is no act passing between them and no listener with a hidden face, and the product is absent where the type makes it dominant. Cast count is a runtime parameter, so this is the same person-fronted testimonial device as images 3 and 6, with two speakers instead of one. Third observation of the proposed 05-social-testimony in this batch.

deviations.observed: the subject is an ANIMAL living the resolved state; no type in the index admits one in its subject slot
no product in the scene, where the type requires it present as the reason

breakdown: A phone photograph looking down at a beagle rolled onto its back in sunlit grass, mouth open in a play-grin, front paws curled, wearing a red plaid collar, while two hands — one with a wedding ring and one with a beaded bracelet — rub its chest and belly from the bottom of the frame. Hard afternoon sun, slightly crushed shadows, a phone's colour response. The argument is the outcome as a state of being: your animal, comfortable and playing, which is what the supplement is for. Register is ugc; camera is a phone held overhead by the person doing the rubbing. No product, no marks, no text. G3 is not engaged. 06-relief-scene is the nearest type by job and it breaks twice: the subject is an animal where the type specifies a person, and the product is absent where the type requires it in the scene as the reason. Proposed 06-relief-animal, matching the proposal made for batch A images 11 and 15, so this is the third observation of an animal subject in the corpus. A correction worth recording: batch A images 3 and 7 were also animal subjects and were filed as variants of 05-social-snapshot for their missing product, before the animal-subject pattern was visible across products. Curation should read all five together; the subject slot is the deeper gap and the missing product is a consequence of it.

A circular avatar about two hundred and forty pixels across: a smiling man in glasses and blue scrubs on a plain light grey studio ground, holding a cocker spaniel puppy in one arm and a French bulldog puppy in the other. Its function is attribution furniture — the portrait chip that makes a quote look sourced — and the filename places it in a review banner. The library's own mapping/slot-rules.md carries an `author` role with every channel cell empty, added deliberately because no library type produces a portrait of a named person and because generating a face to sit under a real byline is a disclosure decision rather than an image one. So this is rejected on the library's recorded scope, not on quality. Register is commercial studio portrait; camera is level at chest height; lighting is flat and even. G3 not engaged. A second scoping lesson after batch A image 19: this file is named as a benefit banner and still turned out to be an avatar, so the benefit-* filter is no more reliable than the avatar filter was. Only opening the file settles what an asset is.

A bright kitchen: an owner's forearms and hands enter from the bottom left holding a branded carton of fresh pet food and a pale blue spatula, scooping the food into a ceramic bowl on a white marble counter, while a yellow labrador in a branded bandana stands up at the far side of the counter with its paws on the edge, tongue out, watching. Plantation shutters and a glazed door behind, a window seat with a blue cushion at the left. The argument is the serving moment: the product being prepared, its texture visible, and the beneficiary present and eager. Register is commercial; camera is at counter height from the owner's side; light is broad daylight from the window bank. G1 holds — the carton is the exact reference and legible. G8 is served: the visible output is the food itself, twice, in the carton and in the bowl. Every 06-relief-hero slot is satisfied — one person reduced to hands and forearms, an operated mid-action pose, one real room filled to the edges rather than a blank ground, no inset which inset_mode `none` permits. The dog is not a second subject in the type's sense but the reason standing in the scene, the same role the product plays in 06-relief-scene. Recorded as a clean match, and noted deliberately against images 11, 15 and 18 of the animal-subject pattern: when a person operates the product and the animal waits, the existing type holds; it is when the animal becomes the subject that the index runs out.

A tight crop of the United States flag rendered as a smooth vector gradient, the canton and seven stripes filling the left two thirds and fading into flat white at the right. There is no product, no person, no place and no symptom. Its function is a country-of-origin trust signal that sits behind or beside a Made in USA line, and the fade to white on the right is the giveaway that it is cut to be composited under page copy. Register is flat vector illustration, not photography; there is no camera and no lighting to assess. Colour is the flag's own red, white and blue, which are not acting as G3 signals but as a national emblem, so G3 is not engaged. Nothing in G1 to G15 is testable against it. It is the same class as the logo and press-mark assets the library places outside its scope: an emblem the library may never generate, both because G6 bans logos and because a national flag is a claim about manufacture that an image cannot substantiate. Recorded rather than skipped because the runbook requires one record per batch image. Evidence value: this is the first flag in the ledger and it belongs with the 220 icon, logo and badge files the corpus carries, which is a third of the folder.

deviations.observed: the subject is a raw ingredient powder, not a magnified region of the product
a mounded heap photographed whole at normal distance, not an extreme close-up of a working surface

breakdown: A single mound of pale cream powder on a very pale grey seamless, lit from the upper left so the heap throws a soft shadow to the lower right and the loose grains scattered around its edge each catch a highlight. Nothing else is in the frame. The filename marks it as the HCI ingredient of a joint formula, so the argument is composition and provenance: this named material is in the tub, and it is shown in the state it arrives in rather than as a claim on a label. That is a step-3 spec argument made about an ingredient rather than about the product's own construction. Register is commercial catalogue still life; the camera is directly overhead and square; the light is a single soft key with no fill, which is what separates the grains. Colour is cream on pale grey with no signal hues, so G3 is not engaged. There is no product, no body, no person, no mark and no text. 03-spec-macro is the nearest active type by intent because it argues material quality at close range, but its PRODUCT REFERENCE requires the magnified area to be a true region of the reference product, and a loose powder is an input to the product rather than a part of it. Two decisions differ, which is one more than a variant may carry. This is the fourth observation of the single-named-material still life after the three of batch 2026-08-31-B, and it is the first on a powder rather than a botanical, which widens the proposed type past plants.

deviations.observed: a nearly empty pale marble counter with two objects at the frame edge, where the type requires one real room filled to the edges with six to eight objects and says never blank

breakdown: A video still looking down at a pale marble bathroom counter. A hand enters from the right and is closing on a matte black razor handle lying on the stone; a white ceramic vessel is cropped at the top edge and a dark grey panel, probably a mirror surround, closes the upper right. The argument is the reach: this is the moment the object is picked up, which sells the object as something that lives in your bathroom and is used without ceremony. That is step-6 relief with the subject reduced to a hand, which the type permits explicitly. Register is commercial — controlled soft light, a deliberate clean surface, nothing accidental. The camera is high and oblique at counter height. G1 is satisfiable: the razor is the exact product and is unmodified. G8 is not engaged because the product emits nothing. No marks, no panels, no inset, no text. Colour is neutral greys and skin with no signal hues, so G3 is not engaged. The single structural break is SETTING: the type's own PARTS entry requires one real room filled to the edges with six to eight objects that genuinely belong, and says never blank with no bare area larger than the product. This frame is deliberately close to bare, and the emptiness is the brand's register rather than a fault in the photograph. One decision, so a variant rather than a type. It is the second observation of a minimal studio-clean setting on this type after batch 2026-08-31-B image 10, which was a blank seamless behind a dose moment.

deviations.observed: the symptoms ring the subject on a drawn circle instead of stacking in a vertical vignette band down one edge
each symptom is a WORD in a pill, not a photographic vignette of the symptom
the hero subject is an animal

breakdown: A square frame of a shaggy apricot dog lying on sunlit lawn, head up and tongue out, filling the centre. Drawn over it: a thin white circle centred on the dog, six white rounded pills spaced around that circle reading Scratching, Head Shaking, Paw Licking, Occasional Loose Stool, Occasional Constipation, Eating Grass and Seasonal Allergies, a two-line serif headline across the top reading Signs your dog may need probiotic support, and one brown soft chew resting on the dog's chest. The argument is symptom coverage: the product answers a spread of complaints at once, and the reader is meant to find their own dog somewhere on the ring. That is exactly 02-symptom-rail's job, done with three structural decisions changed. The rail stacks photographic vignettes in a band down one edge at seventy-two percent hero; this rings the hero with text pills. The rail's vignettes SHOW each symptom; these NAME them, which is only possible because the page bakes type into the picture. And the hero subject is an animal, which no active type admits. Register is commercial-lifestyle; camera is level at the dog's height; light is hard afternoon sun. G3 is not engaged — the pills are white and carry no signal colour. G6 is broken outright by the seven text elements, which is the owner's Q1b decision rather than a fault in the image. Three decisions is well past a variant. Recorded as the first observation in this ledger where a text layer REPLACES a picture element rather than adding to one, which is a distinct thing from the benefit headlines seen so far.

A white supplement bottle turned so the back panel faces the camera, on pure white with a soft contact shadow. The panel carries suggested use, a tamper-evident line, a pregnancy and medication warning, a caffeine-equivalence sentence, a dosage caution and a diet-and-exercise line; below them a green rounded pill reads NO major food allergens, synthetic colors, fillers, artificial or natural flavors; below that five icon-and-text benefit lines each closing with an asterisk; and at the bottom a boxed FDA disclaimer. The argument is transparency plus a benefit stack: read everything, and here is what it does. Strip the added green pill, the five benefit lines and the boxed disclaimer and what remains is a back-of-pack photograph, which the classification template names as a raw product photo. Everything that argues is typography added over the packshot. Register is clean e-commerce studio; camera level and centred; a broad soft key with a subtle gradient behind. G1 is trivially satisfied. G3 is not engaged. This is the second observation of the pattern after batch 2026-08-31-B image 27, which was a carton back panel with six yellow accreditation roundels; two independent products now build the same tile the same way. It is rejected on the same ground as that one and as the price table of batch B image 8: the argument is carried entirely by set type, and no type in this library emits a paragraph.

deviations.observed: the frame's job is to show the object and stamp claims onto the space beside it; no funnel-step argument is made by the picture itself
four separate text clusters — an authority shield and three offer pills — where G16's drafted budget is one block plus one badge

breakdown: A white and periwinkle capsule bottle standing centred on a pale grey seamless with a long soft shadow to the right. Composited around it: a gold shield at the upper right reading number one GI doctor recommended, Akkermansia-based probiotics; and three blue rounded pills stacked at the left reading HIGHER POTENCY, BEST SELLER and NEW + IMPROVED. The photographic layer alone is a plain packshot and argues only identity. Everything persuasive is a stamp. This is the shape the owner's Q2b and Q1b decisions together point at — a packshot that carries its own claims — so it is recorded as a candidate rather than rejected as the equivalent tiles were in batches A and B, and the change of standard is stated here rather than left for a reader to infer. Register is commercial catalogue; camera level at bottle height; broad soft key. G1 holds. G3 is not engaged. Three of the four text elements are classes the drafted G16 refuses on purpose: an authority endorsement, a best-seller flag and a new-and-improved flag are respectively an expert claim, a ranking that changes and an offer fact that changes, and the file outlives all three. So the honest reading is that the ARGUMENT structure is new and admissible while three of its four fills are not. Proposed id uses a step and job that do not exist yet and both are flagged as new vocabulary. This file is byte-identical to the asset filed under lp3-12northfold-washno1 in this same batch; one hash, one record, and the shared asset is noted below.

A teal stand-up pouch printed with a leaf motif and the words Life Starts Here stands at the left of a cream frame. A large plus sign sits between it and a column of eight white cards at the right, each with a small line icon and a phrase: Custom Formulation, Monthly Check-in Calls, Fertility Diet Guide, Lab Tested, Email Support, Full Guidance, Free Shipping, Pause or Cancel Anytime. The argument is offer completeness — you are not buying a bag, you are buying a programme. Four of the eight items are service and commerce terms rather than product facts, and the library's own slot-rules place offer furniture outside its scope with an empty cta row. Register is flat e-commerce layout; the packshot is a studio cut-out and the rest is set type on cards. There is no scene, no camera position worth naming and no lighting to assess beyond the packshot's own. G3 is not engaged. G1 holds on the pouch. The decisive fact is the text budget rather than the argument: nine text clusters in one frame against the drafted G16's one block plus one badge, and no evidence anywhere in this library that a diffusion renderer holds nine clusters. Rejected on the same ground as batch B image 8's price table — the argument is carried by typography and a ruled layout, and this library emits pictures. Second observation of the list-beside-a-packshot component after that one.

A pink line-art icon of two leaves on a stem, centred inside a thin pink circle on a very pale pink disc, delivered as a square with the circle nearly filling it. There is no product, no person, no place, no symptom and no photograph of any kind. Its function is page furniture: the chip that sits above a short benefit label in a row of three or four such chips. Register is flat vector illustration; there is no camera and no lighting. Colour is a single brand pink used decoratively rather than as a signal, so G3 is not engaged, and nothing else in G1 to G15 is testable. It is the same class the library has rejected consistently and the corpus carries 99 files named as icons across nine of thirteen products. Recorded rather than skipped because the runbook requires one record per batch image, and because the count matters: icons, logos and badges together are 220 of the 653 files in this folder, which is the number that should shape how a batch is selected rather than a surprise found one image at a time.

deviations.observed: a verbatim review card with an attributed name and a five-star row composited over the lifestyle base, which no ACTIVE type carries — 05-social-card legislates exactly this and is still in _staging

breakdown: A close frame of a man's forearm and bare chest in a gym, a black woven fitness band on the wrist, a dumbbell in the hand and gym equipment thrown out of focus behind. Across the lower third sits a dark translucent rounded card carrying the name Tom D. at the left, a row of four and a half gold stars at the right, and a four-line quote in white. The argument is testimonial social proof with the product visibly worn by the person being quoted. This is precisely 05-social-card's definition — a verbatim review card composited over a lifestyle base photo — and that type is a staging draft at one exemplar, so this is its second and the verdict is new-candidate rather than match because nothing in _staging is routable. Register is commercial-editorial; camera is close with a long lens; light is warm practical gym light. G1 holds on the band. G3 is not engaged. Two things in this exemplar are un-generatable by this library and both are worth the record: the quote names a competitor brand outright, which SPEC 6.4 bars from any prompt, and the card carries an attributed name and a star row, which G14 says turns any generated image in that slot into a fabricated endorsement. So the type's own boundary is visible in its second exemplar: 05-social-card can be made only where the quote is real and the library is filling the picture, never where the library would be inventing the endorsement.

Two foil stand-up pouches overlap on a transparent cut-out ground, the front one a pink-to-blue gradient reading hydroh, MOLECULAR HYDROGEN, generates 12ppm of hydrogen per tablet, raspberry flavour, 30 tablets, 30 day supply; the one behind is a cream-to-blue variant of the same pack. Three small iridescent bubble graphics float at the lower left. The argument is quantity and offer: this is the multi-pack you are being sold, and the second pouch exists to say two rather than one. The library's slot-rules place the standard product shot and the offer furniture outside its scope, and batch 2026-08-31-B image 17 rejected the same thing in its four-bottle form. Register is catalogue cut-out; camera level at pack height; broad even light with no shadow of consequence. All the words in frame are the pack's own printed surface, which G6's scope note permits as diegetic, so the text is not what disqualifies it. G1 is trivially satisfied and nothing else in G1 to G15 is engaged. Second observation of the bundle packshot. Under the owner's Q2b decision a bundle belongs to the proposed identity family rather than to the argument registry, and it is recorded here as a reject against the current standard with that route named.

A cream oversized hooded sweatshirt floating on pure white, shot flat and symmetrical with the hood propped, the kangaroo pocket visible and a tonal embroidered word barely legible on the left chest. The filename places it as a gift item on a coffee brand's page, so the object in frame is not the product being sold at all — it is a premium offered with the purchase. There is no funnel-step argument: no symptom, no mechanism, no comparison, no result, no audience. Register is catalogue packshot; camera straight on and centred; broad even light with the shadow removed in post, which the ragged cut-out edge along both sleeves shows plainly. Colour is a single cream on white, no signal hues, G3 not engaged. It is a raw product photo of a non-product, which the classification template's reject class covers twice over. Recorded because it is the first gift-with-purchase asset in the ledger and it names a real hazard for any future identity family: a page's gallery carries packshots of things that are not the product, and a type keyed on the product photo would happily render the wrong object.

deviations.observed: the subject is a raw ingredient, not a magnified region of the product
a mounded heap at normal distance rather than an extreme close-up of a working surface

breakdown: A mound of fine white crystalline powder on a pale grey seamless, lit hard from the upper right so the heap casts a defined shadow to the lower left and the individual crystals at the edge read as granular rather than floury. Nothing else is in the frame. The filename names it as the MSM component of the same joint formula whose HCI ingredient is image 2 of this batch, so the argument is the same: this named material is really in the tub, shown in its delivered state. Register, camera and lighting design are the same commercial overhead still life. G3 is not engaged; there is no product, no body, no person, no mark, no text. The two decisions that separate it from 03-spec-macro are identical to image 2's — an ingredient rather than a region of the product, and a whole heap rather than an extreme close-up. This is the fifth observation of the proposed still life and it reaches SPEC 6.3's count, BUT it must not be counted as a fifth DISTINCT source: images 2 and 13 come from the same product page and the same photographic set-up, differing only in which powder is on the seamless. Curation should treat the two as one source, which leaves the proposal at four distinct sources and one short. Recording that here rather than letting a count do the arguing.

deviations.observed: a plain out-of-focus pale ground with no room at all, where the type requires one real room filled to the edges
the hand PRESENTS the product to the lens rather than operating it; the person exists only to give the object a scale

breakdown: A fist holds a matte black razor handle upright against a plain pale out-of-focus background, the product occupying the upper half of the frame and the hand the lower. The head of the razor is turned square to the camera so its silhouette reads cleanly. There is no room, no surface, no second object and no text. The argument is identity plus scale: this is the object, this is how big it is, and a human hand is the only ruler anyone needs. It is not a use moment — nothing is being shaved and the grip is a display grip rather than a working one. Register is commercial; camera is level and close with a long lens; light is broad and frontal with a soft falloff behind. G1 holds and is the whole point of the frame. G8 is not engaged. G3 is not engaged. 06-relief-hero is the nearest active type because it is the only one that puts a reduced subject with a product in a frame, and it breaks in two places: it demands a real room filled to the edges, and its POSE branch is about operating or not operating the product rather than about showing it. This is the FOURTH observation of present-to-lens: batch 2026-08-31-A recorded three across both registers and said in its own summary that the library has no home for it at either. With this one the pattern is past the evidence rule's three-observation bar and is the best-evidenced gap the corpus has produced after the animal subject.

A pale grey square carrying a two-line italic serif headline, Premium quality daily soft chews, above four ruled rows. Each row holds a small circular photograph at the left — a white cream, a pale yellow cream, an orange translucent slice and a beige granular powder — then a bold ingredient name, a benefit line under it, and a purple pill giving a dose: 3 Billion CFU, 100 mg, 100 mg, 75 mg. The argument is formulation transparency with dosage, which is a legitimate step-3 spec beat and one this library has no single frame for. It is rejected anyway, and the reason is instructive rather than dismissive. The four circular photographs are exactly the subject of the proposed 03-spec-stilllife, and on a live page that argument is usually delivered as separate ingredient tiles with the names and doses set in page HTML beside them. Here the page has baked the whole table into one asset. The library's answer to this beat is therefore N still-life tiles, not one table: thirteen text clusters in a single frame is an order of magnitude past anything a diffusion renderer has held in this library's evidence, and a dose figure baked into a picture is a claim that cannot be corrected without a re-render. Register is flat layout with photographic insets; there is no camera. G3 is not engaged. Recorded as the combined form of an argument the library already proposes to serve in pieces.

deviations.observed: a flat pale green field with no room at all, the subject cut out and placed against it
six text clusters — a headline, four icon-and-line claims and a regulatory footnote — where the drafted G16 budget is one block plus one badge

breakdown: A square split by content rather than by a drawn line: the right third carries a young woman laughing with her head tipped back, cut out and lit warm from behind, and the left two thirds carry a bold green headline, Feel Energy That Lasts, followed by four claims each with a small line icon — works within sixty minutes and lasts up to five hours, sustained energy and mental alertness, supports focus and mental clarity, supports thermogenesis and fat metabolism — and a two-line FDA disclaimer at the foot. The argument is the benefit stack: a face that has the feeling, and the feeling enumerated beside it. This is the single most common shape in the benefit slice of this corpus and the library has no type that produces it. 06-relief-hero is the nearest because a person carries a state, and it breaks in two ways that matter: the type demands one real room filled to the edges and this has no room at all, and the type carries no words while this carries six clusters. Register is commercial-editorial; the camera is close and the light is a warm backlight through hair. G3 is not engaged. This record is the central tension of the owner's Q1b decision stated as evidence: the argument is a real image argument, the picture half is inside this library's reach, and the text half is six times the budget the founding render round supports. Either the budget rises on measured evidence or this beat stays a page component with the library supplying only its photograph.

deviations.observed: the evidence is a pair of survey percentages set as type, not a physical difference the viewer inspects inside the frame
a footnote naming the study population and duration, which no type in this library has a slot for

breakdown: A warm brown-grey frame: a hand comes in from the upper right holding a cream capsule bottle with a blue cap over a marble ledge, loose capsules lie at the lower right, and the left half carries two very large numerals in a light serif — 91% over the line reported reduced overall food cravings, and 88% over reported reduced sugar cravings — separated by a thin rule, with a small footnote across the bottom naming a consumer survey of 274 participants over six weeks. The argument is statistical proof: most people who took it felt the thing you want to feel. That is a step-4 proof beat, and 04-proof-lockedframe is the nearest active type by job, but its whole discipline is that the difference must be visible to the naked eye inside a static frame and judged by the viewer. Here nothing is visible; the evidence is a number and its authority comes from the footnote. Register is commercial-editorial with a heavy warm grade; the camera is close and low over the ledge. G1 holds on the bottle. G3 is not engaged. The footnote is the part worth recording: it is substantiation, and this library has no rule about substantiation anywhere — G14 covers fabricated endorsement and nothing covers a fabricated statistic. A proposed statistic type would need that rule before it could have a skeleton. This file is byte-identical to the asset filed under lp3-12northfold-washno1 in this batch; one hash, one record.

deviations.observed: the frame shows the object and nothing else — identity, not a funnel-step argument

breakdown: A teal stand-up pouch stands square to the camera on a very pale grey ground with a soft contact shadow, its printed leaf motif and the words PROJECT:LIFE and Life Starts Here fully legible, a thirty-day supply and net weight line across the foot. Nothing else is in the frame: no hand, no prop, no scene, no added text, no badge. The argument is identity — this is the object, this is what arrives — which is the same class the ledger has rejected four times as a raw product photo. It is recorded as a candidate rather than a reject because the owner's Q2b decision of 2026-09-03 brings packshots inside the library's scope, and the change of standard is stated here so that a reader comparing this record with batches A and B is not left to guess why identical frames took opposite verdicts. Register is commercial catalogue; camera level at pack height; a broad soft key with a faint gradient behind to separate the pouch from the ground. G1 is trivially satisfied and is the point rather than a constraint. G7 would refuse this frame outright as an arrangement that exists only to make a photograph, which is the collision any identity family has to resolve before it can have a first type. Proposed id uses a step and a job that do not exist in the vocabulary and both are flagged. This is the clean sibling of image 6, which is the same class with claims stamped on.

A pink line-art double helix inside a thin pink circle with a diagonal bar struck through it, on a very pale pink disc. It is a no-GMO chip, and its whole meaning lives in the slash. There is no product, no person, no place, no photograph. Register is flat vector illustration; no camera, no lighting. The pink is decorative rather than a G3 signal. Nothing in G1 to G15 is testable. It is the second icon in this batch after image 9 and from the same product's set, which is the ordinary density: this corpus carries 99 icon files across nine of thirteen products. Recorded per the runbook's one-record-per-image rule. Together with images 1, 9 and 12 it makes the point the batch summary should carry: a gallery-biased selection is still roughly a third furniture, and no filename pattern separates the furniture from the argument reliably enough to skip opening the file.

deviations.observed: eight magnified callouts ring the subject on leader lines instead of stacking in a vertical band down one edge
a 3D anatomical render, where the rail is a photographic hero with photographic vignettes

breakdown: A translucent blue 3D anatomical figure stands centred on a dark teal ground, its skeleton visible through the body and eight joints glowing red — neck, both shoulders, elbow, lumbar spine, hip, both knees, ankle and hand. Eight circular callouts ring the figure on thin leader lines, each magnifying one of those joints so the inflammation reads at a size the whole-body view cannot give it. The argument is symptom coverage: the product answers pain in many places at once, and the reader finds their own joint somewhere on the ring. That is 02-symptom-rail's job with the layout changed from a band to a ring and the medium changed from photograph to render. Register is technical-medical; there is no camera, the light is a 3D key from the front, and the depth is synthetic. G3 is honoured exactly — red on the problem areas and nothing else carries a signal colour. G1 is not engaged because no product appears. No text of any kind, which distinguishes it from the other halo observation. Two structural decisions differ, so this is a type rather than a variant. It is the SECOND observation of the halo layout after batch 2026-09-03-C's dog-with-symptom-pills, and the two are from different products and different registers, which is what the evidence rule wants.

deviations.observed: a photographic still life of the culprit, where the type is a two-panel 2D illustration of a body structure
no product and no body structure — a tray of food carries the whole indictment

breakdown: A cafeteria tray shot from just above table height, desaturated to grey: a double cheeseburger in wrapper, a bag of nacho-cheese crisps, a paper sleeve of fries, a slice of pepperoni pizza, a plastic-lidded chocolate lava dessert, a foil energy bar and a soft drink in a paper cup. A single broad pink-magenta X is painted across the cup and the pizza. Behind, an empty canteen of tables and stools recedes out of focus. The argument is the indictment: this is what you are eating, and it is the cause. That is a cause-family argument made with no body and no product, exactly as batch 2026-08-31-B's abundance still life made the positive half of the same pair — and this is the NEGATIVE half, from the same product's page, which is why the two belong to one proposal. Two library rules are honoured here without being asked: G11's desaturation marks the unresolved state and the single X is the sanctioned signal mark, and G3's red family sits only on the problem. Register is documentary photograph plus one hand-painted mark; camera is level; the grade is the argument. This is the second observation of the cause still life.

deviations.observed: two parallel rows of three, an everyday analogy above and the biology below, joined by arrows
a heading and three captions baked into the frame

breakdown: A pale laboratory-toned square carrying the heading OXIDATIVE STRESS. The upper row holds three apple pairs, whole and halved: fresh green, then browning yellow, then shrivelled brown. The lower row holds three 3D cell renders: a smooth pink cell, then the same cell studded with blue radical clusters, then a collapsed brown cell with its membrane breaking. Two blue arrows run left to right between the rows, and three captions name the cells. The argument is an analogy: you already know what happens to a cut apple, and this is that, happening in you. That is a cause argument built from a familiar object rather than from anatomy, which is what separates it from 02-cause-anatomy's illustrated structure. Register is mixed — photographic fruit above, technical render below — which G5 would refuse inside a comparison frame, and this frame is a progression rather than a comparison, so the boundary is worth curation's attention. Camera is level and synthetic. Colour runs green to brown as decay and blue for the attacking agent, which reads against G3's assignment of blue to correct flow. No product, no body, no person.

deviations.observed: no person at all; the product in its working state carries the whole frame
a black cloth ground with no room, where the type requires one real room filled to the edges

breakdown: A tumbler of clear water on black cloth, lit from the front so the glass edge and the water line read against the dark. A white effervescent tablet sits mid-dissolve on the bottom, its edge already crumbling into a fine cloud rising through the water. In the upper right corner a thin circular badge with a tick-mark rim reads 90 MIN. The argument is the dose moment plus a duration claim: this is what taking it looks like and this is how long it works. G8 is satisfied in the purest form the library has seen — the visible output IS the product acting, made of real substance, and it is the whole subject. Register is commercial product photography; camera is level at glass height; the black ground is a studio choice rather than a place. **This is also the THIRD distinct observation of a person-free hero**, which 06-relief-hero's own KNOWN-FLAKY says is the trigger to draft a `--product` variant: it records two, names the bar as three, and says no prompt should ship a person-free hero until one arrives. Curation must decide whether this lands there or stands alone, because a second deviation — no room at all — is what stops it being a clean variant. The badge is a drawn mark carrying characters, which G6 bans and the owner's Q1b decision now permits under a declared text layer.

breakdown: A stock 3D render of a blue molecular lattice — glossy spheres joined by rods, receding into a blue-green haze with two lens-flare stars — with the letters NRF2 set across the middle in a heavy white slab face with a blue outer glow. There is no product, no body, no person, no place and no symptom. The argument is authority by association: a molecule the reader has not heard of, named in capitals, standing in for science. Strip the four characters and what remains is a generic molecule render that says nothing about this product or any other. Register is 3D stock illustration; there is no camera and no real light; the colour is decorative rather than a G3 signal. Nothing in G1 to G15 is testable against it. It is the same class as the price table and the offer list this ledger has already rejected — the argument is carried entirely by set characters over a stock image — with the extra problem that the image half is generic enough to belong to any supplement in the category. Recorded rather than skipped because the runbook requires one record per batch image, and because a science graphic is a shape the owner's Q1b decision will otherwise invite.

SUBJECT is a full person; POSE is operated and mid-action; SETTING is one real room filled to the edges with objects that genuinely belong; LIGHT is flat available daylight with mild overexposure at the window, which is exactly what the ugc register asks for and forbids cleaning up. G1 holds — the pouch is the exact reference and its printed face is legible. G8 is served: the fizz in the glass is the visible output. two FORMS of the same product, the retail carton and one single-dose sachet, rather than variants of it

deviations.observed: near-duplicate of the back-panel-plus-roundels tile recorded in batch 2026-08-31-B from the same product; same panel, same six yellow accreditation roundels, same blue ground, differing in crop and in the panel's size in frame

breakdown: The back panel of a white carton stood upright on a pale blue ground with a hard diagonal shadow, its PRODUCT FACTS table legible — glucosamine, MSM, chondroitin, bone broth, boswellia, UC-II collagen with milligram figures — followed by cautions, directions, a warning, storage and a manufacturer address. breakdown: A white tile: a bold headline 'Freestyle splicing' at the top, one rounded-corner photo panel filling the middle, a two-line caption beneath it. The photo is a close hand shot: two hands hold the edges of two inflatable mats together so the mating press studs on each edge meet, one stud on the grey underside of the upper mat and one on the green upper face of the lower one. The argument is a capability proved by demonstration rather than by a label: the frame does not name the part, it shows two hands performing the join the caption describes. Job is use rather than spec, because what is being sold is the ACTION of splicing two units and its ease, not the stud as a component. The device is a close-range hand demonstration, which vocabulary carries as the reserved value `demo` and which the ledger has already proposed twice under this id. Register is plain product photography at close range, no studio key, even light; camera is at the subject's level and close enough that the hands are cut by the frame. Ground is white and the text sits on it directly, which is well inside the corpus's own median of 0.89 value and 0.06 saturation. G3 is not engaged, no signal colour appears. G1 would bind hard if this were generated, because the studs are the whole claim and a redesigned edge makes the frame false. Strong: the caption and the picture argue the same thing, and the hands give scale without a ruler. Weak: the two mats are different colours, which reads for a moment as two different products rather than two of the same.

A dense composite: a dark headline bar 'Double layer air valve' across the top, one main photo, a circular inset at the lower right, a row of three yellow icon chips, and a grey note bar at the foot. The main photo shows a sock-clad foot pressing down on the mat's inflation valve, which is the operating action the product is sold on. The circular inset repeats the action with two hands instead of a foot, so the frame legislates that the valve works either way. The three chips read 'Press to inflate', 'Wear-resisting' and 'Comfortable', each an icon in a filled rounded square above a short label, which is one of the badge forms G16 names. The note bar carries an operating caveat, 'When inflating, close the air release valve on the back', which is an instruction rather than a claim. Job is use: every element teaches operation. Device is the same close hand or foot demonstration as img-03, here carrying an inset, so `inset_mode: detail` is the axis observed. Register is plain photography, mixed available light, no studio key; camera is close and slightly above. Ground inside the photo is the product's own fabric; the tile ground is white. G3 is engaged and breached in spirit: yellow is used as the chip fill, and G3 reserves yellow for neutral structure, but here it is acting as a highlight colour rather than as a signal about state. Strong: four separate things are taught in one tile without crowding. Weak: the main photo's foot reads oddly at thumbnail size, and the inset competes with the chips for the same corner.

deviations.observed: a three-panel press-and-restore strip is appended below the callout, so the tile carries a durability proof as well as a component map

breakdown: Two arguments stacked in one square. The upper two thirds is a CGI cross-section of the mat's internal air cells, drawn as a cutaway so the welded chambers and the top sheet read as separate parts, with three small dots on dashed leaders running down to three labels: 'Air support', 'Array welding connection', 'Comfortable material'. That is exactly the callout construction the library legislates: a subject at the centre with labelled satellites around it, joined here by the dashed-leader form which the type already names as one of its three parameters. The lower third is a strip of three small panels showing a finger pressing the inflated surface and the surface returning, captioned 'Round and plump', 'Exert oneself Press', 'Restore as before'. That strip is a locked-frame durability proof and it is a second argument, which is the one structural decision recorded as the variant. Job is spec: every label names a construction feature. Register is a technical render in the upper half and photography in the lower, which is a register mix G5 would refuse inside a comparison frame but which is not a comparison. Ground is white throughout. Colour is the product's own tan; the leader dots are yellow, which G3 reserves for neutral structure and which is defensible here. G1 is not testable, the subject is rendered rather than photographed. Strong: the cutaway makes an invisible internal structure locatable, which is the job A3 asks a mark to do. Weak: three labels compete with three captions in one square, and at tile size the lower strip's captions are the first thing to go.

A full-bleed photograph of the inflated mat lying inside a tent, shot down its length so the air channels run away from the camera, with warm low light raking across them from the right. Over the photograph sits a three-part text block: a gold eyebrow 'Skin-friendly fabric', a large white headline 'Bed like comfort', a short rule, and a two-line white support sentence naming the material, 'Nylon fabric with TPU coating is comfortable and soft without air leakage'. There is no panel, no card and no field behind the words; they are set directly into the photograph's own darker area, which is the third field form ADR-066 legislated for a claim stack and which works here because the tent's shadowed end gives the type somewhere to sit. Job is spec: the eyebrow and the support line both name the fabric, and the headline is the benefit that material buys. Device is a single photographic scene carrying a baked text layer, which the registry has no id for; `hero` is the nearest device value and the proposal keeps it. Register is available-light photography, warm, slightly hazy; camera is low and central. Ground is the scene itself rather than a seamless, so the ADR-068 measurement does not apply. G3 is not engaged. G6 is broken by design, which is what a declared text layer is for. Strong: the raking light does the material's work, showing the sheen and the weave without a macro. Weak: the headline is a category phrase rather than a hook, and the eyebrow and support line say the same thing twice.

A white tile whose upper half is a text block and whose lower half is the product. The text is the same three-part construction as img-06: a gold eyebrow 'Sleep comfortably', a black headline 'Integrated pillow', a short rule, and a support line 'Fit neck curve to ensure healthy curve'. Below it the pillow end of the inflated mat is photographed against white and cropped by the bottom edge, turned three-quarters so the raised pillow section and the flatter body behind it read as one continuous piece rather than two parts. The argument is a construction claim: the pillow is integral, so nothing else needs carrying. Job is spec. Device is again a single product scene with a baked text layer, so it files with img-06 and img-08 under the same proposal; here the scene is a plain white studio rather than a location, which is an environment parameter and not a second type. Register is commercial product photography, soft broad light from the upper left, no hard specular. Camera is low and close to the pillow's level, which is what makes the swell of the pillow legible. Ground is white, well within the corpus median. G3 is not engaged; no signal colour is used. G1 would bind if generated: the whole claim is that the pillow is not a separate object, so a redesigned join would make the frame false. Strong: the crop is doing real work, since cutting the mat off at the frame edge keeps the eye on the pillow. Weak: nothing gives scale, so a reader cannot tell whether the pillow is a head's width or a hand's.

A full-bleed close photograph of the inflated mat's surface, the tan air channels running diagonally across the frame and the grey underside visible at the lower right with one black valve set into it. The text block repeats the page's template exactly: gold eyebrow 'Comfort upgrade', large white headline '10CM thickening', a short rule, and a white support line 'Effectively isolate the ground moisture/cold air'. Job is spec and the claim is dimensional. This is the third instance of the same device on one page, which makes the construction a template rather than a one-off and is the reason the proposal is worth a file. The headline carries a FIGURE, '10CM', with nothing in the frame to substantiate it, which is exactly the fault A15 names; the same page substantiates the same number correctly in img-16 by putting a tape measure against the mat, and the contrast between the two frames is the most useful thing in this batch for the substantiation rule the library has not yet written. Register is available-light product photography, warm, shallow depth. Ground is the product's own surface. G3 is not engaged. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. Strong: the diagonal channels give the type a quiet band to sit in without a panel. Weak: the number is unsupported, and the eyebrow and headline both claim thickness so the block spends two lines on one idea.

A white tile with a headline 'Storage step' and a support line 'Easy storage and easy travel', over a two-by-two grid of four photographic panels, each on white, each with a numbered caption beneath it: '01. After deflation, spread it evenly on the ground', '02. Fold it twice in the left and right', '03. Roll it up from the top', '4. Close the air nozzle and put on the bandage'. The panels are ordered by action and the order is carried by the numerals rather than by arrows, which is precisely the distinction ADR-066 drew when it added the `--labelled` variant to this type: a label NAMES a panel, an arrow CARRIES the reading order, and only the second does the job the actions are supposed to do. Four panels in a two-by-two is also the layout that moved this type's panel count to four, and at a square ratio it PACKS the frame rather than striping it, which is what G15 asks. Job is use; device is sequence; the match is clean and this is the cleanest single observation in the batch. Register is plain product photography on white, even light, no shadow. G3 is not engaged. G1 would bind: the product must be the same object in all four panels, and here it is. Strong: each panel shows a genuinely different state of the same object, so the sequence teaches rather than decorates. Weak: the fourth caption drops the leading zero, and panel two and panel three are hard to tell apart at tile size.

A white specification tile. The top half is the inflated mat seen from above with dimension lines drawn along two edges and a third across the thickness, labelled '70cm 27.5"', '25cm/ 9.8"' and '165cm/ 65"'. Below it sit three measurement elements: a circular inset holding a steel tape measure stood against the mat's thickness, a graphic of a weight on a kitchen scale reading 'Weight / approximately 1.0kg (2.2lb)', and a photograph of the packed stuff sack with its own dimension lines, '29cm 11.4"' and '15cm/ 6"'. A row of four dark icon chips closes the tile: Comfortable, Waterproof, Portable, Environmental protection. The argument is the specification itself, and the device is the dimension line drawn onto the object rather than a label pointing at a part, which is what separates this from a callout. Job is spec; the device has no vocabulary value and `dimension` is proposed. This frame is the batch's second useful A15 datum: every figure here is a DIMENSION of the physical object, and a dimension line drawn on the object is substantiated by the object in a way a performance percentage never is. Register is mixed: knockout product photography, a photographic inset and flat vector graphics in one frame. Ground is white. G3 is not engaged; the chips are neutral dark grey. Strong: the tape-measure inset makes the thickness claim checkable. Weak: three different graphic registers in one tile, and the scale graphic is an illustration of a measurement rather than a measurement.

deviations.observed: a lifestyle photograph carrying force arrows is stacked above the two-panel comparison, so the tile argues the mechanism and then adjudicates it

breakdown: Four zones stacked. A headline 'Integrated design of pillow' and a support line; a gold spine icon with the label 'Protect the spine'; a main photograph of a woman lying on her back on the inflated mat, seen from the side, with a row of red upward arrows drawn along the mat's underside; two sub-headings with support lines, 'Ergonomic design' and 'Strip shape connection'; and at the foot a two-panel comparison, the product at the left carrying a green tick and a rival arrangement at the right, a separate pillow on a differently built mat, carrying a red cross. The comparison is the tile's verdict and is the reason it files against the split type rather than against a callout. G3 is obeyed by the marks and breached by the arrows: green is the confirmation badge and red is the wrong side, both correct, but the red upward arrows denote SUPPORT, which is a working mechanism and which G3 assigns to blue or cyan. That is worth recording as corpus evidence rather than as an error in the page, because a red or orange arrow for lift or support is a market convention this library's colour lock does not currently allow. Job is spec. Register is photography throughout, which keeps G5 satisfied across the comparison. Ground is white. Strong: the comparison names the alternative honestly, showing a real rival arrangement rather than a strawman. Weak: five separate text clusters plus two marks in one square is past any budget this library has measured, and the sub-headings are the first casualties at tile size.

A single photograph with no words anywhere in the frame. The inflated mat lies on a forest floor of dry leaves and bare earth, dappled sunlight falling across it, a folded wooden camp crate with a magazine on top standing just beyond it. There is no person, no hand, no packaging and no graphic layer. The argument is placement: this is where the object goes and what the evening around it looks like, and the frame sells the situation rather than a feature. Job is relief in the sense of the state after buying, but the state is carried by the SETTING rather than by a person's body, which is why it will not file against the existing relief scene type whose subject slot demands a person matched to a paired pain image. The ledger already carries one observation under this id and this is the second. The device name is provisional and probably wrong by this repo's own standard, since `mood` names a feeling rather than the mechanism; what the frame actually does is place the product alone in its destination, and a rename along those lines belongs in curation. Register is available-light documentary photography, warm, high sun through leaves, slight haze. Camera is high and looking down at maybe forty-five degrees. Colour is entirely natural; G3 is not engaged. G6 holds, there is no text and no logo. G1 would bind if generated and would be easy to break, since the mat's channel count and the valve's position are both legible here. Strong: the crate and the magazine give scale and a reason to be there without staging a person. Weak: nothing in the frame says the mat is inflatable, so the tile assumes the reader has already seen another one.

A white specification card split vertically. The left column carries a large '10cm' over 'Thickening', then a rounded colour pill holding a khaki swatch and the word 'Khaki', then three labelled figures set as label-over-value pairs: 'Expanded size: 195cm*70cm*10cm', 'Storage size: 29cm*15cm', 'Weight: approximately 1.0kg'. Beneath them the packed stuff sack in the same colourway. The right column shows the mat twice, its tan face and its grey underside abutted down a vertical seam, each half tagged with a small rounded pill reading 'Front' and 'Back'. The argument is the specification plus the colourway, and the front/back pairing answers a question a single face cannot: what the underside is made of. It files with img-10 under the same proposal because the device is the same, the specification presented as text beside the object, even though img-10 draws dimension lines and this one tabulates them. Job is spec. Register is knockout product photography on white with no shadow. Ground is white, at the very top of the corpus's value distribution. G3 is not engaged. Every figure here is a dimension or a mass, checkable against the object, which is the A15-friendly kind. Strong: front and back in one frame with two words is an efficient answer to a real doubt. Weak: the two halves are butted with no gap, so at a glance the mat reads as one object that is tan at one end and grey at the other.

The same specification card as img-13, identical in layout, typography, figures and structure, with the colourway changed to green: the pill reads 'Green', the swatch is sage, the mat's face and the stuff sack are sage, and the grey underside is unchanged. Nothing else differs. Under the absorption ladder this is level one: colorway is named in `vocabulary.parameters` as a runtime value that must never become identity, so a change of colourway does not change what the frame argues and the verdict is a match on the same proposal rather than a second candidate. Recording it as a match rather than a duplicate matters, because the bytes differ and the frame is a real page asset; what it is not is a second piece of evidence for the type. Job is spec. Register, ground, light and camera are all identical to img-13. G3 is not engaged. G1 would bind and the green face is a real colourway rather than an invented one, which is the distinction G2 draws when it permits choosing among real colourways and forbids inventing one. Strong: the page is internally consistent, three colourways on one template, which is what a buyer needs to compare them. Weak: nothing, at the level of this frame; the weakness is at page level, where three near-identical cards occupy three gallery slots that could have carried three different arguments.

The third instance of the specification card, identical to img-13 and img-14 in every structural respect, with the colourway set to navy blue: the pill reads 'Navy blue', the swatch and the mat's face and the stuff sack are dark navy, the grey underside is unchanged, and all three figures are the same. Absorption ladder level one again, colorway as a runtime parameter, verdict match. Three colourway cards on one page is itself a finding about the format rather than about the type: a direct-response product page will spend three of its gallery slots on the same tile with one variable changed, which is the behaviour `03-spec-lineup` exists to compress into a single frame. That compression is the argument for promoting the lineup type and it is visible here in the negative, as three slots doing what one could. Job is spec. Register is knockout product photography on white. Ground is white. G3 is not engaged. G1 would bind; navy is a real colourway. Strong: the dark face makes the grey underside read as a deliberate two-tone construction rather than as a shadow, which the khaki card does not manage. Weak: as with img-14, the weakness is the page's not the frame's, and a reader scrolling three of these learns one fact three times.

deviations.observed: two macro panels are stacked in one square, each with its own caption bar, rather than one frame filling the square

breakdown: Two horizontal panels stacked with a caption bar between and beneath them. The upper panel is a macro photograph of the mat's edge in cross-section with a steel tape measure stood vertically against it, the tape reading up past the 10 mark, and a white speech-bubble badge at the right carrying '10cm'; its caption reads 'The thickness upgrade is about 10cm, more comfortable'. The lower panel is an extreme close-up of the double inflation valve, the outer cap swung open on its tether and the inner nozzle visible, captioned 'Double inflation valve, more labor-saving'. Both panels are the macro type's own register, polished close-range product photography with the component filling the frame; what deviates is that there are two of them in one square, and at a square ratio two horizontal bands is striping rather than the packing G15 asks for. The upper panel is the most valuable frame in this batch for the substantiation question: it carries the same 10cm figure that img-08 asserts with nothing behind it, and here the instrument that produced it is in shot, which makes the number checkable by the reader rather than merely stated. That is the shape a substantiation rule would legislate, and the page contains both the right and the wrong version of the same claim. Job is spec. Ground is the product's own surface. G3 is not engaged. Strong: the tape measure. Weak: the speech-bubble badge duplicates a number the tape already gives, and the two panels share no light direction.

A white tile carrying a two-line headline '40D nylon TPU / Wear-resistant' and a support line 'Skin friendly smooth fabric'. Beneath them three sheets of material float apart along a vertical axis, each drawn as a soft curved plane with visible thickness: a white top sheet, a tan middle sheet, a darker tan lower sheet. Each has a small orange dot on a dashed leader running right to a labelled brown pill: 'Outer acrylic coating', '40D nylon fabric', 'Inner TPU film'. A row of three icon chips closes the tile: Antibiosis, Moisture-proof, Tear resistance. This is the exploded construction exactly as the type defines it, the product separated into its real component groups along one axis in a technical render, with the addition of labels that name each group. Job is spec; device is explode; the match is clean. It is worth flagging that this type had ZERO observations across the twenty-six source pages of the earlier direct-response corpus, and was one of the four active types the routing table recorded as absent from the format; this is its first, and it is the corpus correcting a table that said in its own words that absence meant absent from what was filed rather than absent from the format. Register is flat vector-and-gradient technical illustration, not photography. Ground is white. G3 is engaged by the orange leader dots, and orange is assigned to wrong pressure or wrong heat, so the dots are using a signal colour as decoration. Strong: three layers and three names, nothing more. Weak: the layers are illustrated rather than photographed, so a reader has no way to check that the real laminate has three.

A knockout packshot on pure white with no text anywhere in the frame. The inflated mat stands vertically, seen from directly above or face-on, the full length of the tan channelled face visible with the small printed care label near its foot; the packed stuff sack in the same colourway stands at the lower left with its drawstring and toggle hanging. Nothing else is in frame, there is no ground plane, no shadow beyond a faint contact shadow, no hand and no setting. This is the identity argument in its plainest form: what the object is and what it packs down to, answered with no claim attached, which is precisely what the type's purpose sentence says and precisely what its trigger warns must never be routed to a slot whose copy argues anything. The knockout setting is one of the three the type legislates and is the one that needs no G7 exemption, since a cut-out is already a graphic layer under that rule's scope note. Job is identity; device is pack; the match is clean, and this observation matters more than most because the type stood at four distinct sources against a criterion-1 bar of five. Register is commercial knockout product photography, broad even light, no specular. Ground is white, which is the top of the corpus distribution. G3 is not engaged, G6 holds, no words appear. Strong: showing the packed sack beside the deployed mat answers the size question without a single figure. Weak: with no shadow and no scale cue the two objects float, and a reader cannot tell whether the sack is the size of a water bottle or a rucksack.

A dark green tile. A white headline '24 hours moisturizing and hydrating' with a three-line support paragraph about not refilling at night. Below it the humidifier stands on an orange disc emitting two tall mist plumes that climb most of the frame's height, and a rounded-rectangle inset at the upper left holds a woman's face with her eyes closed and mist drifting across it. The argument is carried by the VISIBLE OUTPUT rather than by the object: the mist is what fills the frame and the product is the smaller half of the composition, which is exactly the configuration G8 legislates when visible_output is not none. The inset is a context inset showing the beneficiary rather than a magnified detail, so the axis value is context. Job is mechanism, because the frame's job is to show the thing working; device is the emanation itself, the plume that leaves the product and is the only visible evidence that anything is happening. Register is commercial product photography composited onto a flat coloured field, with a photographic inset in a different register again. Ground is dark green and heavily saturated, which sits in the third of the corpus ADR-068 legislates as a legitimate CHOICE rather than in the light near-neutral two thirds, and it is earned here because a white plume needs a dark field to read at all. G3 is not engaged; the green is brand rather than signal. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. Strong: the plumes are the product's whole proposition and they are given two thirds of the frame. Weak: the inset's woman is lit and graded quite differently from the product shot, so the two layers read as two sources.

A white tile carrying no photograph at all. A centred heading 'Product Parameter' over a small gold rule, then six green gradient bars stacked down the frame, each holding a label at the left and a value at the right: Product Name / Double nozzle spray, Tank Capacity / 2000ml, Product Material / ABS/PP, Timing Spray / 12 hours, Product Dimensions / 130*130*159mm, Power / 5V/1A. The argument is the specification stated as a table, with nothing to look at and nothing to judge visually. This is a real and common product-page gallery tile and it is not a screenshot of text, so it is not a reject; what it is is a type this registry has no id for, because every existing spec type puts an object in the frame. Job is spec; the device is the table itself. Every figure here is a physical specification of the object or its supply, checkable against the unit or its manual, which is a different class from the performance percentages A15 was written about and worth separating when that rule is eventually drafted. Register is flat graphic design, no photography, no render. Ground is white behind green bars. G3 is not engaged. G6 is entirely broken, which is the point of the tile. Strong: it answers the six questions a buyer actually types into a search box, in the order they ask them. Weak: gold type on a mid-green gradient is close to the contrast floor, and at tile size the values are the first thing to go.

Two identical units stand side by side on the same dark green field, lit identically, photographed from the same height and distance, each emitting mist from its twin nozzles.
