The left unit's plumes are continuous columns; the right unit's are broken into separate puffs. Beneath each sits one label in a serif face: 'Continuous spray' and 'Interstitial spray'. This is the locked-frame construction exactly as the type defines it, a multi-panel comparison with the camera held and exactly ONE variable changed, and the variable here is an operating MODE rather than a build difference, which is what separates it from the lineup type. The reader judges the difference themselves, which is the type's whole purpose. Job is proof; camera_lock is strict. Register is commercial product photography on a flat field. Ground is dark saturated green, the same legitimate choice the page makes throughout, and here it is doing real work because neither plume would read against a light ground. G3 is not engaged. G4 is not engaged: neither side is the wrong side, both are correct modes, which is the deliberately neutral proof layout the rule's scope note exempts. G1 would bind hard, since the two units must be the same object for the comparison to mean anything, and here they are. Strong: the only difference in the frame is the difference being argued. Weak: the two mist patterns are genuinely hard to tell apart at tile size, so the labels are carrying more than they should.

The humidifier stands on a low orange plinth against a dark green field, two mist plumes rising and spreading across the upper half of the frame. Above them a white headline '2000ml large capacity' and a support line 'Continuous humidification is effective'. Same construction as img-03 without the inset: product low, output high, text at the top, dark field throughout. The tile's claim is a capacity figure but its PICTURE is the emanation, and under G8 the output is the subject whenever the product has a visible one, so it files with img-03 rather than with the page's text-led spec tiles. Job is mechanism; device is emanation. Register is commercial product photography composited on a flat field, with a soft rim of teal light along the product's shoulder that reads as the unit's own indicator rather than as a studio rim. Ground is dark and saturated, the page's consistent choice and the right one for white mist. The headline carries a figure, 2000ml, with nothing in the frame to substantiate it, which is the A15 fault; unlike the capix-mat tape measure there is no instrument in shot here, and the page's own parameter table is the only place the number is supported. G3 is not engaged. G6 is broken by the text layer. Strong: the plinth lifts the product clear of the frame's bottom edge and gives the plumes room. Weak: the headline's number and the picture's argument are two different claims sharing one tile.

The white colourway of the humidifier stands at the right on a green table against a pale wall, mist rising from both nozzles. The left third of the frame carries a headline 'Air humidifier', a two-line support sentence, and then a vertical stack of four claims, each a line-drawn icon in a thin circle followed by a short label: High capacity, Double spout, Ambient Light, Mute. This is the claim-stack construction — a subject holding one side and a headline with short claim lines filling the other — and it is the single commonest argument image on a direct-response product page, which is why the existing claimstack proposal carries nine sources. What differs here is the JOB: the existing type is step six and its claim lines describe a felt state, while these four describe FEATURES. Under SPEC 3.1 two jobs are two types however alike the picture, so this is filed as a spec-job sibling rather than as a match, and whether the two should merge is a curation question this batch is deliberately not answering. Register is commercial product photography in a real interior. Ground is a pale wall, light and near-neutral, with the green table as a colour accent. G3 is not engaged; the icons are neutral dark. G6 is broken by the text layer. Strong: four features, four icons, no paragraph. Weak: 'Mute' is a noise claim with nothing behind it, and the icons are generic enough that three of the four teach nothing the label does not.

A white tile headed 'Product Size'. The green humidifier stands centred and is drawn with three dimension lines: a vertical line at the right with arrowheads at both ends labelled '159mm', and two lines running along the base's front edges labelled '130mm' and '130mm'. Nothing else is in the frame, no icons, no claims, no support text. This is the dimension device in its purest form and it is the second distinct SOURCE for the proposal raised in batch A, where the capix-mat page carried it four times. The device is the dimension line drawn onto or beside the object, which is what separates it from a callout: a callout's leader points at a PART and names it, a dimension line spans a distance and measures it. Job is spec. Register is knockout product photography on white with no shadow. Ground is white, at the very top of the corpus value distribution. G3 is not engaged. Every figure is a dimension of the physical object and is substantiated by the object itself, which is the A15-benign class. G1 would bind: a redesigned body makes all three numbers wrong at once. Strong: three numbers, one object, no decoration, and it answers the question a buyer of a desk appliance actually has. Weak: the lines are drawn in thin black on white with no leader offset, so at tile size the '130mm' pair crowds the product's base.

deviations.observed: there is no hero photo; the tile is the symptom band alone, with panels alternating photo-left and photo-right

breakdown: A dark green tile headed 'Are you still worried about dryness?' with a second line 'Large capacity humidifier can solve the problem'. Below it two white bands, each holding a photograph at one end and a symptom name with an explanatory paragraph at the other, alternating sides: 'Dry skin' with a woman touching a reddened cheek, and 'Dry and itchy nose' with a woman pinching a reddened nose. Both photographs are DESATURATED to greyscale with only the afflicted area left red, which is G11 and G3 both obeyed precisely — saturation carrying the state, and red reserved for the problem area. The type this files against is the symptom rail, whose skeleton pairs a hero photograph with a vertical vignette band; here the hero is absent and the band is the whole tile, which is the one structural decision recorded. Job is symptom: the tile widens the problem across complaints rather than naming a single pain. Register is stock photography, greyscale with a spot tint. Ground is dark green behind white bands. G4 is not engaged, there is no correct side in frame. Strong: the spot-tint convention does the locating work A3 asks for, putting the claim exactly where the body hurts. Weak: the paragraphs are four and three lines of small type, far past anything this library has measured as legible at tile size, and the second model's expression is performed rather than physical, which is the fault G9 exists to rank below evidence.

The same tile construction as img-09 with two further symptoms: 'Dry throat', with a greyscale photograph of a woman's neck and the throat area tinted red, and 'Be depressed', with a greyscale photograph of a woman holding her head. Headline, band layout, alternation and type treatment are identical, so this is a second instance of the same variant rather than a second decision, and it is filed as a match supporting the variant img-09 proposes. Job is symptom. The second panel is the weaker of the four across both tiles and is worth recording: 'Be depressed' is a MOOD rather than a symptom, the photograph shows a performed gesture rather than a physical fact, and no part of the image can be tinted because there is nothing locatable to tint — so the spot-tint convention that carries the other three silently fails here. That is A3 read forwards: where the effect cannot be located, the device that locates effects has nothing to do. Register is greyscale stock photography with a spot tint. Ground is dark green behind white bands. G3 is obeyed, red on the afflicted area only. G11 is obeyed. G9 is broken by the second panel, where an expression stands in for evidence. Strong: four symptoms across two tiles builds a real breadth argument for an appliance whose benefit is otherwise invisible. Weak: the fourth panel is doing the type's job without the type's evidence.

The same tile as img-07 with the colourway changed from white to green: identical headline 'Air humidifier', identical two-line support, identical vertical stack of four icon-and-label claims — High capacity, Double spout, Ambient Light, Mute — identical interior setting, identical mist. Only the product's body colour differs. Under the absorption ladder this is level one, colorway being named in vocabulary.parameters as a runtime value that must never become identity, so the verdict is a match on the same proposal and this frame adds no evidence for the type beyond confirming that the page treats the construction as a template. Job is spec. Register, ground, camera and light are unchanged from img-07. Ground is a pale wall, light and near-neutral. G3 is not engaged. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. This is the second colourway pair observed in two batches: capix-mat repeated a specification card across three colourways, and this page repeats a claim stack across two. Both are the behaviour that the lineup type exists to compress into a single frame, and seeing it twice in two sources is the beginning of a real argument for promoting that type. Strong: the green body against the green table is the more coherent of the two frames. Weak: the same weakness as img-07, and repeated: 'Mute' is still a noise claim with nothing behind it, and this page elsewhere uses the word quiet about the same fact.

deviations.observed: a circular inset showing the unit running on a dark field is added to the plain knockout packshot

breakdown: A knockout packshot on pure white: the green humidifier seen three-quarters, its white lid and teal indicator line clearly legible, the printed 'H2O Humidifier' mark on its face. At the lower left a circular inset holds the same unit on a dark green field with both mist plumes running. There is no text anywhere in the frame. The base construction is the identity argument in its plainest form — what the object is, answered with no claim attached — and the one structural decision is the inset, which shows the product in operation rather than magnifying a detail. That matters because the type as drafted declares no axes at all, so an inset is an addition to its skeleton rather than a value within it. Job is identity; device is pack; the setting is the knockout form, which is the one that needs no G7 exemption since a cut-out is already a graphic layer under that rule's scope note. This is the third distinct source for the type across two batches. Register is commercial knockout photography for the main subject and a composited field shot for the inset, which is a register mix the library would refuse inside a comparison frame but which G5 does not reach here. Ground is white. G3 is not engaged; G6 holds, no words appear. Strong: the inset answers 'and what does it do' without a single word, which is the cheapest possible way to keep an identity tile from being inert. Weak: the inset's dark field is the only dark area in an otherwise white frame and pulls the eye before the product does.

A pale tile carrying no photograph. A two-line heading, 'Double Nozzle Spray / Humidification Large Capacity Durable', sits under a small corner bracket, and below it six claims are laid out in a two-by-three grid, each an orange line icon in a thin orange circle followed by a short green label: Quiet humidification, Super large capacity, Fine spray, Prevent dry burning, Double spray port, Mild night light. Thin rules separate the rows. This files with img-04 under the same proposal because the argument is identical — the specification stated as text and graphics with no object in the frame — but the two are different sub-forms and the difference is worth recording for curation: img-04 is a parameter TABLE giving label-and-value pairs that are measurements, while this is a feature GRID giving icon-and-name pairs that are capabilities. Whether those are one type or two is exactly the kind of question the absorption ladder settles on evidence, and two sub-forms on one page is not yet that evidence. Job is spec. Register is flat graphic design. Ground is a pale warm grey, light and near-neutral. G3 is engaged and breached: orange carries every icon and every circle, and G3 assigns orange to wrong pressure or wrong heat, so a signal colour is being used decoratively across six marks. Strong: six capabilities in one glance with no paragraph anywhere. Weak: 'Quiet humidification' is the third appearance of a noise claim on this page and the frame still has nothing behind it.

deviations.observed: macro panels alternate with text blocks in a packed two-by-two checkerboard rather than one component filling the frame

breakdown: A white tile headed 'Intimate details' over a two-by-two checkerboard: upper left a macro photograph of the lid's concentric water-wave moulding with the two nozzle holes in it, upper right a text block naming it 'water wave spray nozzle' with a three-line explanation about preventing overflow; lower left a text block naming the 'button switch' with a four-line explanation of the click sequence, lower right a macro photograph of the lid's button. Both photographs are the macro type's own register — polished close-range product photography with the component filling its cell and the material's surface quality readable — and what deviates is the layout, two components and two explanations packed into one square rather than one frame carrying one component. At a square ratio this PACKS rather than stripes, which is what G15 asks, and it is worth noting against the capix-mat frame in batch A which carried the same two-component idea as two horizontal bands and therefore striped. Job is spec. Ground is white and the product is white, so the frame is almost entirely high-key and the moulding reads only by its shadow. G3 is not engaged. Strong: the checkerboard gives each component its own quadrant and its own sentence, and the diagonal reading order is legible without an arrow. Weak: the explanations are three and four lines of small type, and a white product on a white ground with soft light is the hardest thing this page asks of a reader's screen.

The same two-by-two checkerboard as img-15 with two further components and no headline: upper left a macro photograph of the unit's teal indicator strip running around its shoulder, upper right a text block 'Colorful mood lights' with a two-line explanation about gradient breathing light; lower left a text block 'USB charging port' with a four-line explanation, lower right a macro photograph of the port set into the body beneath the same teal strip. Identical construction, identical register, identical cell proportions, so this is a match supporting the variant img-15 proposes rather than a second decision. Job is spec. The teal light strip is the product's own indicator rather than a signal mark, so G3 is not engaged even though the frame is dominated by cyan; that distinction matters, because a reader of the ledger looking for cyan-as-correct-mechanism would otherwise count this frame wrongly. Register is polished macro product photography on white. Ground is white. Strong: both photographs show a feature that is genuinely invisible in the page's other tiles, which is the job a macro is for, and the port shot answers a real doubt about whether the cable is captive. Weak: dropping the headline leaves the tile with no statement of what it is about, so read alone it is two details and two paragraphs with no argument over them.

Visually identical to img-08 in this same batch: the 'Product Size' heading, the green humidifier centred on white, the same three dimension lines labelled 159mm, 130mm and 130mm, the same type treatment and the same crop. The file hash differs, so this is a second asset rather than the same file twice, but nothing in the argument, the layout, the register or the measurements differs and it adds no evidence. Filed as a duplicate rather than a match so that curation's source and instance counts are not inflated by a page shipping the same tile at two sizes, which is a common export artefact. Job is spec; the nearest id is the dimension proposal raised in batch A and matched by img-08 here. Register is knockout product photography on white. Ground is white. G3 is not engaged; G6 is broken by the dimension labels, which is what a declared text layer is for. The observation worth keeping is procedural rather than about the image: a duplicate verdict on a byte-distinct file is the only way a source's real instance count survives an export that ships tiles twice, and this batch's manifest found exactly one true byte-identical pair elsewhere in the drop, so both kinds occur and both need catching.

deviations.observed: two in-use photo panels are appended at the right of the knockout packshot, so the tile identifies the object and demonstrates it in one frame

breakdown: A marketplace-style composite on white. The left two thirds hold a knockout packshot of a lilac electric fascia ring, its LED display reading L5, with the grey fastening strap laid below it. The right third is two stacked photographic panels: the device held against a waist, and the device worn strapped around a waist, each with cyan wave arcs drawn radiating from it. The base argument is identity — what the object is and what comes with it — and the one structural decision is the pair of in-use panels appended at the side, which turns a plain packshot into a packshot plus proof of placement. Job is identity, device is pack, setting is the knockout form that needs no G7 exemption. The cyan arcs are the most correct use of a signal colour in three batches: G3 assigns blue and cyan to correct support, correct flow and working mechanism, and the arcs denote the vibration doing its job. Register mixes knockout product photography with two lifestyle photographs, which G5 does not reach because there is no comparison in frame. Ground is white throughout. G6 holds, no words appear anywhere. G1 would bind hard across three layers, since the same device must be the same object in the packshot and in both panels. Strong: a buyer learns the object, the accessory and two placements without a single word. Weak: the two panels are small enough that at tile size the arcs read as noise rather than as vibration.

A pale lilac tile headed 'Constant Vibration Mode'. The left half is a photograph of a woman wearing the device strapped at her waist, cyan wave arcs drawn at each of the two contact rings. The right half holds two white cards: '5 Intensity Levels' listing L1 Muscle Activation, L2 Fascia Relaxation, L3 Muscle Mobility, L4 Daily Massage, L5 Professional Mode as labelled pills, and below it '3 Smart Variable Frequency Modes' with three circles reading P1, P2, P3. This is the claim-stack construction with a subject holding one side and a headline plus short claim lines filling the other, and the claims are SETTINGS rather than felt states, which is the spec job. It is the SECOND distinct source for the proposal raised on clou-diaxi in batch B, which matters because the existing relief-job claimstack carries nine sources and the question of whether these are one type or two will be settled on exactly this count. Register is commercial lifestyle photography with flat graphic cards. Ground is pale lilac, light and low in saturation, inside the corpus's ordinary two thirds. G3 is obeyed by the cyan arcs. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. Strong: five levels named by what they are FOR rather than by number alone, which is rare and is the difference between a spec list and a reason to buy. Weak: the two cards are stacked with no visual hierarchy between them, so the second reads as an afterthought.

A headline 'Innovative Dual-Ring Vibration' with two support lines, 'Larger Cover Area & Stronger and More Even Vibration' and 'Promote body sculpting and fat burning'. Below it the device sits on a rendered cross-section of human tissue — a skin layer over rows of illustrated fat cells — with white wave lines drawn from each of its two contact rings down into the tissue. The argument is what happens at the boundary between product and body, which is a mechanism job, and the device is the contact surface itself rather than an interior cutaway of the product; the ledger has proposed this id twice before and this is the third instance. Register is a technical render with no photography. Ground is pale lilac. G3 is not engaged: the waves are white rather than a signal colour, which is a missed opportunity since cyan would have carried the working-mechanism meaning the rule assigns. What this frame does that no rule in this repo governs is assert a physiological OUTCOME — body sculpting and fat burning — through an illustration of fat cells that nothing substantiates, which is A15's problem arriving in a picture rather than in a figure. Strong: the cross-section makes an invisible action locatable, which is the job A3 asks of a mark. Weak: the tissue render is generic enough to mean nothing, and the claim attached to it is the strongest on the page with the least behind it.

The device shown large on pale lilac with its body rendered semi-translucent so an internal cylindrical battery glows green through it. A labelled pill 'Type-C Charging' sits at the upper right on a dashed leader running to the charging port, with a black USB-C connector drawn entering from the frame edge. Two icon-and-figure claims close the tile: a battery icon with '1200mAh Large Capacity Battery', and a timer icon with '15Mins Timer Auto-Off'. The device that carries the frame is the see-through interior, which is the x-ray idiom the registry already owns, but the JOB is spec rather than mechanism: the frame argues capacity and charging rather than how the product acts on a body. Under SPEC 3.1 that makes it a different type from the existing x-ray however alike the picture, and it is the fourth job-and-device recombination this corpus has produced in three batches. G3 is engaged and breached: green is reserved for a confirmation badge only, and here it is the fill of a component. Register is a product render rather than a photograph. Ground is pale lilac, light and low in saturation. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. Both figures are physical specifications of the cell and the timer, checkable against the unit, which is the A15-benign class. Strong: showing where the battery sits answers a real doubt about a hollow-looking object. Weak: a glowing green battery is a rendering convention rather than an x-ray, and nothing in the frame says how large the cell is relative to the body.

deviations.observed: a circular accessory inset is composited into one cell, and each cell carries a caption bar

breakdown: A tile headed '2-in-1 Massage Method' over two photographic cells of equal size. The left cell shows a hand gripping the device and pressing it against a forearm, captioned 'Handheld Massage Fascia Ring'. The right cell shows the device worn strapped around a waist, captioned 'Hands-free Massage Fascia Ring with Strap', with a circular inset at its upper corner holding the folded strap and the label '1.4M Strap'. The argument is that ONE unit does two jobs, which is exactly the distinction the lineup type's own trigger draws when it sends that case to the grid type. What deviates from the grid's skeleton is the accessory inset composited into a cell and the caption bars beneath each, since the type is defined as a photographic multi-cell collage with no graphic overlays. Job is use. Register is commercial lifestyle photography. Ground is pale lilac behind white-bordered cells. G3 is not engaged. G15 is satisfied at a square ratio, two equal cells side by side packing rather than striping. G1 would bind across both cells and the inset. Strong: the two modes are genuinely different actions rather than two angles on one action, which is what makes the cell count honest. Weak: the strap inset sits on top of the second photograph's subject and the '1.4M' figure is the only measurement on the tile, orphaned from the page's dimension frame.

A tile headed 'Full-Body Muscle Recovery & Relaxation' over a three-by-two grid of six photographic cells, each showing the device placed on a different part of a body and each captioned with a single word in a lilac bar: Butt, Back, Waist, Thigh, Arm, Shoulder. This is the grid type in its purest observed form — one unit, many jobs, photographic cells, one variable across them — and it is the cleanest match in this batch. At a square ratio a three-by-two PACKS the frame, which is what G15 asks and which the page's other multi-panel tiles do not always manage. Job is use. Register is commercial lifestyle photography throughout, one model, one wardrobe, consistent light across all six cells, which is what keeps the set reading as one product rather than six. Ground is white behind the cells. G3 is not engaged; no signal colour appears. G6 is broken by the caption bars, which are the minimum text a grid of this kind can carry and still be legible. G1 binds across six layers and holds: the same object appears in all six. Strong: six placements is a breadth argument that no single photograph could make, and the one-word captions cost nothing. Weak: the sixth cell breaks the pattern by showing the device held at a neck rather than strapped, so the grid's own variable is not quite constant.

A tile headed 'Product Details' over three horizontal bands. Each band pairs a lilac label block at the left with a macro photograph at the right: 'Digital LCD Display' beside a close shot of the lit display and gold button, 'Standard Soft Strap' beside the strap laid flat, 'Ergonomic Comfortable Grip' beside a close shot of the moulded handle aperture. The construction is the macro type carrying more than one component in one square, paired with text, which is the variant clou-diaxi raised in batch B as a two-by-two checkerboard; this is the SECOND distinct source for that variant and it uses a band layout rather than a checkerboard. The difference matters for G15: at a square ratio three horizontal bands is striping rather than packing, and the checkerboard form packs. Both forms are now observed and whether they are one variant or two is a curation question. Job is spec. Register is polished close-range product photography on white. Ground is white behind lilac label blocks. G3 is not engaged; the lilac is brand rather than signal. Strong: three components, three names, no paragraph anywhere, which is the discipline the page's other tiles lose. Weak: the middle band's subject is an accessory rather than a part of the product, so the tile's own category slips between the second and third rows.

A tile headed 'How to Use:' over five photographic panels, three across the top and two across the bottom, each numbered and captioned: long press to turn on with the display reading L1, short press to select intensity with the display reading P2, hold the ring to massage, long press to turn off, and attach the strap for hands-free use. The order is carried by numerals and captions rather than by arrows, which is the labelled variant ADR-066 added to this type and the SECOND distinct source for it in this drop after capix-mat's storage sequence in batch A. Panel count here is five against that frame's four, which SPEC 3.2 already makes a parameter rather than a second decision. Job is use; device is sequence. Register is close product photography for the four control panels and lifestyle photography for the fifth, a register shift inside one sequence that the type does not currently legislate and that is worth recording. Ground is white. G3 is not engaged. G15 is satisfied, a three-plus-two arrangement packing a square. G1 binds across five panels and holds. Strong: the display is legible in the first two panels and reads a different value in each, so the instruction is demonstrated rather than asserted. Weak: panels one, two and four are nearly identical framings of a thumb on a button, and only the display distinguishes them.

A white tile with no headline. The device sits at the upper right with three dimension lines around it reading 14.5cm/5.71inch across the top, 13.5cm/5.31inch down the left and 3.5cm/1.38inch across the lower right for its depth. The strap is coiled at the lower left with three further lines reading 8cm/3.15inch, 140cm/55.12inch and 9.5cm/3.74inch. Nothing else is in the frame. This is the THIRD distinct source for the dimension proposal — capix-mat in batch A, clou-diaxi in batch B, fosen-ring here — which puts it past SPEC 6.2's evidence threshold and more than half way to criterion 1. The device is consistent across all three: a line spanning a distance with arrowheads and a dual-unit label, drawn beside or onto the object, which is what separates it from a callout whose leader points at a part and names it. Job is spec. Register is knockout product photography on white. Ground is white, at the top of the corpus value distribution. G3 is not engaged. Every figure is a dimension of a physical object and is substantiated by the object, the A15-benign class, and this frame gives both metric and imperial which none of the earlier three did. Strong: dimensioning the strap as well as the device answers the one question a wearable accessory raises. Weak: six lines in one frame with no visual hierarchy, and the two shortest labels collide with the objects they measure.

A knockout packshot on pure white: the lilac device alone, seen three-quarters from above, its black control strip with the lit L5 display, gold button and charging port all legible, no strap, no text, no shadow beyond a faint contact tone. This is the identity argument stripped to nothing but the object, which is what the type's purpose sentence describes and what its trigger reserves for a slot whose copy argues nothing. The setting is the knockout form, the one that needs no G7 exemption under that rule's scope note. Job is identity; device is pack. Register is commercial knockout product photography, broad even light, a soft specular along the upper moulding that reads as the material's own sheen rather than as a studio rim. Ground is white. G3 is not engaged. G6 holds: the only lettering in frame is the product's own lit display, which is diegetic. G1 would bind absolutely, since there is nothing else in the frame to carry the argument. Strong: the three-quarter angle shows the aperture, the grip and the control strip at once, which is the most information a single angle on this shape can give. Weak: with no scale cue and no shadow the object floats, and a reader cannot tell whether it is hand-sized or the size of a dumbbell, which is precisely the doubt the in-hand type exists to answer.

A second knockout packshot on pure white, the same lilac device seen square-on from the front so both apertures and the waisted outline read as a symmetrical silhouette, with only the top edge of the control strip visible. No strap, no text, no shadow. Viewing angle is one of the four kinds of information G2 permits a product slot to carry, so a second angle on the same object is a parameter rather than a second argument and the verdict is a match. What the frame adds over img-12 is the outline: the three-quarter view flattens the waisted shape and this one does not, which is why a page ships both. Job is identity; device is pack; setting is knockout. Register is commercial knockout product photography, broad even light, no specular. Ground is white, at the top of the corpus distribution. G3 is not engaged; G6 holds. G1 would bind absolutely. This is the fifth identity-pack instance on this one page across four assets, which is the finding worth carrying to curation: the identity family is not a single tile on a direct-response product page, it is a SET of angles and states, and the type as drafted describes one frame rather than the set a page actually ships. Strong: the silhouette is the fastest way to recognise this object again in a gallery. Weak: front-on hides the control strip entirely, so read alone the tile shows an object with no controls.

A flat-lay on white headed 'Packing List:' with five lines of text in two columns — Electric Fascia Ring, 140cm Strap, Instruction Manual, Charging Cable, Packaging Box. Below the text the five items are photographed laid out: the printed lilac carton standing at the centre, the coiled strap at the left, a folded instruction leaflet, a black USB cable, and the device itself at the right. This is the identity type's 'with contents' form — the pack plus what is inside it — and it is the clearest instance of that form in three batches. Job is identity; device is pack; setting is knockout on white. The carton carries printed marketing copy: 'Fascial ring', 'Deep shock grease', 'Tight Shape', 'Relaxing massage' and a model code. That printing is diegetic and permitted, and it is exactly the surface A15's addendum names as the door nothing was watching — a claim set legibly on an object, written by the packaging rather than by the page, and unverifiable from the frame. Register is commercial flat-lay product photography. Ground is white. G3 is not engaged; G6 holds for the page's own layer, since the only claims are on the box. Strong: the text list and the photograph say the same thing twice in two registers, which is the right redundancy for a question about what arrives. Weak: 'Deep shock grease' on the carton is a translation artefact that a reader will notice before they notice the contents.

The same composite construction as img-03 with the colourway changed to black: a knockout packshot of the device at the left with the grey strap below it, and two stacked lifestyle panels at the right showing the device held against a waist and worn strapped, cyan wave arcs at each contact point. The model's wardrobe differs from img-03's, pale blue rather than olive, but the structure, the proportions and the argument are identical. Colorway is named in vocabulary.parameters as a runtime value that must never become identity, so this is absorption-ladder level one and the verdict is a match on the variant img-03 proposes rather than a second decision. Job is identity. Register mixes knockout product photography with lifestyle panels. Ground is white. G3 is obeyed by the cyan arcs, which denote the working mechanism. G6 holds, no words appear. G1 binds across three layers and holds. This is the third colourway repetition observed across three sources — capix-mat spent three slots on one specification card, clou-diaxi two on one claim stack, and this page two on one identity composite — which is now a pattern rather than a coincidence and is the strongest argument this drop has produced for the lineup type, whose whole purpose is to compress exactly this into one frame. Strong: the black body makes the cyan arcs read better than the lilac version does. Weak: a buyer who has already seen img-03 learns nothing here but a colour.

A third instance of the composite: knockout packshot of the lilac device at the left with the strap below it, two lifestyle panels at the right showing the handheld and strapped placements with cyan arcs. It differs from img-03 in the product's viewing angle, square-on rather than three-quarter, and in the panels' wardrobe, which matches img-17's pale blue rather than img-03's olive. Both differences are parameters — angle is one of the four kinds of information G2 permits a product slot to carry, and wardrobe is environment — so this is a match rather than a duplicate, and it is a third asset of one construction rather than a third argument. Job is identity; device is pack. Register mixes knockout and lifestyle photography. Ground is white. G3 is obeyed by the cyan arcs. G6 holds. G1 binds across three layers. Taken with img-03, img-12, img-15, img-16 and img-17 this page ships SIX identity-pack frames out of fifteen, which is the single most useful count in this batch: on a direct-response product page the identity family is not one tile among twelve, it is nearly half the gallery, and the type as drafted legislates one frame rather than the set. Strong: the square-on angle reads the silhouette better than img-03's three-quarter. Weak: three near-identical composites in one gallery is the behaviour the lineup type exists to replace.

A white tile headed 'Product Parameters:' with twelve label-and-value lines running down the left — Product Name, Material ABS, Color Purple, Rated Voltage 3.7V, Rated Power 10 W, Battery Type, Battery Model 18650, Battery Capacity 1200mAh, Charging Time 3-4 hours, Full Charge Usage Time 4-50 minutes, Net Weight 286g, Charging Indicator, and whether it can be used while charging — and the device photographed knockout at the right. This is the SECOND distinct source for the table proposal raised on clou-diaxi in batch B, and it differs from that one in a way worth recording: clou-diaxi's parameter table carried NO object at all, while this one puts the product beside the list. Whether the presence of the object is a parameter or a second type is a curation question, and two sources with two forms is the evidence that makes it worth asking. Job is spec. Register is flat typography beside knockout product photography. Ground is white. G3 is not engaged. G6 is broken by the whole tile, which is what a declared text layer is for. Every figure is a physical specification checkable against the unit or its manual, the A15-benign class, with one exception: 'Full Charge Usage Time: 4-50 minutes' is either a typographical error or a range so wide it tells a buyer nothing, and it sits directly above a net weight given to the gram. Strong: twelve answers in one tile, in the order a buyer asks them. Weak: twelve lines of small type is past anything this library has measured as legible at gallery-tile size.

A knockout flat-lay on white: a white and gold HIFU/RF beauty wand at the right with its lit display reading HIFU / RF / EMS and 88min, a white mains adapter with coiled cable at the lower left, a folded operation manual titled 'HIFU RF Beauty Instrument', and a line-drawn plug icon above the words 'AU PLUG 100 - 240V'. This is the identity type's with-contents form: the object, what powers it and what documents it, answered with no claim attached. Job is identity, device is pack, setting is the knockout form that needs no G7 exemption. Register is commercial knockout product photography, broad even light, no cast shadow. Ground is white, at the top of the corpus value distribution. G3 is not engaged; the blue ring on the treatment head is the product's own LED rather than a signal mark, which is a distinction a reader counting colour usage in this ledger must hold. G6 holds for the page's own layer, and the only lettering is the plug label and the product's diegetic display and manual cover. The manual's own small print reads 'This product is a non-medical device used for family and personal beauty only', which is a disclaimer the page carries in a photograph rather than in its copy. This frame opens an eight-tile run on this page and is the first of a two-colourway by four-plug matrix, which is recorded in full on img-10. Strong: the contents answer the one question an imported mains appliance raises. Weak: the plug icon is the only element carrying information and it is the smallest thing in the frame.

The same with-contents knockout as img-03 with the wand in black and gold rather than white and gold. Adapter, cable, manual, plug icon and the 'AU PLUG 100 - 240V' label are identical, as is the layout, the light and the crop. Colorway is named in vocabulary.parameters as a runtime value that must never become identity, so this is absorption-ladder level one and the verdict is a match adding no type evidence. Job is identity; device is pack; setting is knockout. Register is commercial knockout product photography. Ground is white. G3 is not engaged, the blue head ring being the product's own LED. G6 holds for the page's layer. This is tile two of the page's eight-tile plug-and-colourway matrix. What is worth recording at this point rather than at the end of the run is that the variable is not one dimension but two, colour and plug territory, and that the page has chosen to spend a gallery slot on every cell of the product rather than on any of the arguments the rest of its tiles make. Strong: the black body reads the gold detailing better than the white one does. Weak: a buyer who has seen img-03 learns only a colour, and this is the first of six such tiles.

The with-contents knockout again, white colourway, with the plug icon and label changed to 'EU PLUG 100 - 240V'. Everything else in the frame is identical to img-03 including the adapter photographed, which is the same European two-pin unit shown in every tile of this run regardless of which plug the label names. That mismatch is the most useful thing in the frame: the label is the variable, the photograph is not, so five of the eight tiles show a buyer an adapter that does not match the territory the tile is sold as. Under G1 that would be a failure of reference consistency; as a corpus observation it is a page shipping a text swap where it needed an asset swap. Job is identity; device is pack; setting is knockout. Register is commercial knockout product photography. Ground is white. G3 is not engaged. G6 holds for the page's layer. Absorption-ladder level one: plug territory is a shipping parameter and not an argument, so the verdict is a match. Strong: naming the voltage range answers a real doubt about an imported appliance. Weak: the photograph contradicts the label in five of eight tiles, and a buyer in the UK looking at img-07 sees a European plug.

The with-contents knockout, black colourway, EU plug label. Tile four of eight in the matrix and the second cell of the EU row. Layout, contents, light, crop and the photographed adapter are unchanged from img-05; only the product body colour differs. Absorption-ladder level one on colorway, verdict match, no type evidence added. Job is identity; device is pack; setting is knockout. Register is commercial knockout product photography on white. Ground is white. G3 is not engaged; the head's blue ring is the product's own indicator. G6 holds for the page's own layer. The count is the point of recording these at all: by this tile the page has spent four gallery slots on one argument, and it will spend four more. For a library that legislates one type once per page, a source page that ships the same type eight times with two runtime variables is the clearest possible statement that the identity family on a direct-response product page is a SET rather than a frame, and that the existing type describes one member of it. Strong: internal consistency across the matrix is total, which is what makes it legible as a matrix at all. Weak: eight slots is a third of a typical gallery spent on a question answered by the first tile.

The with-contents knockout, white colourway, 'UK PLUG 100 - 240V'. The plug ICON is redrawn correctly as a three-pin British outline, but the adapter PHOTOGRAPHED beside it is still the European two-pin unit, which is the mismatch first recorded on img-05 and now confirmed as systematic rather than accidental. Tile five of eight. Job is identity; device is pack; setting is knockout. Register is commercial knockout product photography. Ground is white. G3 is not engaged. G6 holds for the page's own layer, and the only text is the plug label plus the product's diegetic display and the manual cover. Absorption-ladder level one: plug territory is a shipping parameter. The observation this tile adds over the earlier four is that the page maintains TWO representations of the same fact at different fidelities, a redrawn icon that tracks the variable and a photograph that does not, which is the kind of internal contradiction a generated frame would be graded a fail for and which a real page ships without comment. Strong: the icon set is clean and legible at tile size. Weak: the contradiction, and the fact that it appears in the tile a British buyer is most likely to open.

The with-contents knockout, black colourway, UK plug label, European adapter photographed. Tile six of eight. Identical in every structural respect to img-07 but for the product's body colour, which is absorption-ladder level one. Job is identity; device is pack; setting is knockout. Register is commercial knockout product photography on white. Ground is white, at the top of the corpus distribution. G3 is not engaged. G6 holds for the page's layer. Recorded rather than skipped because the runbook requires one record per batch image and because the instance count is the finding: the ledger needs to be able to show, later, that one source page spent eight of twenty-one frames on a single argument with two runtime variables. That count is what will decide whether 03-spec-lineup is worth promoting, since a lineup exists precisely to put a variable matrix into one frame instead of one slot per cell. Strong: nothing new. Weak: nothing new, which is the point.

The with-contents knockout, white colourway, 'US PLUG 100 - 240V', with a redrawn two-flat-pin American icon and the same European adapter photographed. Tile seven of eight. Job is identity; device is pack; setting is knockout. Register is commercial knockout product photography. Ground is white. G3 is not engaged; G6 holds for the page's own layer. Absorption-ladder level one on plug territory. The four plug territories observed across this run are AU, EU, UK and US, each in two colourways, which is a complete two-by-four matrix with no cell missing — and completeness is itself evidence, because it shows the page treating the matrix as a specification to be exhausted rather than as a set of alternatives to be compared. That is the opposite of what a lineup frame does, which is to put the alternatives beside each other so a buyer can choose. Strong: the matrix is complete and internally consistent. Weak: a buyer cannot compare the two colourways in any single frame on this page, which is the one thing eight tiles of colourway variation might have been expected to deliver.

The last tile of the run: with-contents knockout, black colourway, US plug label, European adapter photographed. This closes a complete two-colourway by four-plug-territory matrix occupying img-03 through img-10, EIGHT of this page's twenty-one frames. Job is identity; device is pack; setting is knockout. Register is commercial knockout product photography on white. Ground is white. G3 is not engaged. G6 holds for the page's layer. Absorption-ladder level one on both variables: colorway is named in vocabulary.parameters and plug territory is a shipping parameter, so all eight file as one argument and seven of them add no type evidence. The three findings this run produces are worth stating once, here. First, on a direct-response product page the identity family is a SET of angles, states and shipping variants rather than the single frame the type as drafted legislates. Second, the page maintains a redrawn plug ICON that tracks the variable beside a photographed ADAPTER that does not, so five of eight tiles contradict themselves. Third, this is the most extreme instance in four batches of the colourway-repetition pattern, which is the argument 03-spec-lineup exists to answer. Strong: completeness. Weak: eight slots, one fact.

deviations.observed: three circular state insets are added showing the treatment head lit in each of its LED colours

breakdown: A warm beige tile. A headline 'Ultrasonic RF Device' with a modality subline 'HIFU + RF + Micro Current + Vibration + LED'. The left half is a woman holding the wand to her cheek with two white contour swooshes drawn along her jaw; the right half is a large knockout of the wand with its display lit; three circular insets across the lower left show the treatment head lit red, green and blue. The base construction is the page-hero form raised on capix-mat in batch A — a photographic scene carrying a baked headline that makes a spec claim — and the one structural decision here is the row of state insets, which show a variable of the product rather than magnifying a part. Job is spec: the subline is a capability list. Register mixes lifestyle photography, knockout product photography and three product insets in one frame. Ground is warm beige, light and low in saturation, inside the corpus's ordinary two thirds. G3 appears engaged and is not: the red, green and blue are the product's own LED modes, not signal marks, and a reader counting colour usage in this ledger must hold that distinction or miscount this page badly. What IS a mark is the pair of white contour swooshes on the model's jaw, which assert a lifting effect the photograph does not show — A2 read exactly: a mark states, it cannot suppose. Strong: the three insets answer 'what are the lights for' before a buyer asks. Weak: the swooshes are the strongest claim on the tile and the only one with nothing behind it.

A headline '10min Beauty Treatment / Makes the skin more radiant' over a lifestyle photograph of a woman using the wand along her jaw. Set into the upper left is a rectangular inset split down the middle, the left half showing a face with visible texture and under-eye shadow and the right half the same face smoother and brighter, captioned 'Before use' and 'After use' in two tabs. The argument is the outcome state and the device carrying it is the before-and-after pair, which this registry has no id for. Job is relief. It is proposed as a new cluster rather than filed against the locked-frame type because the pair here is an INSET inside a lifestyle frame rather than the whole frame, and because the existing type is a proof job. Every argument fault this library owns about comparisons lands on it at once: A6 asks that a comparison be of a SWITCHABLE state and a ten-minute skin treatment is not switchable; A7 says a difference below roughly two to one cannot be drawn, and the difference here is drawn rather than photographed; A8 says a change of state needs a boundary rather than two states side by side. Register is commercial lifestyle photography with a retouched inset pair. Ground is warm beige. G3 is not engaged. Strong: the inset is small and subordinate, so the tile does not rest its whole weight on it. Weak: the claim is unsubstantiable by construction, and a ten-minute timeframe attached to a skin-texture change is the most aggressive figure on the page.

A tile headed 'How To Use' over six photographic panels in a three-by-two grid, each carrying a numbered disc and a caption: connect the power, clean face and apply gel, long press to turn on, select the mode and gear, follow the arrows and press on the circles, slide along the arrow line to massage. A note bar closes the tile: 'Be sure to gel/essence on face before use, otherwise you will not feel the effect'. This is the labelled variant of the sequence type and the THIRD distinct source for it in this drop after capix-mat and fosen-ring, which puts that variant well past the evidence threshold. The order is carried by numerals and captions rather than by arrows between panels, which is the distinction ADR-066 drew when it added the variant. Panels five and six carry treatment-path marks drawn on the model's face, circles and dotted arrows, which are marks inside a sequence panel and are not something the type currently legislates. Job is use; device is sequence. Register is close product photography for panels one, three and four and lifestyle photography for two, five and six. Ground is a pale warm tint behind white cells. G15 is satisfied, a three-by-two packing a square. G1 binds across six panels and holds. Strong: the note bar carries the one instruction that makes the rest work. Weak: the treatment-path marks in panels five and six are doing the job of a seventh and eighth panel inside two cells.

deviations.observed: a magnified sub-diagram of the display carries its own second tier of four labels, so the tile is a callout nested inside a callout

breakdown: The wand shown large on white with EIGHT labels around it on dashed right-angled leaders: EMS & RF Area, Ultrasonic Hole, Function Indicator with its three light meanings, Power Button with its press behaviours, Gear plus, Function Mode Button, Gear minus, Power Port. At the right a magnified rectangular inset of the display carries FOUR further labels of its own — Timing display, Vibration symbol, Gear display, Function display — each on its own dashed leader. This is the callout construction and the dashed leader is one of its three legislated joining forms, but two things exceed what the type has measured. The label count is twelve against a legislated band of three to six and a tested ceiling of eight. And the magnified inset carries its own leader tree, where the type legislates at most one magnified circle joined by a taper and says nothing about a second tier of labels inside it. The nesting is recorded as the one structural decision. Job is spec. Register is knockout product photography with flat vector leaders. Ground is white. G3 appears engaged and is not: the label 'Blue Light: HIFU / Red Light: RF / Green Light: EMS' names the product's own indicator code, which collides with this library's meanings for red and green without being a signal at all. Strong: twelve labels and every one points at something visible. Weak: twelve labels.

deviations.observed: a specification table and a contents list are appended below the dimensioned object, fusing the dimension tile and the table tile into one frame

breakdown: The upper two thirds show the wand at an angle with five dimension lines around it — 5cm/2.0in and 4.7cm/1.9in across the head, 16.8cm/6.6in down the body, 3cm/1.2in and 3.5cm/1.4in across the base. The lower third is a pale panel carrying two columns: 'Specification' with ten label-and-value lines from item type through HIFU frequency, RF temperature and timing, and 'Product Include' with four lines. This is the FOURTH distinct source for the dimension proposal, and it is the first frame in four batches where the dimension device and the table device appear FUSED rather than as separate tiles. That is the most useful thing in the frame for curation: two proposals kept apart across three sources are shipped here as two zones of one tile, which is evidence either that they are one type with two zones or that they are two types that commonly pair, and the distinction matters because the absorption ladder settles it. Job is spec. Register is knockout product photography above flat typography. Ground is white above a pale pink panel. G3 is not engaged. Every figure is a physical specification checkable against the unit or its manual, the A15-benign class, with the RF temperature of 43C being the one that also appears as a claim inside a mechanism frame on img-22 where nothing substantiates it. Strong: dimensions, specification and contents in one tile is the whole factual answer. Weak: fourteen lines of small type below a dimensioned object is two tiles' worth of reading in one slot.

A headline 'HIFU Face Lifting Machine' at the upper left over a bulleted stack of five modality claims — HIFU, RF, EMS, Vibration, Blue/Red/Green Light — with a lifestyle photograph of a woman holding the wand to her jaw filling the right two thirds, and three circular insets across the lower right showing the head lit red, green and blue. This is the claim-stack construction with a spec job, a subject holding one side and a headline with short claim lines filling the other, and it is the THIRD distinct source for that proposal after clou-diaxi and fosen-ring. Three sources is the count SPEC 6.2 sets as its evidence threshold, so the proposal is now past it and the open question is no longer whether it exists but whether it merges with the nine-source relief-job claimstack under one id or stands beside it under SPEC 3.1. Job is spec. Register mixes lifestyle photography with three product insets. Ground is warm beige, light and low in saturation. G3 appears engaged and is not, the three colours being the product's own LED modes. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. Strong: five claims as bare nouns with no verbs is the tightest claim stack in four batches. Weak: 'Blue/Red/Green Light' is a feature name rather than a claim, and it is the only one of the five a buyer cannot act on.

A headline 'RF import' with a two-line support sentence claiming four RF contacts reach the dermis layer and stimulate collagen regeneration. The frame below is a macro of the wand's treatment head glowing red, meeting a rendered cross-section of skin and dermis lit orange from within, with '43C/109.4F' set large into the tissue. This is the contact device raised on fosen-ring in batch C — the product at the boundary with a rendered tissue section — and it is the SECOND distinct source for it. Job is mechanism. Register is product photography composited onto a technical render. Ground is pale pink outside the panel. G3 is engaged and the collision is the finding: red and orange carry the heat here, and G3 assigns orange to WRONG heat and red to pain or a broken state, while the heat in this frame is the working mechanism the product is sold on. That is the second such collision in two batches, after fosen-ring drew red upward arrows to denote support. Two independent sources using a signal colour against its assigned meaning, for the correct function rather than the faulty one, is now a pattern rather than an error, and it is the strongest evidence this drop has produced that G3's lock does not match the market for heat and for lift. The temperature figure is substantiated elsewhere on the page, in img-19's specification table, and nowhere in this frame. Strong: the glow makes an invisible action locatable. Weak: collagen regeneration is asserted by an illustration.

A headline 'HIFU 1.8MHz Ultrasonic' with a support sentence about reaching the SMAS fascia layer. The wand's head sits over a rendered cross-section of facial tissue with cyan beams penetrating downward through the layers, two depth labels in rounded tabs reading '4.0mm' and '4.5mm' joined by a brown arrow, and a circular inset at the upper right showing the head emitting mist, captioned 'Ultrasonic nano atomization'. Third contact-device frame on this page and the second on this source. Job is mechanism. The depth labels put this squarely under A13, which this library wrote about exactly this construction: how deep the cut goes is a claim about how far the product reaches, and a rendered depth is a claim a render cannot substantiate. Register is product photography composited onto a technical render, with a second photographic inset. Ground is pale pink. G3 is obeyed here where img-22 breaches it: the beams are cyan, and cyan is what the rule assigns to a working mechanism. The same page therefore uses a signal colour correctly for ultrasound and incorrectly for heat, which sharpens the finding rather than weakening it — the market reaches for the colour of the PHENOMENON, blue for sound and red for warmth, not for the colour of the verdict. Strong: the beam geometry makes the depth claim legible without a paragraph. Weak: two depth figures half a millimetre apart is a precision the render cannot carry.

deviations.observed: a glowing contour line is drawn along the subject's jaw to assert the outcome the tile claims

breakdown: A lifestyle portrait filling the frame: a woman holding the black wand to her jaw with its head lit green, a bright green glowing line traced along her jawline from chin to ear, and a rounded caption panel across the foot reading 'V-Face Lift' with a three-line support sentence about activating deep muscles and achieving a three-dimensional V-shaped face. Job is relief, the state after buying, and the frame files against the relief hero type with one structural decision recorded: a mark drawn on the subject's body that asserts the outcome. That mark is the whole argument and it is the fault A2 names — a mark states, it cannot suppose — because the photograph shows a jawline and the line claims the jawline has been changed. A4 is satisfied, the mark lands where the claim is made; A2 is not. G3 is engaged and breached: green is reserved for a confirmation badge only, and here it is an effect contour. Register is commercial lifestyle photography with a flat graphic caption panel. Ground is warm beige. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. G9 is relevant and obeyed by accident: the subject's expression is neutral rather than performed, so the frame does not ask a face to carry evidence. Strong: the caption is the clearest statement of benefit on the page. Weak: the green line is the strongest claim in the batch with the least behind it, and it sits on a model whose jaw was that shape before the device touched it.

A headline 'High-frequency Vibration / 8000-10000 times/min' with a support sentence about opening the skin channel so skincare products penetrate. The wand's head, ring lit blue, sits over a rendered skin cross-section with concentric wave lines spreading through it, golden droplets rising among them labelled 'Nutrients' on a dashed leader, and two brown arrows at the left and right edges labelled 'Metabolites' pointing upward and out. Fourth contact-device frame on this page and the third on this source, which makes the contact construction this page's single commonest mechanism tile. Job is mechanism. Register is product photography composited onto a technical render with flat vector marks. Ground is pale pink. G3 is engaged twice and obeyed once: the blue ring is the product's own LED rather than a mark, and the brown arrows carry direction rather than state, which is a colour the rule does not govern. The frame's argument is a two-way exchange — nutrients in, metabolites out — asserted entirely by arrow direction, which is A10's territory: direction words belong to the structure rather than to the frame, and here the structure is a render nobody can check. The vibration figure is substantiated in img-19's specification table and not here. Strong: two marks, two directions, one idea, and the reading is instant. Weak: 'Metabolites' leaving the skin because a wand vibrates is the least supportable claim on a page that makes several.

deviations.observed: each claim line carries a macro photograph of the state it names, so the stack is half text and half evidence

breakdown: A headline 'Colourful nursing' with a support line about four fixed LED wavelengths. The left half is a lifestyle portrait of a woman holding the wand to her cheek. The right half is three stacked cards, each split: a label side naming a mode and its light — 'RF / Red Light (625nm)', 'HIFU / Blue Light (413nm)', 'Micro Current / Green Light (532nm)' — and a photograph side showing the treatment head actually lit in that colour. This is the claim-stack construction with one structural decision: every claim line is paired with a macro photograph of the thing it names, so the stack stops being assertion and becomes a small proof set. That is a genuinely different construction from the four-icon stacks observed on clou-diaxi and fosen-ring, where the icons were drawn rather than photographed and carried no evidence at all. Job is spec. Register mixes lifestyle photography with three macro product photographs and flat typography. Ground is warm beige. G3 appears engaged and is not: red, blue and green are the product's own wavelengths, named in nanometres, which is the clearest instance in four batches of a product's colours being mistaken for signal colours by anyone counting. Strong: a photograph beside each claim is the cheapest substantiation available to a page, and this tile is the only one here that takes it. Weak: three wavelengths in nanometres is a precision no buyer can act on.

A headline 'Do you have the following skin problems?' over a central portrait of a smiling woman holding the wand to her cheek, RINGED by eight circular vignettes, each a photograph of a different complaint with a small label bar: Puffy eyes, Dark circles, Wrinkle, Sagging skin, Dull skin, Acne, Large pores, Frown lines. There are no leader lines at all; each vignette simply sits nearest the part of the face it concerns. This is the halo-or-callout device with a SYMPTOM job, which ADR-066 renamed from 02-symptom-halo to 02-symptom-callout, recorded at two sources, and said in as many words 'gets no file until it has three'. This is the third. The ring form with no leaders is one of the three joining parameters that ADR-066 legislated on the feicemat frame, so the construction needs no new grammar. Job is symptom; the tile widens a problem across complaints rather than naming one pain. Register is commercial lifestyle photography at the centre with eight stock macro vignettes around it. Ground is warm beige. G3 is not engaged; no signal colour is used. G11 is NOT used, and its absence is notable: clou-diaxi's symptom rails desaturated everything but the afflicted area, and this page leaves all eight vignettes in full colour, so the locating work is done by the crop alone. Strong: eight complaints in one glance, each one a real photograph rather than an illustration. Weak: the central model is smiling and unafflicted, so the tile's own subject contradicts its headline.

The same construction as img-11 with the wand in black rather than white: headline 'Ultrasonic RF Device', modality subline 'HIFU + RF + Micro Current + Vibration + LED', a woman holding the device to her cheek with two white contour swooshes along her jaw, a large knockout of the wand at the right, and three circular insets showing the head lit red, green and blue. Colorway is absorption-ladder level one, so the verdict is a match adding no type evidence. Job is spec. Register mixes lifestyle photography, knockout product photography and product insets. Ground is warm beige, light and low in saturation. G3 appears engaged and is not, the three inset colours being the product's own LED modes. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. The contour swooshes are present here exactly as in img-11 and carry the same A2 fault: a mark that supposes a lift rather than stating a fact. Counting this frame with img-11 and with the eight-tile plug matrix, this source page ships TEN of its twenty-one frames as colourway or shipping-variant repeats of four underlying arguments, which is the highest repetition rate in four batches and the clearest single number this drop has produced about how a direct-response product gallery actually spends its slots. Strong: the black body reads the gold and the LED colours better. Weak: nothing here that img-11 did not already say.

A memory-foam bath mat photographed from above in a pale room, two bare feet standing on it and a clear footprint depression pressed into the surface beside them. A black headline across the top reads 'Soft And Resilient Not Easily Collapsed' and two grey support lines sit at the lower right, 'Long Lasting Support' and 'Slow Rebound Kernel'. This is the page-hero construction raised on capix-mat in batch A — one photographic scene carrying a baked headline that makes a spec claim — and it is the THIRD distinct source for that proposal after capix-mat and glowy-liff. Job is spec: the claim is about what the foam does under load. What makes the frame unusually strong is that the evidence is IN it: the depression is the product's own response, visible and locatable, so the headline is demonstrated rather than asserted. That is G9 satisfied in a register where G9 is not usually engaged, and A3 satisfied without a single mark. Register is commercial lifestyle photography, soft daylight from the upper left, no studio key. Ground is a pale near-white room, light and low in saturation, inside the corpus's ordinary two thirds. G3 is not engaged. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. Strong: a physical impression is the cheapest proof a foam product can offer and this page takes it in almost every frame. Weak: the two support lines are set in low-contrast grey over a light floor and are the first thing lost at tile size.

A white tile carrying a flat grey rounded rectangle that stands in for the mat, with three dimension labels set against its edges: '60Cm' across the top, '40Cm' down the left, '0.6Cm Thick' at the right. Below it three lines of black type: 'Manual Measurement May Result In An Error Of 1-3 Cm / This Will Not Affect Usage / Please Do Not Purchase If You Mind'. This is the FIFTH distinct source for the dimension proposal — capix-mat, clou-diaxi, fosen-ring, glowy-liff and now this — which clears SPEC 6.3's criterion 1 bar of five distinct sources. It also shows the device at its most abstract: the object here is a DIAGRAM rather than a photograph, so the type's subject slot takes a drawn stand-in as well as a product shot. The three-line disclaimer is the most valuable thing in this batch for the substantiation question A15 leaves open. The page states the TOLERANCE of its own measurement inside the frame that carries it — an error band, a statement that the band does not affect use, and an instruction to buy elsewhere if it does. That is the honest behaviour A15 asks for, appearing in the wild, and it is the first instance of it in five batches. Job is spec. Register is flat vector graphic. Ground is white. G3 is not engaged. Strong: a declared tolerance is worth more than a decimal place. Weak: the object is so abstracted that it teaches nothing about the product except its outline.

deviations.observed: a circular anatomical inset is composited over the photograph, showing a foot skeleton with pressure arrows and a cushioning layer

breakdown: Bare feet on the grey mat with a footprint depression, and a circular inset at the upper right holding a rendered foot skeleton in side view with red arrows pressing down into a cyan cushioning band over a honeycomb layer. A pale caption panel across the lower right reads 'Cushion & Soft / Walking on the clouds'. The base is the page-hero construction and the one structural decision is the anatomical inset, which moves the argument from what the surface does to what the foot experiences. Job is spec. This frame is the clearest G3-COMPLIANT use of signal colour in five batches and is worth setting against the breaches recorded on fosen-ring and glowy-liff: red carries the downward pressure, which is the wrong or harmful force, and cyan carries the cushioning layer, which is the correct support. Both match the rule's assignments exactly. That matters because two other sources in this drop used red for support and red for therapeutic heat, so the market is not uniformly against G3 — it is against G3 for HEAT and for LIFT, and with it for PRESSURE. Register mixes lifestyle photography with a technical render inset. Ground is a pale room, light and near-neutral. G6 is broken by the caption panel. Strong: the inset explains the depression the photograph already shows. Weak: the inset's honeycomb layer is not a feature of this product, so the render illustrates a generic insole rather than this mat.

The mat laid in a cream-toned entryway beside a pair of white trainers and two pairs of slippers, a footprint depression visible in its surface, sunlight falling across the floor. A black headline reads 'Entering The Entranc Step Firmly / Onto The Shoe-Changing Platform' and a brown support line beneath it reads 'Non-Slipbottom To Reduce Sliding Back And Forth'. Same construction as img-03: one photographic scene with a baked headline making a spec claim, so it files as a match rather than a second decision. Job is spec, with the claim being the non-slip backing. Environment is a parameter, and the shift from bathroom to entryway is the page making a placement argument rather than a new type. Two lettering faults are worth recording because this library counts lettering across every frame it sees: 'Entranc' is missing its final letter and 'Non-Slipbottom' has lost its word space. Both are in a real market page rather than a render, which is a useful counterweight to the render ledger's perfect run — human pages misspell too, and at a rate this drop can now begin to measure. Register is commercial lifestyle photography, warm daylight. Ground is a cream floor, light and low in saturation. G3 is not engaged. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. Strong: the slippers and trainers give the mat a reason to be in that doorway. Weak: the depression is in shadow and reads as a stain rather than as an impression.

A knockout on white: the mat seen in perspective with two bare feet mid-step onto it, the forward foot already sunk into a fresh depression and the rear foot lifting off the floor behind. There is no text anywhere in the frame, no room, no props and no ground beyond a faint contact shadow. The argument is carried entirely by the ACTION — a foot pressing and the surface yielding — which is the close-range demonstration device the vocabulary reserves as `demo` and which the ledger carries from capix-mat in batch A. This is the SECOND distinct source for that proposal. Job is use rather than spec, because the frame teaches what happens when you step on it rather than naming a property of the foam. Register is commercial knockout product photography with a live subject, broad even light, no studio key. Ground is white, at the top of the corpus value distribution. G3 is not engaged. G6 holds: not a single word appears, which makes this one of very few frames in five batches carrying no text layer at all. G1 would bind hard, since the depression is the whole argument and a redesigned surface makes it false. Strong: a wordless frame that still says exactly one thing, which is what the owner's message law asks of every tile. Weak: the mid-step pose is ambiguous enough that the rear foot reads as floating.

deviations.observed: a four-chip claim rail is added below the photograph, so the tile carries a headline and a claim set rather than a headline and a support line

breakdown: A headline bar across the top reads 'Soft To The Touch Dry And Non-Slip'. Below it bare feet stand on the mat with two clear depressions. Across the foot of the frame runs a rail of four alternating light and white chips, each carrying one claim: Slow Rebound, Absorb Water, Anti-Slip, Comfortable. The base is the page-hero construction and the one structural decision is the claim rail, which distinguishes this from the claim-stack construction seen on clou-diaxi and fosen-ring: a stack puts the subject on one side and the words on the other, while a rail runs the claims along an edge and lets the photograph keep the whole frame. Both are now observed and the difference is a layout decision rather than a job change, which is what makes it a variant. Job is spec. Register is commercial lifestyle photography on a pale ground. G3 is not engaged. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. This frame is duplicated byte-for-byte elsewhere in the drop as img-09, the only true byte-identical pair in 157 files; the ledger is keyed on hash so the second copy adds no record, which is the append-only design working as intended. Strong: four claims in four words each, along an edge, costing the photograph nothing. Weak: 'Comfortable' is the fourth chip and says nothing the other three have not.

Two hands lift the folded mat in front of an open washing-machine drum, a pale leaf-patterned band down the left edge, and a translucent teal panel at the upper left carrying 'Machine Wash on Cold' with a support line 'Tumble dry on low. Colors won't fade'. The construction is the page-hero form — one photographic scene with a baked headline — but the JOB is use rather than spec: the tile teaches care and operation rather than naming a property. Under SPEC 3.1 two jobs are two types however alike the picture, which is the same reasoning that separated 03-spec-claimstack from the relief-job claimstack in batch B, so this is filed as a third job sibling of the hero construction rather than merged into the spec one. Whether the family should instead be collapsed into one device-led type with a job parameter is exactly the question the curation pass exists to settle, and three job variants across five sources is the evidence it will settle on. Job is use. Register is commercial lifestyle photography with a flat graphic panel and a decorative vector border. Ground is a pale laundry interior, light and low in saturation. G3 is not engaged; the teal panel is brand rather than signal. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. Strong: showing the mat mid-load answers the washability claim in the same gesture that states it. Weak: the decorative leaf border is the only ornamental element on the whole page and reads as a different designer.

The mat laid on a dark tiled bathroom floor beside a black marble step, folded white towels on a lit shelf behind, a bare foot pressing into the surface and leaving a depression while the other foot rests on the step. No text anywhere in the frame. Same demonstration device as img-07 with the environment changed from a white knockout to a real bathroom, and environment is named in vocabulary.parameters as a runtime value, so the verdict is a match. Job is use. What the change of setting buys is the one thing the knockout cannot give: a reason for the mat to be where it is, and a floor surface the non-slip claim can be judged against. Register is commercial lifestyle photography, warm shelf light against cool daylight, shallow depth. Ground is a dark tiled floor, which is the darker third of the corpus distribution and is earned here because a grey mat on a pale floor would have no edge. G3 is not engaged. G6 holds, no words appear. G1 would bind on the depression. This is the second wordless frame on this page, and on a page whose other eleven tiles all carry baked text that is a deliberate rhythm rather than an oversight. Strong: the depression reads more clearly against the dark floor than in any other frame on the page. Weak: the crop puts the standing foot half out of frame, so the step's role is unreadable at tile size.

The mat photographed on a pale ground with one corner folded back to reveal the textured rubberised underside, faint footprint depressions visible in the upper face. A black headline reads 'Non-Slip Bottom Stable And Unmovable' and a white circular icon badge at the right shows a foot with a slip arrow beneath it. Same page-hero construction, job spec, so this files as a match. The move worth recording is the FOLD: the frame argues a property of a face the product never presents in use, and it does so by physically turning the object rather than by an inset or a cutaway. That is the cheapest possible way to show a hidden surface and this library has no device name for it — the closest are the explode device, which separates components, and the macro device, which magnifies one. A fold is neither; it is the object demonstrating its own other side. Register is commercial product photography, soft even light, no studio key. Ground is a pale near-white surface.
