G3 is not engaged. G6 is broken by the headline and the icon badge. The badge is the page's only mark and it is a line-drawn glyph in a white disc, which is one of the badge forms G16 lists. Strong: the fold shows the claim rather than stating it. Weak: the underside texture is dark on dark and reads as a shadow at tile size.

Two panels side by side with a hard divide. The left is headed 'Ordinary Floor Mats' and shows bare feet on a thin mat that has rucked into deep folds under the toes; the right is headed 'Slow Rebound Comfortable Floor Mat' and shows the same feet on this product, flat, with one clean depression. Each panel carries a small circular anatomical inset at its lower right, the left showing an unsupported foot skeleton and the right the same skeleton over a cushioning layer. This is the two-panel comparison device exactly as the type defines it, and it is the SECOND source for that type in this drop after capix-mat carried it as a variant in batch A. Job is spec. G5 is satisfied: both sides are photographic, no register mismatch, which is the rule's whole concern. G4 is satisfied weakly — the right panel's header is lighter and its floor brighter, but the two photographs are close enough in exposure that the correct side is not obviously the airier one. A6 is satisfied properly: the comparison is of a switchable state, since removing this mat and substituting a thin one really does produce the rucking shown. Register is commercial lifestyle photography throughout. Ground is a pale room in both panels. Strong: the rucked fold is a real failure mode a buyer recognises, not a strawman. Weak: the two insets are too small to read and repeat an argument img-05 already made better.

The same bathroom demonstration as img-11 with the mat in black rather than grey: dark tiled floor, black marble step, folded white towels on the lit shelf, a bare foot pressing a depression into the surface, no text. Colorway is named in vocabulary.parameters as a runtime value that must never become identity, so this is absorption-ladder level one and the verdict is a match adding no type evidence. Job is use; device is the close demonstration. Register is commercial lifestyle photography, identical light and camera to img-11. Ground is a dark tiled floor. G3 is not engaged. G6 holds, no words appear. The colourway repetition pattern now stands at FOUR sources out of five in this drop — capix-mat spent three slots on one specification card, clou-diaxi two on one claim stack, fosen-ring two on one identity composite, glowy-liff eight on a two-by-four matrix, and this page two on one demonstration. That is not an occasional habit; it is how a direct-response product gallery spends its slots, and it is the single most consistent finding across five batches. Strong: the black mat against the dark floor reads the depression better than the grey one does. Weak: a buyer who has seen img-11 learns only a colour.

deviations.observed: a three-chip claim rail is set into the upper corner of the scene, so the tile carries a felt-state headline and a spec claim set at once

breakdown: A woman in a cream bathrobe steps out of a glass shower enclosure onto the grey mat, backlit by a bright window, with a headline 'Bathroom Entrance/Exit / Stay Dry And Confident' and a brown support couplet 'Absorbs Water Faster Making / The Bottom Of Your Feet More Placid'. Three diamond-marked chips run down the upper right: Absorb Moisture, Anti-Slip, Soft. Job is relief: the headline names a felt state rather than a property, which is what separates this from the page's spec-hero tiles even though the construction is the same. The one structural decision is the claim rail, the same addition recorded on img-08 but attached to a relief job rather than a spec one, which is exactly the evidence the curation pass needs to decide whether the hero family is one device with a job parameter or three types. Register is commercial lifestyle photography, strong backlight, warm grade. Ground is a pale bathroom, light and low in saturation. G3 is not engaged. G9 is relevant and obeyed: the subject's face is out of frame entirely, so no expression is asked to carry evidence, and the argument rests on the situation instead. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. Strong: cropping the head out is a deliberate and unusual choice that keeps the tile about the floor. Weak: 'More Placid' is a translation artefact in the one line meant to carry the feeling.

deviations.observed: the product is composited into a METAPHORICAL environment, standing on cloud forms rather than in any real place

breakdown: The mat floats in a field of white cloud forms and pale silk ribbons, two bare feet standing on it with a depression pressed into the surface. A black headline reads 'The Feet Feel Soft Comfortable And Not Tired' with a support line 'The Feeling Of Being Wrapped Like Stepping On Clouds'. Job is relief. The one structural decision is the setting: this is not a room, a studio ground or a knockout but a METAPHOR, a place that does not exist, built to make the support line literal. No type in this registry legislates that and G7's context integrity would refuse it outright — the rule exists to keep a product in a place it could actually be. The corpus carrying it twice would make it a real gap; this is the first instance in five batches and it is recorded as such. Register is a composite of product photography and rendered cloud forms, which is a register mix G5 does not reach because there is no comparison in frame. Ground is near-white throughout, the lightest frame in the batch. G3 is not engaged. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. Strong: the metaphor and the copy say the same thing, so neither is decoration. Weak: the clouds sit BEHIND and AROUND the mat rather than under it, so the mat reads as floating on nothing and the softness claim loses the surface it needed.

A headline 'The Details Are Visible And The Texture Is More Solid' over the mat photographed in perspective on white, with three circular magnified insets arranged across it, each captioned beneath: 'Tightly Bound Edges: Not Easy To Curl' showing the bound corner, 'Moderate Thickness: Soft To The Touch' showing the folded edge in section, 'Fine Surface: Moisture-Absorbing And Comfortable' showing the pile at high magnification. This is the macro-paired-with-text variant in a THIRD layout after clou-diaxi checkerboard and fosen-ring bands, and the THIRD distinct source for it. The layout here is circles composited OVER the subject rather than cells beside it, and that produces the distinction worth recording: these satellites are MAGNIFIED VIEWS of the object, while a callout satellite is a LABEL naming a part. Both ring a central subject; only one of them shows you something the main frame cannot. That is a real discriminator between the macro family and the callout family and it has not been written down anywhere in this repo. Job is spec. Register is commercial product photography throughout, broad even light. Ground is white. G3 is not engaged. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. Strong: three magnifications of three genuinely different surfaces, none of them decorative. Weak: the captions sit below their circles and collide with the mat's own edge in two places.

A hand holds the hydrogen water bottle at the right against a snow-mountain background, the water lit blue and full of rising bubbles. The left half carries a headline '#1 Hydrogen Water Bottle' with a support couplet naming the brand, and three dark claim cards each with a line icon in a white disc: Hydrogen Enriched Water, Eco-Friendly Design, Boost Your Health. This is the claim-stack construction with a spec job and it is the FOURTH distinct source for that proposal after clou-diaxi, fosen-ring and glowy-liff. Job is spec. The bubbles are the product's visible output and under G8 they would be the subject of a mechanism frame; here they are the setting for a claim stack, which is the distinction between this type and the emanation proposal raised on clou-diaxi. Register is commercial product photography composited onto a stock landscape. Ground is a pale blue mountain scene, light and moderately saturated. G3 appears engaged and is not: the blue is the product's own illuminated water, not a signal mark. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. Two claims carry no substantiation of any kind — '#1' is a ranking with no source, and 'Boost Your Health' is a health claim — which is the page's pattern rather than this frame's fault. Strong: three claims, three icons, one photograph, read in a second. Weak: the mountain is a mood rather than a place the bottle would be, and it makes the composite visible.

A headline bar '5 Reasons Why' over a photograph of a man's hand steadying the bottle on a kitchen counter. Five white labelled pills ring the bottle — Hydrogen-Infusion Technology, Stainless Steel, USB Rechargeable, Durable Glass Body, Quick Charging — each sitting on a dashed circular ARC that runs behind all of them rather than on individual leaders. This files against the spec callout rather than the identity callout for exactly the reason that type's own trigger gives: the labels name PARTS and what they do, materials and capabilities, not what the object IS. That boundary was drafted on 2026-09-10 with no render behind it and this frame is the first corpus evidence that it holds. Job is spec. The joining form is worth recording as new: ADR-066 legislated three parameters — leader line, dashed leader, and nothing — and this is a fourth, a continuous dashed ARC connecting all satellites to each other rather than each to the object. Register is commercial lifestyle photography with flat graphic pills. Ground is a pale kitchen, light and low in saturation, well inside the corpus median. G3 is not engaged. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. Strong: five labels, all legible, none overlapping the subject. Weak: the arc joins the labels to each other and not to the parts, so nothing points at the glass body or the steel.

A headline 'The Magic of AliveBlue' over four outlined pills running down the left edge, each with a line icon and a short label: Hydrogen Water, Antioxidant Power, Eco-Friendly & Durable, One-Touch Use. A vertical dashed line with dots joins them in sequence. The bottle stands at the right against a pale blue water backdrop, bubbling. Second claim stack on this page and the same construction as img-03 with a different chrome, so it is a match rather than a second decision. Job is spec. The dotted connector between claims is the same joining idea as img-04's arc, applied to a vertical stack rather than a ring, which suggests the joining line is a page-level design habit rather than a property of either device. Register is commercial product photography composited onto a water-surface backdrop. Ground is pale blue, light and moderately saturated. G3 appears engaged and is not, the blue being the product's own water and light. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. 'Antioxidant Power' is the second health claim in three frames with nothing behind it. Strong: the one-touch claim is the only one on the page a buyer can verify from the photograph, and the button is visible in it. Weak: the headline names a brand rather than a benefit, which spends the largest type on the page on the thing a buyer cares least about.

A headline 'HydroCharge Technology' with a support sentence, a large soft '3 min' set with radiating tick marks at the left, and at the right a rendered exploded view of the bottle's base: a translucent membrane disc lifted clear, a dark mesh plate below it, a lit blue chamber beneath that, and the steel base holding them, with floating 'H' bubbles drifting between the layers. This is the exploded construction as the type defines it — the product separated into its real component groups along one axis in a technical render — and it is the SECOND distinct source for that type in this drop after capix-mat's fabric laminate in batch A. Job is spec. Register is a product render, not a photograph. Ground is a pale blue-white gradient, light and low in saturation. G3 is not engaged; the blue is the product's own indicator. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. 'HydroCharge Technology' is an invented trademarked technology name, which is the same device the clip-fan brief described as this category's habit — a coined capitalised name standing where a mechanism explanation would go. The three-minute figure is substantiated nowhere in the frame. Strong: the explode shows a stack a buyer cannot see through the glass, which is the one thing the rest of the page cannot do. Weak: the layers are rendered rather than photographed, so the count is a claim about construction that the render itself supplies.

deviations.observed: the proof is performed on a PROXY object rather than on the product or a body — three apple slices stand in for the effect being claimed

breakdown: A headline '6 Hours Antioxidant Experiment' over three labelled subjects on a pale water surface: an apple slice exposed to air, an apple slice in a glass of tap water, and an apple slice in a glass of hydrogen-rich water. The first two have browned heavily; the third is pale and fresh with its red skin intact. This is the locked-frame proof construction and it is the SECOND distinct source for the type in this drop after clou-diaxi's twin spray modes. The one structural decision is that the proof is performed on a PROXY: the product is not in the frame at all, and what is compared is the effect of its output on a third object over time. That is a genuinely different move from photographing the product twice and it is the cleanest way a page can make an invisible chemical claim visible. The fault is the one this type exists to catch. Its whole discipline is that exactly ONE variable changes, and here three DIFFERENT apple slices are shown — different shapes, different cut faces, and only the third with skin on it. So the frame's own control is broken: a reader cannot tell whether the third slice is fresher because of the water or because it was cut later. A6 is satisfied, the state is switchable; the single-variable rule is not. Strong: the idea. Weak: the execution, in the one respect that decides whether a proof is a proof.

A woman in gym kit with white earphones drinks from the bottle, a spin bike blurred behind her. A blue caption bar across the foot reads 'Anti-Aging Properties' with a support line 'Protects your skin & reduces signs of aging', and a circular line-icon badge showing a face sits at its right end. Job is relief: the headline names an outcome state rather than a property. Device is one photographic scene carrying a baked caption block, which is the relief hero construction, and this is the SECOND source in this drop for that form after gripi-mata. Register is commercial lifestyle photography, available gym light, warm skin tones. Ground is a blurred gym interior, mid in value and low in saturation. G3 is not engaged; the blue bar is brand. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. G9 is relevant: the subject's expression is neutral and the argument rests on the situation, so no face is asked to carry evidence. The claim is the problem — 'reduces signs of aging' is a cosmetic efficacy claim with no source, no timeframe and no measurement anywhere in the frame or on the page, and it is one of four such claims this page makes. Strong: the scene is ordinary and the product is being used rather than presented, which is what a relief frame should do. Weak: the badge icon is a face with sparkles and adds nothing the caption has not said.

A woman sits stretching on a blue yoga mat outdoors beside white trainers, the bottle standing upright on the mat in the foreground. A blue caption bar reads 'Post-Workout' with a support line 'Eases muscle fatigue by up to 30%', and a circular line-icon badge of a torso sits at its right end. Same construction as img-08 and a match on the relief hero form. Job is relief. The support line is the clearest A15 fault in six batches: a bare percentage, no source, no study, no n, no timeframe, and hedged with 'up to' so that any result satisfies it. A15's own measured degradation across seven corpus frames ran from a named survey with n=307 down to nothing; this sits at the bottom of that scale with an added qualifier that makes it unfalsifiable. Recorded in full because the three proposals blocked behind the substantiation rule need exactly this kind of example to legislate against. Register is commercial lifestyle photography, overcast daylight. Ground is a concrete path and blue mat, mid in value. G3 is not engaged. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. G9 is obeyed by accident: the subject's face is turned away entirely. Strong: the product stands where a real bottle would stand, upright on the mat within reach. Weak: the percentage.

deviations.observed: each claim line carries a circular photographic vignette of the outcome it names, so the stack is half text and half evidence

breakdown: A headline 'Benefits of Hydrogen Water' over four circular photographic vignettes in a two-by-two, each captioned beneath: Improves Sleep with a woman asleep, Better Skin Hydration with a woman touching her face, Anti-Aging Properties with an older woman at her temple, Helps with Weight Loss with a tape measure at a waist. The bottle stands at the right, bubbling. This is the FIRST frame in six batches to file against the nine-source relief claimstack proposal, and it matters: that type is the best-evidenced in the library and this drop had not touched it until now. The one structural decision is that each claim carries a photographic vignette rather than an icon or nothing, which is the SAME decision recorded on glowy-liff img-26 against the spec-job sibling. Two sources, two jobs, one decision — which makes 'claims carry photographs' a cross-job variant rather than a property of either type, and that is a real finding for the curation pass. Job is relief: all four claims name outcome states. Register is commercial product photography with four stock lifestyle vignettes. Ground is pale blue. G3 is not engaged. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. All four claims are health or cosmetic efficacy claims with no substantiation. Strong: a photograph beside each claim is the cheapest substantiation a page can offer. Weak: what the photographs substantiate is the FEELING, not the claim — a sleeping woman is not evidence that water improved her sleep.

deviations.observed: the two sides are fused into a single continuous silhouette, a crushed disposable bottle becoming the product across one hard vertical divider

breakdown: A headline 'MAKE A CHANGE' with a support sentence, and at the right a single vertical object split down the middle by a hard white line: the left half is a crushed blue plastic water bottle, the right half is this product, bubbling and lit. The two halves are scaled and aligned so they read as ONE object rather than as two panels, which is the structural decision recorded. That is a genuinely different move from the type's ordinary two-panel form and it does something the two-panel form cannot: it makes the comparison an act of substitution rather than a judgement between alternatives. Job is closer to cause than spec — the indicted thing is disposable plastic rather than a rival product feature — but the device is the split and the type is filed on the device. G5 is satisfied: both halves are photographic, no register mismatch. G4 is satisfied: the product half is brighter and cleaner than the crushed half. Register is commercial product photography composited on a water-texture ground. Ground is pale blue, light and moderately saturated. G3 is not engaged. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. The support line reads 'Say goodbye to plastic waist', a misspelling of waste, and is the second lettering error this drop has found in a real market page. Strong: one silhouette, two states, no explanation needed. Weak: the crushed bottle is a strawman — nobody compares a hydrogen generator to a crushed bottle.

A headline 'How to Use' over three horizontal bands, each pairing a photograph at the left with a heading and a short paragraph at the right: Fill it with Water, Press to Activate, Stay Hydrated. The order is carried by vertical position and by the captions themselves; there are no numerals and no arrows. That is the labelled variant exactly as ADR-066 defined it — a caption breaks the same clause a numeral does — and this is the FOURTH distinct source for that variant in this drop, after capix-mat, fosen-ring and glowy-liff. Four sources in one drop makes it the best-evidenced variant here. Job is use; device is sequence. At a square ratio three horizontal bands is STRIPING rather than packing, which G15 refuses for any type laying out more than one frame, and it is worth recording that three of this drop's four labelled sequences pack and this one does not. Register is commercial lifestyle photography for panels one and three and close product photography for panel two. Ground is a pale blue gradient behind white cells. G3 is not engaged. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. G1 would bind across three panels and holds. Strong: each panel shows a genuinely different action, and the middle one is a thumb on the button rather than a repeat of the first. Weak: three to four lines of body copy per band is far past anything this library has measured as legible at tile size.

deviations.observed: a circular label ring with a knockout product at its centre is composited over the grid's intersection, so the four cells are named by one overlay rather than by four captions

breakdown: Four photographic cells in a two-by-two — the bottle on a desk beside a laptop, on a bench beside a rucksack, in a car cup holder, and held by a woman mid-yoga-pose outdoors. Over the intersection sits a blue circular ring carrying four labels curved around it, DAILY HYDRATION, TRAVELING, ON THE GO, POST-WORKOUT, with a knockout of the bubbling product filling the ring's centre. The argument is that one unit serves many contexts, which is the grid type's purpose, and it is the THIRD distinct source for the type in this drop after fosen-ring's two frames. The one structural decision is the ring overlay: the type is defined as a photographic multi-cell collage with NO graphic overlays, and here a single large graphic names all four cells at once and carries a product layer besides. Job is use. G15 is satisfied, a two-by-two packing the square. Register is commercial lifestyle photography with a composited graphic ring and a knockout product. Ground varies by cell, all light to mid in value. G3 is not engaged. G6 is broken by the ring's labels. G1 binds across five product instances — four in cells plus the knockout — and holds. Strong: the ring solves a real problem, since four captions would have eaten four corners of four photographs. Weak: the ring covers the exact centre of all four images, which is where three of the four put their subject.

The same photograph as img-09 with the caption bar and badge removed: a woman stretching on a blue yoga mat outdoors, white trainers beside her, the bottle standing upright in the foreground. No words anywhere in the frame. This is the wordless context frame raised on capix-mat in batch A, where the product stood alone on a forest floor, and the binding feature is the same — the SITUATION is the argument and nothing is stated. What differs is that a person is present, and persona_cast is named in vocabulary.parameters as a runtime value, so cast does not change identity and the verdict is a match. That widening is worth recording, because the proposal as first written said 'no person' and one frame is not enough to legislate a cast rule. Job is relief. Register is commercial lifestyle photography, overcast daylight. Ground is a concrete path and a blue mat, mid in value and low in saturation. G3 is not engaged. G6 holds: not a word appears. The page shipping both the captioned and the uncaptioned version of one photograph is itself the finding — a gallery spends two slots on one image, once as an argument and once as atmosphere. Strong: without the percentage claim the frame is honest and still sells the situation. Weak: read alone it says only that a bottle exists near a yoga mat.

A man in a dark t-shirt stands at a kitchen counter holding the bottle with both hands, one on the steel lid and one cupping the base, in the act of opening or closing it. The background is a blurred pale kitchen. No text anywhere in the frame. The argument is carried by the ACTION and by the hands, which is the close demonstration device the vocabulary reserves as `demo`, and this is the THIRD distinct source for that proposal after capix-mat and gripi-mata. Job is use: the frame teaches how the thing is handled rather than naming a property. Register is commercial lifestyle photography, soft daylight, shallow depth so the hands and the lid are the only sharp elements. Ground is a pale kitchen, light and low in saturation, well inside the corpus median. G3 is not engaged. G6 holds, no words appear. G13 is not engaged, the subject is an adult and cropped at the neck. G1 would bind on the lid and the base, which are the two parts the hands are demonstrating. Three sources puts this proposal past SPEC 6.2's evidence threshold. Strong: two hands on two different parts of the object teaches the grip and the scale at once, and the crop keeps the face out so the tile stays about the product. Weak: the action is ambiguous — opening and closing look identical in a still — so the frame teaches handling without teaching a step.

The same photograph as img-08 with the caption bar and badge removed: a woman in gym kit with white earphones drinking from the bottle, a spin bike blurred behind her. No words. Second uncaptioned twin on this page, which confirms the pattern img-14 raised rather than leaving it a single observation: this gallery ships the clean plate AND the captioned version of the same photograph as two separate slots. Job is relief. Register is commercial lifestyle photography, available gym light. Ground is a blurred interior, mid in value and low in saturation. G3 is not engaged. G6 holds. G9 is relevant and obeyed: the subject's expression is neutral and the act of drinking carries the frame. What this pair lets the ledger measure, later, is whether the captioned or the uncaptioned version is picked more often when both are offered, which is exactly the kind of question feedback/picks.jsonl exists to answer and has no records for. Strong: the frame is ordinary in the way a real photograph is ordinary, and nothing in it is asserted. Weak: with the caption gone the tile carries no message at all, which is precisely the fault the owner named on 2026-09-11 about a wordless testimony render — and here a real market page ships it deliberately.

A third wordless lifestyle frame: a woman with a ponytail drinks from the bottle outdoors against blurred green foliage, holding the steel lid in her other hand. No text, no marks, no product layer. Third instance of the wordless context frame on this page and the sixth in the drop, which makes it one of the better-evidenced proposals here. Job is relief. Register is commercial lifestyle photography, natural daylight, shallow depth, slightly soft focus on the subject's face. Ground is blurred foliage and a dark fence, mid in value and moderately saturated, which is the darker third of the corpus distribution. G3 is not engaged. G6 holds, no words appear. G9 is obeyed: her eyes are down and her expression is neutral, so the frame does not ask a face to carry evidence. The detail worth recording is the detached lid held in her free hand — it is the only element in three wordless frames that teaches anything mechanical, and it does so incidentally. Strong: an unposed act with the product doing its only job. Weak: the focus is softest exactly on the bottle's label area, so the one identifying feature in the frame is the least legible thing in it.

A two-panel comparison with a hard vertical divide and a dark 'VS.' tab at the top. The left panel is headed 'Regular Water Bottle' and shows a disposable plastic bottle carrying a red disc with a white cross; the right is headed 'Hydrovia Hydrogen Bottle' and shows this product bubbling, carrying a green disc with a white tick. Three claim lines sit beneath each, separated by rules: plastic waste, microplastics in the water, repeat purchases against eco-friendly bottle, hydrogen-infused, lasts for years. This is the two-panel comparison device as the type defines it and the SECOND instance on this page after img-11 fused version. Job is spec. This is the most rule-compliant comparison frame in six batches and it is worth saying why. G3 is obeyed exactly: red carries the wrong side, green carries the confirmation, and neither colour appears anywhere else. G4 is obeyed: the right panel is measurably brighter and cleaner than the left. G5 is obeyed: both sides are photographic. A6 is satisfied: the state is switchable, since buying this really does remove the disposable. Register is knockout product photography on a blue gradient. Ground is pale blue, light and moderately saturated. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. Strong: three claims a side, marked, weighted and lit correctly — the market reproducing four of this library's rules without being told them. Weak: 'microplastics in the water' is a health claim about a rival category with nothing behind it.

deviations.observed: a large hero product shot occupies the left half beside the step column, so the tile identifies the object and instructs at once

breakdown: A headline 'Easy to use & clean' over a split tile: the left two thirds hold a black dehumidifier on a side table in a pale room, the right third a column of three captioned panels showing the water tank being removed, opened and emptied, each with blue directional arrows. The captions read 'Put Out The Water Tank', 'Open The Tank Cover', 'Dumping The Water'. The order is carried by vertical position and by the captions, with no numerals, which is the labelled variant of the sequence type. The one structural decision is the hero: the type as written is a set of equal panels, and here a large product photograph sits beside the sequence so the tile does two jobs at once. Job is use. Register mixes commercial lifestyle photography for the hero with knockout product renders for the three panels, a register shift inside one tile that the type does not legislate. Ground is a pale room for the hero and white for the panels, both light and low in saturation. G3 is engaged by the blue arrows, and blue is what the rule assigns to correct flow, so the usage is defensible. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. G15 is satisfied, the panels pack their column rather than striping the whole square. Strong: showing the tank at three stages answers the one maintenance question this product class raises. Weak: the panels are small and the arrows do most of the work at tile size.

A headline 'Say Goodbye to Damp' with a support line naming a capacity of up to 450ml a day. The white dehumidifier stands on a round table in the middle of the frame. To its LEFT the room is drawn damp — condensation on a window, water droplets everywhere, a blue-grey cast — with white arrows flowing INTO the machine. To its RIGHT the room is clear and warm, with arrows flowing OUT past bubbles and green leaves. Two bubble marks label the two halves: 'Before 80%' at the left and 'After 45%' at the right. This is a before-and-after made as ONE frame with the product as the boundary between the two states, and that is exactly the shape argument-fault A8 asks for: a change of state needs a BOUNDARY, not two states side by side. It is the first frame in seven batches to satisfy A8 properly, and the boundary is the product itself, which is the most economical form the rule could take. The device is a directional through-flow rather than an emanation — air enters one side and leaves the other changed — so it does not file against the emanation proposal raised on clou-diaxi. Job is mechanism. Register is a product photograph composited into a rendered room with vector flow marks. Ground is a pale interior, light and low in saturation. G3: the arrows are white and carry direction rather than state. Strong: the frame teaches the whole mechanism with no diagram. Weak: both percentages are bare figures with no source anywhere on the page.

A headline 'Semiconductor Dehumidification' with a two-line support. The product is rendered with its casing cut away so the internal Peltier cooling block sits visible above the transparent water tank, the tank filled with blue water and a large three-dimensional '2200ml' figure floating inside it. Two outlined claim pills sit at the lower left, 'Dehumidification capacity approximately 45 percent' with a thermometer icon and 'Dehumidification approximately 450ml' with a droplet. Bubbles and green leaves drift across the frame. This is the see-through-interior device arguing a SPEC rather than a mechanism, which is the recombination raised on fosen-ring in batch C, and this is its SECOND distinct source. Job is spec: the frame argues capacity, and the internals are how it shows the capacity rather than what it is claiming. Register is a product render, not a photograph. Ground is a pale interior, light and low in saturation. G3 is engaged by the blue, which here is the water rather than a signal. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. Both figures use an approximation sign, which is the second time in this drop a page has declared the PRECISION of its own number rather than asserting it flat — gripi-mata stated a manual measurement error band, this one hedges with a tilde. Both are the honest behaviour A15 is waiting for a rule about. Strong: the tank figure set INSIDE the water is the clearest way to attach a capacity to a volume. Weak: 'Hight-efficiency' in the support line is a misspelling.

A headline about seven-colour LED lights for a soothing sleep atmosphere, three circled line icons with labels beneath them — sleep, 7 Light, Timer — and below them a photograph of a woman asleep in bed with the black product standing at the right inside a large rainbow light arc. This is the claim-stack construction with a spec job and it is the FIFTH distinct source for that proposal, after clou-diaxi, fosen-ring, glowy-liff and hydrovia. Five distinct sources CLEARS SPEC 6.3's criterion 1 for it, which makes it the second proposal in this drop to get past that bar after the dimension type. What remains open is criterion 2, and it is a real question rather than a formality: this construction and the nine-source relief-job claimstack are the same picture with a different job, and the router-confusion test between them has never been run. Job is spec. Register is commercial lifestyle photography with a composited light arc and flat vector icons. Ground is a dark bedroom, which is the darker third of the corpus distribution and is earned here because the claim is about light. G3 appears engaged and is not: the rainbow arc is the product's own LED output. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. Strong: the arc is the product's output drawn at room scale, which is more persuasive than a swatch row. Weak: 'romanticand' has lost its word space, the third lettering error this drop has found in a real page.

A horizontal band of five circular photographic vignettes runs across the top of the frame, each captioned: Mouldy Corner, Wet Clothes, Water Condensation, Respiratory Problems, Wood Damage. Below them the black product stands on a round table in a pale room, with a large iridescent glass shield graphic composited beside it. This is the symptom rail in its BASE form — a hero photograph with a vignette band listing symptoms — where clou-diaxi in batch B carried the band-only variant with no hero. So the two sources in this drop show the type at both its full and its reduced form, which is the cleanest possible evidence for a variant. Job is symptom: the tile widens the problem across five complaints rather than naming one. Register is commercial lifestyle photography with five stock vignettes and one rendered graphic. Ground is a pale room, light and low in saturation. G3 is not engaged; the shield is iridescent white rather than a signal colour. G11 is NOT used — the vignettes stay in full colour where clou-diaxi desaturated everything but the afflicted area — which is the second page in this drop to leave that instrument on the table. G6 is broken by the caption layer. Strong: five complaints, five photographs, all of them physical consequences rather than feelings. Weak: the shield is a mark that supposes protection rather than stating anything, which is A2's fault.

A headline 'Ultra-Quiet Technology' with a support line, a woman asleep in a blue-lit bedroom with the white product on the nightstand, a large figure reading 'greater than or equal to 32dB' at the upper right, and across the foot a horizontal SCALE: three circular vignettes on a connecting line, labelled 15dB with autumn leaves, 32dB with the product itself, and 50dB with a group of people talking. The device is the scale: a measured figure placed on an axis between two familiar anchors so a reader can judge it against things they already know. That is a genuinely distinct construction and this registry has no id for it; it is also the THIRD instance in this drop of a page substantiating its own number properly, after capix-mat's tape measure and gripi-mata's declared error band. Job is proof. Two faults are worth recording precisely because the device is otherwise the honest one. The anchors are mislabelled — 15dB and 32dB BOTH read 'Leaves rubbing', so the middle anchor names the wrong reference. And the headline figure is written with a greater-than-or-equal sign, which claims the product is AT LEAST 32dB, the opposite of the quietness being sold. Register is commercial lifestyle photography with three composited vignettes. Ground is a dark bedroom. G3 is not engaged. Strong: the idea is the best substantiation instrument in the drop. Weak: its own labels break it.

deviations.observed: a hero product carrying its own callout occupies the left half beside the two state panels

breakdown: A headline 'Auto Shut Off Protection' with a two-line support. The left half holds the black product with its water gauge lit RED and a labelled pill on a leader reading '2200ml large water tank'. The right half holds two stacked panels of the same tank photographed identically: the upper lit blue and captioned 'Working normally' with a green tick, the lower lit red and captioned 'Water tank full' with a red cross and three numbered consequences. The two panels are the locked-frame construction — same subject, same framing, one variable changed, the reader judging — and the one structural decision is the hero with its callout alongside. Job is proof. This frame is the second-most rule-compliant in the drop after hydrovia's VS tile, and the reason is worth stating: G3 is obeyed FOUR times over, with blue for the correct working flow, red for the stop state, green for the confirmation tick and red for the cross, and not one of those colours is used for anything else. What makes it unusual is that those are the PRODUCT's own indicator colours, so here the manufacturer's LED code and this library's colour lock agree exactly — the first time in seven batches. Register is commercial product photography throughout. Ground is a pale wall and wooden surface. Strong: the state pair answers the only real objection to a tank product. Weak: 'No more worriers' is a misspelling of worries.

deviations.observed: a hero lifestyle scene occupies the upper two thirds above a four-cell context rail, so the tile argues one placement in depth and four more in passing

breakdown: A headline 'Remove Excess Moisture In The Air' with a support line. The upper two thirds are a laundry-room scene: a woman sitting cross-legged with a basket of washing, holding up a damp shirt, the black product at the right with white airflow marks, bubbles and green leaves drifting between them. Across the foot runs a rail of four captioned photographic cells — Living Room, Bedroom, Office, Cloakroom. The grid type's argument is that one unit serves many places, and the one structural decision here is that a single placement is given a full hero scene while four more are reduced to a rail. Job is use. This is the same hero-plus-rail shape the page used in img-03 for a sequence, which makes it a page-level layout habit rather than a property of either type — worth recording so curation does not read it as two independent variants. Register is commercial lifestyle photography with composited vector marks for the hero and four stock cells for the rail. Ground is a pale laundry room, light and low in saturation. G3 is not engaged; the airflow marks are white. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. G15 is satisfied. Strong: the hero gives one context enough room to be believable, which a four-cell grid alone never does. Weak: the bubble-and-leaf marks are decorative and say nothing the airflow lines do not.

A clean two-by-two photographic grid, each cell showing the white product in a different place with a caption tab: Living room, Bedroom, Office, RV. No headline, no support text, no marks. This is the grid type at its purest and it is the FOURTH distinct source for the type in this drop. Job is use; device is grid; G15 is satisfied, a two-by-two packing the square. The finding is in the lettering. The product's own printed 'Dehumidifier' badge is legible and correct in the first cell and MALFORMED in the other three — letterforms smeared, spacing collapsed, characters that are not characters. That is the signature of a generated image, and it means this real market page ships AI-rendered frames carrying the exact fault this library measures in its own render ledger. The quality flag is set accordingly. Its importance is not that the page cheated; it is that the corpus this library learns from is no longer purely photographic, so a frame's register can no longer be inferred from the fact that it appears on a real page. Register is generated product photography in four composited interiors. Ground varies by cell, all light to mid in value. G3 is not engaged. G1 would bind hard and is broken by the page's own asset: the product is not the same object in all four cells, since its printed mark differs. Strong: four placements, one glance, no paragraph. Weak: three of four products carry gibberish.

deviations.observed: the product is composited into an IMPOSSIBLE setting — an indoor appliance standing outdoors in deep snow — to literalise the claim

breakdown: A headline 'Automatic Defrost Function' with a support line about the machine recognising dehumidification regardless of season. Below it the black product stands on a snow-covered deck in front of snow-laden trees and a snowy cabin roof, with a blue circular snowflake badge at the lower left. The construction is the page-hero form — one photographic scene with a baked headline making a spec claim — and the one structural decision is the setting, which is not a place this product could be. A mains dehumidifier does not stand in a snowdrift, and the scene exists only to make the word 'defrost' literal. This is the SECOND instance in this drop of a page building an impossible setting to literalise a claim, after gripi-mata composited a bath mat onto cloud forms in batch E. On that frame the record said one instance is not a gap and two would be. This is the second, so it is now a gap: G7's context integrity refuses a product in a place it could not be, and the corpus does it deliberately, twice, in two unrelated categories. Job is spec. Register is a product render composited into a stock winter photograph. Ground is snow, very light and near-neutral. G3 is engaged by the blue badge, which here reads as cold rather than as correct flow. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. Strong: nobody misreads what defrost means after seeing this. Weak: the shadow under the product falls the wrong way for the scene's light.

The product photographed twice on a pale ground, three-quarter at the left and rear-on at the right, with three dimension lines — 140mm across the depth, 270mm down the height, 170mm across the width — and below them a panel headed 'Specifications' carrying six label-and-value pairs: Material ABS, Power 25W, Working Voltage AC100-240V 50/60Hz, Noise 32-38db, Water tank capacity 2.2L, Product size 170x140x270mm. This is the SIXTH distinct source for the dimension proposal and the SECOND instance of the FUSED form, where the dimension device and the table device appear as two zones of one tile rather than as separate tiles — glowy-liff img-19 was the first. Two sources for the fusion is the evidence that decides whether they are one type with two zones or two types that commonly pair, and it now exists. Job is spec. Register is knockout product photography above flat typography. Ground is white and pale grey. G3 is not engaged. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. The internal contradiction is the finding: this tile states the noise as 32-38db while img-08 on the same page headlines 'Ultra-Quiet Technology' with a figure of 32dB and anchors it against leaves rubbing. The specification's own upper bound is six decibels louder than the marketing tile's floor, and both frames sit in one gallery. Strong: every figure here is checkable against the unit. Weak: the page contradicts itself in the two tiles a buyer would compare.

A headline 'Details' over three horizontal bands, each pairing a close product photograph at the left with a heading and a short support line at the right: 'LED Digital Panel / Function display is clear at a glance' over the lit control panel, 'Portable Handle / Mobile convenience' over the moulded rear grip, 'Pull Out Water Tank Design / Easy to clean' over the tank sliding out with blue arrows. This is the macro-paired-with-text variant in the band layout and the FOURTH distinct source for it — clou-diaxi as a checkerboard, fosen-ring and now moisosat as bands, gripi-mata as circles over the subject. Four sources and three layouts is enough for curation to decide whether the layout is a parameter or three variants. Job is spec. At a square ratio three horizontal bands is STRIPING rather than packing, which G15 refuses for multi-frame layouts, and this drop's tally on that rule is now clear: the checkerboard and the circles pack, the bands stripe, and the bands are the commonest form in the corpus. Register is knockout product photography throughout with flat typography. Ground is white and pale blue. G3 is engaged by the blue arrows in the third band, carrying direction. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. Strong: three components, three named benefits, no paragraph. Weak: the third band's benefit, 'Easy to clean', is a claim the photograph does not show, where the other two are visible facts.

A two-line headline over a gold support bar, and below it a solar mosquito lamp mounted on twin poles at dusk in a garden, its three UV tubes glowing magenta behind a wire grid, white electric arcs drawn across the grid and three mosquitoes composited around it. This is the page-hero construction — one photographic scene carrying a baked headline making a spec claim — and it is the fifth distinct source for that proposal across the drop. Job is spec: the headline names the power source and the category. Register is a product render composited into a dusk garden photograph. Ground is a deep blue night sky, which is the darker third of the corpus distribution and is earned absolutely here, since a UV lamp has no argument against a light ground. G3 is engaged and defensible: the arcs read blue-white and the tubes magenta, and blue is what the rule assigns to a working mechanism. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. The arcs and the mosquitoes are MARKS rather than photography — no camera records an insect mid-electrocution at this scale — and they are the frame's whole evidence, which puts them under A2: a mark states, it cannot suppose. Here they state something the product genuinely does, so the fault is mild. Strong: the dusk setting is the only time this product is visible at all, so the scene is honest about when it works. Weak: the gold support bar carries three claims in one line at the smallest type on the tile.

A headline 'Can Be Used Both Outdoors And Indoors / Dual Charging Mode' with a support line about solar energy and mains supply. The lamp stands in a flower bed against a picket fence in soft daylight, angled so the solar panel on its roof is the most legible element in the frame, UV tubes lit and arcs drawn across the grid. Same page-hero construction as img-03, so a match. Job is spec: the claim is the dual power path and the picture puts the solar panel where the eye lands first. Register is a product render composited into a garden photograph. Ground is a bright garden, light and moderately saturated, which is the corpus's ordinary two thirds and a deliberate reversal of img-03's night — the page shows the same object in day and in night to argue it works in both, which is the same reasoning img-15 later makes explicit as a split. G3 is engaged by the arcs. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. The tile has one internal oddity worth recording: the tubes are drawn LIT in full daylight, which contradicts img-15's claim that the lamp turns itself off during the day. Strong: tilting the panel toward the camera is the cheapest way to make a power claim visible. Weak: the frame contradicts a claim the same page makes two tiles later.

A headline 'Fearless Of Wind And Rain / IPX5 Waterproof Rating' with a two-line support. Two units stand in heavy rain beside a lake at dusk, one on poles and one on a low ground base, both lit, rain streaks drawn across the whole frame. Page-hero construction, job spec, match. What this frame does that the page's other hero tiles do not is put the product under the STRESS the claim is about: an ingress rating is invisible on a dry object, and rain in the frame is the cheapest way to make it legible. That is the same instinct behind capix-mat's tape measure and moisosat's decibel scale — a claim shown under the condition it concerns rather than asserted beside a dry product. Register is a product render composited into a rainy dusk photograph. Ground is a dark lake and sky, the darker third of the distribution. G3 is engaged by the arcs. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. The rating itself, IPX5, is a standards figure with nothing in the frame to substantiate it, which is the ordinary A15 position; the rain is evidence of the CLAIM's subject rather than of the rating. Strong: two mounting forms in one frame, shown incidentally rather than argued. Weak: rain drawn as uniform diagonal streaks across the product reads as a filter rather than as weather.

A headline about long-lasting eradication for one night and an upgraded high-capacity battery. The lamp is shown at a steep angle with its right end-cap cut away so the interior is visible: stacked circuit boards, a lens module, and a central chip lit magenta and labelled 'AI'. The rest of the frame is the lit grid with mosquitoes and arcs. This is the see-through-interior device arguing a SPEC, and it is the THIRD distinct source for that recombination after fosen-ring and moisosat, which puts it past SPEC 6.2's evidence threshold of three. Job is spec. Register is a product render, not a photograph. Ground is near-black. G3 is engaged by the magenta and blue, which are the product's own emission rather than marks. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. Two faults are worth recording together. The headline claims a BATTERY and the cutaway shows CIRCUIT BOARDS — the component named is not the component revealed, which makes the x-ray decorative rather than evidential. And the chip is labelled 'AI', a capability claim asserted by a two-letter label on a rendered component, which is the same invented-technology device hydrovia used with 'HydroCharge' and which this category reaches for whenever a mechanism would need explaining. Strong: an interior is genuinely interesting on a sealed outdoor product. Weak: it is the wrong interior for the claim above it.

deviations.observed: the grid is DISSOLVED — one context fills a whole tile with its own label tab, and the page spends a separate gallery slot on each context instead of packing them into cells

breakdown: A gold label tab in the upper left reading 'Fish pond for aquaculture', and below it the lamp on twin poles beside a still pond at night, trees and a far bank behind, arcs across the grid and two mosquitoes in frame. There is no other text. The argument is placement — this is one of the places the thing goes — which is the grid type's job, and the one structural decision is that the grid has been taken apart: instead of four contexts in four cells, the page gives one context a whole tile and repeats the tile. Three more follow on this page. This is the same slot-spending behaviour the drop has now recorded five times in seven sources under a different guise — capix-mat three colourway cards, clou-diaxi two claim stacks, fosen-ring three identity composites, glowy-liff an eight-cell plug matrix, gripi-mata two colourway demos — and it is the clearest statement yet of the underlying habit: a direct-response gallery spends a slot rather than compressing a variable. Job is use. Register is a product render composited into a night photograph. Ground is a dark pond and sky. G3 is engaged by the arcs. G6 is broken by the label tab. Strong: a pond at night is a context a grid cell could never establish. Weak: four tiles doing what one grid does.

A headline 'Four Major Upgrades / Mosquito Core Technology' with a support line naming a 395nm wavelength favoured by mosquitoes and flies. The frame is a steep low-angle view along the lamp's face so the three UV tubes run away to a vanishing point, magenta light filling the whole picture, white arcs crawling across the grid and several mosquitoes caught in them. The product's visible OUTPUT is the subject and the object is barely legible as a shape, which is the configuration G8 legislates and the emanation device raised on clou-diaxi in batch B. This is its SECOND distinct source. Job is mechanism. Register is a product render, dramatically lit by its own emission. Ground is near-black, the darkest frame in the drop. G3 appears engaged and is not: the magenta is the product's own UV output rather than a signal mark, the same distinction glowy-liff's LED modes forced. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. The wavelength figure is substantiated nowhere. Strong: the perspective makes an ordinary grid look like a mechanism, which is exactly what an emanation frame is for. Weak: the mosquitoes are rendered at a scale that would make them the size of a hand, and at tile size they read as debris.

A two-line support at the top about a built-in temperature control system that simulates the temperature mosquitoes prefer, with no headline. Below it a close three-quarter view of the lamp's end, tubes lit magenta and white, arcs branching across the grid in a dense web, and one large mosquito rendered mid-electrocution at the centre. Second emanation frame on this page and a match. Job is mechanism. Register is a product render lit entirely by its own emission. Ground is near-black. G3 is not engaged as a signal system. G6 is broken by the support line. The claim is the finding: a temperature-simulation mechanism is asserted in text over a picture that shows only light and electricity, so the frame's evidence and its claim are about different things — the same mismatch img-08 makes between a battery headline and a circuit-board cutaway. Twice on one page is a habit rather than an accident, and it is worth naming because the library's own types are built the opposite way round: a skeleton names what the picture must SHOW and the copy follows it. Strong: the arc web is the most legible drawing of the killing action on the page. Weak: nothing in the frame is about temperature.

A gold label tab reading 'Camping in the wilderness', and below it two units — one on poles, one on a low base — lit in a night campsite, with a tarp shelter strung with festoon lights, four people at a table, a parked SUV and mountains behind. Second dissolved-grid context tile on this page and a match to the variant img-09 proposes. Job is use. Register is a product render composited into a night photograph. Ground is a dark sky and grass, the darker third of the distribution. G3 is engaged by the arcs. G6 is broken by the label tab. What this frame adds over img-09 is PEOPLE at a distance, which is the only human presence in sixteen frames on this page: the campers are small, unlit and turned away, so no face carries any argument, which is G9 satisfied by composition rather than by intent. It also does the one thing a context tile can uniquely do — it shows the product at a distance from the people it protects, which is a spatial claim about coverage that no close frame could make. Strong: the scene explains the product's poles, which every other tile leaves unexplained. Weak: two units in one campsite implies a coverage limit the page never states.

A headline 'Strong mosquito attraction ability / 3 tubes of purple light to lure mosquitoes' with a two-line support naming the 395nm wavelength and comparing the attraction to magnetism. The lamp sits on its poles over dark grass, and large concentric magenta wave rings are drawn radiating outward from it across the whole frame, with mosquitoes drawn flying inward along them. Third emanation frame on this page. Job is mechanism. Register is a product render composited into a night photograph with vector field marks. Ground is near-black. The wave rings are the finding and they are the clearest A2 breach in the drop: a mark states, it cannot suppose, and these rings assert an attraction FIELD that has no visible existence — the support line says the attraction is 'like magnetic attraction', and the frame draws the simile as if it were a photograph of a physical thing. Compare the arcs in img-10, which draw something that genuinely happens; the difference between the two marks on one page is the difference A2 exists to name. G3 is not engaged as a signal system, the magenta being the product's own emission. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. Strong: the rings make an invisible claim locatable, which is what A3 asks. Weak: what they locate does not exist.

A headline 'Fully automatic light control system / Turn off lights during the day and work at night' with a two-line support. The frame is divided by one hard vertical line: the left half is bright daylight over a house and lawn with the lamp UNLIT, the right half is a deep blue starfield with the same lamp LIT in magenta. The product runs continuously across the divide as ONE object. This is the fused-silhouette form of the split, the same structural move hydrovia img-11 made with a crushed plastic bottle becoming the product, and it is the SECOND distinct source for it — which turns a single observation into a real variant. It is also the second frame in the drop to satisfy A8 properly: a change of state needs a BOUNDARY rather than two states side by side, and here the boundary is a line through one continuous object, where moisosat img-04 made the product itself the boundary. Two different solutions to the same rule, from two unrelated categories. Job is spec. G5 is satisfied, both halves are the same register. G4 is engaged and INVERTED by necessity: the correct state is the dark half, because the product working is the night half, which is the one legitimate case for a darker correct side the rule's scope note would have to admit. Strong: one object, two states, no explanation. Weak: the divide falls across the product's face rather than at its edge.

A gold label tab reading 'Park Scenic Area', and below it the lamp on twin poles beside a lit footpath at dusk, with a low modern building, bollard lights and a bench behind it. Third dissolved-grid context tile on this page. Job is use. Register is a product render composited into a dusk photograph. Ground is a violet dusk sky and lit lawn, mid in value and moderately saturated. G3 is engaged by the arcs. G6 is broken by the label tab. This frame is the one where the dissolved-grid decision pays for itself: a park at dusk with warm path lighting establishes SCALE for a product whose size is otherwise unreadable — the lamp reads against a bench and a building, which no grid cell at a quarter of this size could do. That is the honest counter-argument to the slot-spending finding this drop keeps recording, and it belongs in the ledger beside it: compressing four contexts into four cells costs the scale cue, and for a pole-mounted outdoor product scale is the doubt. Strong: the bench. Weak: three of the four context tiles on this page are dusk or night and read as one place.

A headline 'Electric mosquitoes do not harm people' with a support line about an external protective net with a one-centimetre gap preventing children from touching the grid. A human hand reaches in from the left and presses a finger against the outer net, and a large magenta shield outline with a tick inside it is composited over the product. Page-hero construction, job spec, match. The frame carries two kinds of evidence and they are worth separating. The HAND is real evidence: a finger on the net, at the gap the copy describes, demonstrating the claim in the only way a still can. The SHIELD is a mark that supposes — it asserts protection rather than showing it, which is A2's fault, and it is drawn in magenta with a tick, where G3 reserves the tick's meaning for green. So one frame makes the same claim twice, once honestly and once decoratively. G13 is relevant and handled correctly: the copy invokes children and the frame shows an adult hand, which is the safe choice and the one this library would require. Register is a product render composited into a dusk photograph with a vector mark. Ground is a dark garden. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. Strong: the finger. Weak: the shield.

deviations.observed: the subject is drawn at three overlaid positions to show its range of adjustment, so the claim stack sits beside a motion diagram rather than a still product

breakdown: Four claim lines run down the left, each a large gold figure with a small white support beneath it: '3-5 hours full / High photoelectric conversion', 'over 10 years / long service life', 'Increase by 46 percent / Strong response to weak light', 'Suitable for 4 seasons / Good weather resistance'. At the right the solar panel is drawn at THREE overlaid angles, two of them ghosted, with a gold labelled pill on a leader reading 'Adjustable sun cup angle'. This is the claim-stack construction and the SIXTH distinct source for it. The one structural decision is the ghosted multi-position subject: the frame shows a RANGE OF MOTION by overlaying the same part at three positions, which is a device this registry has no name for and which no other frame in seven batches has used. Job is spec. Register is a product render composited into a night garden. Ground is dark grass and foliage. G3 is not engaged; gold is not a signal colour. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. 'Increase by 46 percent' is a bare percentage with no baseline and no source — increase over what is never stated — which puts it with hydrovia's 'up to 30 percent' at the bottom of A15's scale. Strong: the ghosted positions teach adjustability in one glance. Weak: four figures, four claims, not one of them checkable.

The lamp drawn as an exploded assembly against a near-black ground: the solar panel lifted clear above, the protective net drawn out to the left, the U-shaped shock net and the three UVA tubes separated in the middle, the stainless tripod below. Six gold labelled pills sit around it on dashed leaders: ABS shell, Solar panel, Protective net, Stainless steel tripod, U-shaped electric shock net, UVA mosquito trap lamp. This is the exploded construction exactly as the type defines it and it is the THIRD distinct source in this drop after capix-mat's fabric laminate and hydrovia's membrane stack, which puts the type past SPEC 6.2's evidence threshold on this corpus. It is also the fullest instance: an explode carrying a full CALLOUT layer, six labels on dashed leaders, which fuses two devices the drop has otherwise seen separately. Job is spec. Register is a technical product render. Ground is near-black with a faint grid, the darkest ground in the drop and the right one for a render whose subject is pale. G3 is not engaged; gold is not a signal colour. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. G15 is not engaged, this is one frame. Strong: six named components, every one visible and separated, and the assembly order readable from the geometry alone. Weak: the protective net is drawn flat and reads as a second grid rather than as a cage.

deviations.observed: dimension lines and a five-chip icon rail are fused into the claim stack, so one tile carries four devices at once

breakdown: The most overloaded tile in eight batches. A headline '10W three tube' with a support line; seven gold claim pills down the left from 'Applicable area 10-1200 square metres' through '3000V high-voltage power grid' to 'Automatic mosquito control at night'; five dimension lines on the product reading 30cm, 18cm, 23cm, 85.5cm and 46.5cm; two white accessory cards showing a charging cable and a grass tripod; and across the foot a rail of five icon chips naming modes. Four devices — claim stack, dimension, accessory inventory and icon rail — in one square. The one structural decision recorded is that fusion. Job is spec. Register is a product render composited into a dusk garden photograph with three flat graphic systems over it. Ground is a warm dusk garden, mid in value. G3 is not engaged. G6 is broken comprehensively. The figure worth recording is 'Applicable area 10-1200 square metres': a hundred-and-twenty-fold range, which is not a specification but a refusal to give one, and it sits in the same pill list as a precise 3000V. Strong: everything a buyer might ask, in one tile. Weak: seventeen separate text elements in one square is past every count this library has measured, and the dimension lines — the only checkable facts here — are the least legible thing in the frame.

A headline 'Pure physical safety mosquito control / Maternal and infant level radiation free protection' with a support line claiming no harmful chemical ingredients. Below it the lamp on its poles at night against a deep blue sky, a lit modern house behind, arcs across the grid and four mosquitoes around it. Page-hero construction, job spec, match, and the fifth spec-hero frame on this page alone. Job is spec. Register is a product render composited into a night photograph. Ground is a deep blue night sky, the darker third of the distribution. G3 is engaged by the arcs. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. The claim is the finding and it is the most aggressive on the page: 'Maternal and infant level radiation free protection' asserts a SAFETY GRADE for the most vulnerable possible users, with no standard named, no test named and no body named — a claim of exactly the class A15 was written about, in the one domain where an unsubstantiated claim does the most harm. The frame handles G13 correctly by showing no child, but the copy invokes infants directly. Strong: the composition is the cleanest of the page's five hero tiles, with the product isolated against sky rather than competing with foliage. Weak: the claim, which no picture on this page could substantiate and which the page does not try to.

deviations.observed: a COMPATIBILITY BAR of six third-party platform marks runs across the foot of the tile

breakdown: An indoor pan-tilt camera stands on a wooden desk in warm daylight. Four line-icon claims sit in a two-by-two at the left — 4MP HD and Infrared, Two-way Intercom, Motion Detection, Pan 360 Tilt 180 — with the headline 'Indoor Smart Camera' beneath them. Across the foot runs a grey bar carrying SIX third-party marks: Alexa, Google Assistant, MOES APP, Smart life, WiFi and Tuya. This is the claim-stack construction and the SEVENTH distinct source for it. The one structural decision is that bar, and it is the finding: this library has refused two mark classes so far, the certification seal and the press mark, both under the trademark question the owner declined on 2026-08-18. A COMPATIBILITY bar is a third class and it is different in kind — it does not confer authority on the product, it states an interoperability fact a buyer can verify by trying it. Nothing in G16, G14 or the two LAW rows reaches it, and it appears on two of this page's sixteen frames. Job is spec. Register is commercial product photography with flat graphic overlays. Ground is a wooden desk and pale wall, light and low in saturation. G3 is not engaged. G6 is broken by the declared text layer and by six logos, which G6 bans outright. Strong: four claims, four icons, one product, one glance. Weak: the compatibility bar is the smallest type on the tile and carries the most legally-loaded content.

Two stacked panels. The upper shows a golden retriever bounding down a staircase with a blue detection bracket drawn around it and a red siren icon beside it. The lower shows an infant standing in a cot crying, a red audio waveform drawn across the frame, and a phone at the left carrying two lock-screen notifications, 'Motion detected' and 'Sound Detected'. The device is the SIGNAL mark: brackets, waveforms and notifications drawn over a scene to show a sensing action that has no visible existence. Job is mechanism. G3 is obeyed exactly — blue for the correct sensing, red for the alert state — and this page uses that pairing consistently across four frames. **G13 is engaged and breached twice.** Its three rules are no private-room setting, no age in years, and a minor's face block limited to attention, effort or ordinary discomfort, never tearful or crying. This frame puts a minor in a cot in a bedroom and shows that minor CRYING. That is precisely the configuration G13 describes as a REFUSAL class — a prompt this library could not render at all — and finding it in a real market page is the finding: a baby-monitor category has a gallery slot the library structurally cannot fill, and no amount of prompt craft changes that. Register is stock photography with flat vector marks. Ground is a pale staircase and nursery. Strong: the two panels name the two sensors separately. Weak: the crying infant.

A headline 'Quick-Access Collected Sites' over a pale living room, with four numbered blue map pins dropped onto points in the space and a phone at the left showing the app: a live view of the same room, a zoom control, a row of function buttons and a 'Site' strip holding three saved thumbnails with a fourth slot reading 'Site added succe...'. The argument is carried by the INTERFACE — what the app can do is the product's value — and the ledger already carries this id at eight observations from a single source, which is the largest observation count with the smallest source count in the whole corpus. This is its SECOND distinct source. Job is proof. The type is one of the three A15 blocked, alongside the statistic and the instrument, because a skeleton has to say where its content comes from and a rendered UI is a claim about software behaviour that no frame substantiates. Register is commercial interior photography with a composited phone and flat vector pins. Ground is a pale cream room, light and low in saturation, at the top of the corpus distribution. G3 is engaged by the blue pins, correct for a working mechanism. G6 is broken by the declared text layer and by a rendered UI full of words. Strong: the pins and the app thumbnails show the same three places, so the interface and the room agree. Weak: the truncated 'succe...' string is a rendering artefact left in a shipped asset.

A headline 'Siren Alerts For Motion & Sound Events'. A figure in a black balaclava and gloves carries a laptop through a dark living room, a red detection outline traced around his whole body, the camera on a sideboard glowing red with a red siren bolt drawn above it, and a phone at the right carrying the notification 'Human body detected'. Second signal frame on this page and a match. Job is mechanism. This is the closest thing to a step-one PAIN frame in nine batches, and it is worth recording against the routing finding this drop has been carrying: mapping/pdp-dr-rules.md recorded 01-pain-scene and 01-pain-split as absent from all twenty-six earlier sources, and nothing here changes that — this is not a pain scene, it is a THREAT staged so the sensing marks have something to detect. The person is a prop for the mechanism, not a reader the frame asks to recognise themselves. G3 is obeyed: red for the intruder outline, red for the alarm, and the blue of the other frames is absent because nothing here is working correctly yet. Register is stock photography with flat vector marks. Ground is a dark interior, the darker third of the distribution. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. Strong: the outline lands on the thing being detected, which is A4 satisfied. Weak: the balaclava is a costume stereotype doing the work a real scenario would.

A headline 'View Video Recordings Anywhere' over a pale living room, with a phone at the centre showing the app's live view of a small child playing on a rug, and three recorded-clip cards floating around it — a dog and a cat asleep together, a cat, and an infant sleeping in a cot — each stamped with a date and time. A blue cloud icon at the left reads 'Cloud Storage'. Second interface frame on this page. Job is proof. G13 is engaged by two minors and handled differently from img-04: the toddler is in a living room with a neutral attentive expression, which is compliant, while the sleeping infant is in a cot in a private room, which breaches the setting rule but not the expression one. So this single page contains three frames with minors at three different G13 states — one clear breach, one partial, one compliant — which is the most useful G13 evidence the ledger has ever held in one place. Register is commercial interior photography with a composited phone and stock clip cards. Ground is a pale cream room, light and low in saturation. G3 is engaged by the blue cloud mark. G6 is broken comprehensively. Strong: showing the recordings as separate cards makes the storage claim concrete. Weak: the clip timestamps are identical on two cards, so the set reads as a mock rather than a history.

A headline 'TF Card Storage' over the camera on a wooden table, a blue card-insertion graphic drawn onto its body, a blue capacity card at the left listing 32 GB, 64 GB and 128GB, and across the foot a black film-strip rail holding four recorded scenes. Page-hero construction, job spec, match. The frame carries three different graphic systems — an insertion diagram on the object, a capacity list beside it, and a footage rail beneath it — which is the same overloading habit mozzapx img-20 showed at its extreme, in a milder form. Register is commercial product photography with flat graphic overlays and four stock interior cells. Ground is a wooden table and pale wall, light and low in saturation. G3 is engaged by the blue, correct for a working mechanism. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. The capacity figures are physical specifications checkable against the product, the A15-benign class. The film strip is the interesting element: it is a use-grid rail doing duty as EVIDENCE of the storage claim, showing what is stored rather than what the product does, which no type in this registry currently describes. Strong: the insertion graphic answers where the card goes without a callout. Weak: the film-strip cells are too small to read as anything but wallpaper.

deviations.observed: the subject is drawn at three ghosted positions to show motion over time inside the monitored zone

breakdown: A headline 'Monitor The Specified Area Only'. A pale living room carries a large blue rectangle with corner nodes marking the monitored zone; a man in an orange top walks through it drawn at THREE overlaid positions, the two earlier ones ghosted and the final one solid with a red detection bracket and red motion marks at his foot; the camera sits on the coffee table; a phone at the left carries 'Human body detected'. Third signal frame on this page. The one structural decision is the ghosted multi-position subject, which shows motion over time in a still — and it is the SECOND distinct source for that device after mozzapx img-18 overlaid a solar panel at three angles to show its range of adjustment. Two sources, two different jobs, one device: showing MOVEMENT by drawing the same thing more than once. That is a real cluster and this registry has no name for it. Job is mechanism. G3 is obeyed: blue for the monitored zone, red for the detection. Register is commercial interior photography with flat vector marks and a composited phone. Ground is a pale room, light and low in saturation. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. Strong: the zone rectangle and the walk-through together make a spatial claim no single pose could. Weak: the ghosts read as three men before they read as one man moving.

A headline 'WDR For Clear Imaging' over a two-panel comparison of the SAME living room from the SAME camera position, divided by one vertical line: the left half washed out and hazy with blown highlights, the right half clear with detail held in both the window and the shadows. Pill labels read 'WDR OFF' and 'WDR ON'. This is the best-formed comparison in nine batches and the reason is A6. That rule asks a comparison to be of a SWITCHABLE state, and here the state is switchable in the most literal sense available: it is a setting toggle on the product itself, so removing the culprit really does restore the harm and restoring it really does remove it. Nothing else in this drop meets the rule that exactly — hydrovia's apple slices approximated it, gripi-mata's mat comparison approximated it, this one IS it. G4 is obeyed, the correct side is brighter and cleaner. G5 is obeyed, both halves are the same register. The camera is locked, the framing identical, exactly one variable changed. Job is proof. Register is commercial interior photography. Ground is a warm cream room, light and low in saturation. G6 is broken by the two pill labels. Strong: everything. Weak: the improvement is drawn rather than photographed through the product's own lens, so the claim is illustrated at a quality the camera will not deliver.

A headline 'Preset Point In Smart Linkage'. A dark entryway with a door standing ajar to a street; a smart lock on the door carries a blue circular targeting reticle with a labelled pill reading 'Preset point'; three dotted blue sight lines run from the camera, which sits on a shelf in a white cabinet at the right, across to the lock. Fourth signal frame on this page, and the page's signal set is now the largest single-device run in the drop after glowy-liff's plug matrix. Job is mechanism.
