G3 is obeyed: blue throughout for a working, correct aim, with no red because nothing in the frame is in an alert state. Register is commercial interior photography with flat vector marks. Ground is a dark entryway with a bright doorway, mid in value. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. What this frame does that the other three do not is draw the camera's ATTENTION as a physical line across a room, which makes a software preset into a spatial fact — the same instinct behind the monitored-zone rectangle of img-09 and the detection bracket of img-06, applied to an invisible configuration rather than to an event. Strong: the sight lines give a preset a place, which is A3 satisfied for something that has no location at all. Weak: the open door to a street is the frame's most striking element and has nothing to do with the claim.

A headline 'Privacy Mode' over a woman asleep in a white bed, with the camera on the nightstand at the right, its lens body rotated fully DOWN and back so the optic faces away from the room, and a blue crossed-out-camera icon floating above it. Page-hero construction, job spec, match. The frame is one of the strongest in the drop on evidence and it is worth saying why: the claim is a privacy state, and the state is PHYSICALLY VISIBLE in the object — the lens is turned away, which a reader can see and check, so the blue icon is a label on a fact rather than a mark that supposes one. Set that against glowy-liff's green jaw contour or mozzapx's protective shield, both of which assert what the photograph does not show. G9 and A3 are both satisfied by the product's own posture. Job is spec. G13 is not engaged, the subject is an adult. Register is commercial lifestyle photography with one flat vector mark. Ground is white bedding and a pale wall, the lightest frame on the page. G3 is engaged by the blue icon, which reads here as a state rather than as correct flow. G6 is broken by the headline and the icon. Strong: a mechanical privacy shutter photographed in its closed position is the whole argument, and the tile trusts it. Weak: a sleeping subject in the same frame makes the tile read as a monitoring scene rather than a privacy one.

A headline 'Freely Switch Resolution: HD/SD' over a two-panel comparison divided by one vertical line, with pill labels 'Standard Definition' and '4MP High Definition'. The left half is softer and lower in contrast, the right sharper. Second locked-frame comparison on this page and a match — but it breaks on the rule img-10 satisfies perfectly, and the contrast between the two frames on one page is the finding. **The two panels are DIFFERENT ROOMS.** The left shows a doorway with a cactus and a step down to a terrace; the right shows a window seat with cushions, two round tables and a chair. So the single-variable control is gone: a reader cannot tell whether the right half is sharper because of the resolution or because it is a different photograph. That is the SECOND instance of a broken control in this drop after hydrovia's three different apple slices, and both occur in the one type whose entire discipline is that exactly one variable changes. Job is proof. A7 is not the problem — SD against 4MP is far past the two-to-one floor. G4 and G5 are satisfied. Register is commercial interior photography. Ground is a warm cream interior, light and low in saturation. Strong: the pill labels are clear and the divide is clean. Weak: the comparison compares nothing.

deviations.observed: the leaders are curved MOTION ARCS naming a range of movement rather than straight leaders naming a static part

breakdown: A headline 'Pan 360 Tilt 180 HD Camera'. The camera sits large at the right of a warm living room with two curved blue arrows drawn around its axes — one arcing over the head labelled 'Tilt 180', one circling the base labelled 'Pan 360' — and a phone at the lower left showing the app's live view with a thumb on a joystick control. The callout construction with one structural decision: the joining forms this library has legislated are the leader line, the dashed leader and nothing, all of which connect a LABEL to a PLACE, and these connect a label to a MOVEMENT. A curved arc around an axis names what the part can DO rather than what it is, which is a different job for the same device. Job is spec. It belongs with the ghosted-position device of img-09 and mozzapx img-18 as a third way this corpus draws motion in a still, and three instances across two sources is enough for curation to look at them together. G3 is obeyed, blue for a working mechanism. Register is commercial interior photography with flat vector marks and a composited phone. Ground is a warm cream room, light and low in saturation. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. Strong: two arcs, two numbers, and the whole articulation is legible in one glance. Weak: the phone repeats the claim a third time and adds nothing.

A headline 'Two-Way Voice Intercom'. A small child in a striped dress sits on a rug with a toy tea set, looking toward the camera which stands on a low table; two speech bubbles carry the exchange, a white one from the child reading 'I'm playing with my toys.' and a blue one from the device reading 'What are you doing baby?', with a 'Push to talk' pill at the right. Fifth and last signal frame on this page. Job is mechanism: the bubbles are marks that make an audio channel visible. **G13 is engaged and this frame is COMPLIANT**, which matters because img-04 on the same page is not. The setting is a living room rather than a bathroom, bath, shower or bedroom; no age is stated; and the child's expression is attention rather than distress. Read together, this page holds a clear breach, a partial and a compliant frame, which is the most useful G13 comparison the ledger has. One thing no rule here reaches: the frame puts invented WORDS in a minor's mouth. G14 governs fabricated endorsement and says nothing about attributed speech, and a speech bubble over a child is a different problem from a quote beside an avatar. Register is commercial lifestyle photography with flat vector marks. Ground is a warm living room, light and low in saturation. Strong: the two bubbles show direction without an arrow. Weak: the invented line.

A headline 'Clear Infrared Night Vision'. A woman lies in bed in a dark room looking at her phone, and a large phone frame at the lower right shows the app's greyscale infrared feed of an infant asleep in a cot, with zoom, record and microphone controls around it. Third interface frame on this page. Job is proof. G13 is engaged and partial: the infant is in a cot in a private room, which breaches the setting rule, but is asleep with a neutral face, which satisfies the expression rule. The frame is also the page's clearest statement of what the product is FOR, and it is worth noting that the most persuasive tile on a camera page is the one where the interface shows the thing the buyer is anxious about. Register is commercial lifestyle photography with a composited phone carrying a greyscale stock image. Ground is a dark bedroom, the darker third of the corpus distribution, earned here because the claim is about darkness. G3 is not engaged; the frame has no signal colour at all, which is unusual on a page that uses blue and red consistently elsewhere. G6 is broken by the declared text layer and the rendered UI. Strong: the greyscale feed is the right register for an infrared claim, and the ambient darkness of the room makes the claim legible without a comparison. Weak: the phone's own screen brightness lights the woman's face more than an infrared scene would.

A white tile headed 'Dimensions'. The camera is shown twice on a plain ground, three-quarter at the left and side-on at the right, with three dimension lines: 64mm/2.52in across the lens housing, 73mm/2.87in across the base, 111mm/4.37in down the full height. Nothing else is in the frame. This is the SEVENTH distinct source for the dimension proposal — capix-mat, clou-diaxi, fosen-ring, glowy-liff, gripi-mata, moisosat and now pawdi-cas — which makes it the best-evidenced new cluster in the entire drop, past criterion 1 by two sources. The device has been consistent across all seven: a line spanning a distance with arrowheads and a dual-unit label, drawn beside or onto the object, distinguishable from a callout because a callout's leader points at a PART and names it while a dimension line measures a SPAN. Job is spec. Register is knockout product photography on white with soft contact shadows. Ground is white, at the top of the corpus value distribution. G3 is not engaged. G6 is broken by the dimension labels. Every figure is a physical dimension substantiated by the object itself, the A15-benign class, and given in both metric and imperial as fosen-ring's did. Strong: two views and three numbers answer the question completely. Weak: the two views are close enough in angle that the third dimension is inferred rather than shown.

deviations.observed: a COMPATIBILITY BAR of six third-party platform marks runs across the foot of the knockout flat-lay

breakdown: A knockout flat-lay on white: the camera at the left, a white USB cable coiled beneath it, a circular wall-mount plate at the upper right, three wall plugs and three screws laid in rows below it. Across the foot runs the same six-mark compatibility bar as img-03 — Alexa, Google Assistant, MOES APP, Smart life, WiFi, Tuya. This is the identity type's with-contents form and the one structural decision is the bar, which appears twice on this page and is therefore a page-level habit rather than a one-off. Job is identity; device is pack; setting is the knockout form that needs no G7 exemption. Including the mounting hardware is the frame's real work: it answers whether the thing can go on a wall, which is a question the page's other fifteen tiles never touch. Register is commercial knockout product photography, broad even light, no cast shadow. Ground is white. G3 is not engaged. G6 is broken by six logos, which that rule bans outright and which no exemption in this library covers. Taken across the drop, 07-identity-pack has now appeared in six of the ten sources, which makes the earlier finding firmer: on a direct-response product page the identity family is a SET of angles, states, contents and shipping variants, not the single frame the type legislates. Strong: screws and plugs shown at actual count. Weak: nothing gives scale, so the plate could be any size.

A blue headline 'WALL DETECTOR SCANNER' at the upper left, a black card beneath it headed 'THREE DETECTION MODES' with three yellow icons and labels — Wooden, Cable, Metal Detection — and two blue claim pills below, 'PRECISE POSITIONING' and 'LITHIUM BATTERY POWERED'. The product stands at the right, shown twice, front with its lit display reading 12cm and Center 100 percent, and rear with the Type-C port and power button. This is the claim-stack construction and it is the EIGHTH distinct source for that proposal across the drop, the most widely evidenced new cluster after the dimension type. Job is spec. Register is a product render on white, no photography. Ground is white, at the top of the corpus value distribution. G3 appears engaged and is not: the yellow, red and green ring around the marking hole is the product's own indicator, and this page later states its code explicitly. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. The display reading is diegetic and legible, which matters because this page carries the product's UI in eleven of sixteen frames and the ledger now has a source where the interface is the argument rather than the decoration. Strong: three modes as three icons is the fastest possible statement of what the thing does. Weak: showing front and rear in one tile without labels leaves the rear view doing nothing.

deviations.observed: each cell carries a CUTAWAY revealing the hidden target that mode detects, so the grid shows three mechanisms rather than three placements

breakdown: Three vertical panels. Each shows the detector held against a concrete wall with a ragged cutaway opened above it revealing what is behind — a steel bar, three copper cables, a timber stud — blue signal arcs running from the device up into the opening, and the display reading a result. Beneath each panel a black block carries an icon, a title and an explanation: METAL DETECTION, CABLE DETECTION, WOODEN DETECTION. The grid type argues that one unit does many jobs; the one structural decision here is that each cell opens the wall to show the TARGET, so the tile teaches three mechanisms rather than three placements. Job is use. The finding is in the cable panel's copy: 'Detects live cables under walls(Non-live cables may be detected by metal objects or not detected by the detector)'. That is a page stating a LIMITATION of its own product inside a feature tile — the fourth instance of honest substantiation behaviour in this drop, after a tape measure, a declared measurement error band and a decibel scale. A direct-response page volunteering what the thing cannot do is rare enough to be worth the ledger's attention. Register is a product render composited into a concrete wall. Ground is grey concrete, mid in value. G3 is engaged by the blue arcs, correct for a working mechanism. Strong: the cutaway makes an invisible sensing action locatable. Weak: three dense paragraphs at tile size.

deviations.observed: the reading order is carried by the product's own DISPLAY STATE rather than by numerals, captions or arrows

breakdown: A blue panel at the upper left reads 'EASY TO USE' with a support line about calibrating before every scan. Below it three units stand in a row on a concrete wall, each with a different display and indicator state: the first reads 0 percent with a green ring, the second Edge 70 percent with an amber ring, the third Center 100 percent with a red ring and a pencil marking through the hole, a cutaway above it showing the stud found. This is a sequence and the one structural decision is how its ORDER is carried. The base type forbids numbers and text outright because the order is meant to be read from the actions; ADR-066 added the labelled variant when numerals and captions appeared. Here it is neither: the order is carried by the product's own DISPLAY, a rising percentage and a changing indicator colour, which is a fourth mechanism and the only one of the four that is diegetic. Job is use. The colour code is the finding and it is stated in words on img-14: green means no target, red means on target. G3 assigns green to confirmation and red to pain, wrong or broken, so this product's own indicator is INVERTED against the library's colour lock — the sharpest of the three product-colour collisions this drop has recorded. Register is a product render on concrete. Strong: three states of one object teach a procedure with no instruction. Weak: nothing says these are three moments rather than three units.

deviations.observed: the obstruction is cut away so the sensed target is visible, and the signal's REACH is given as a published maximum per material

breakdown: Three horizontal bands, each pairing a cutaway wall at the left with a black text block at the right. The cutaways show a timber stud, a bundle of copper cables and a length of rebar, each with blue signal arcs running from the device to it and the display reading a result. The text blocks name the mode and give depths: stud detection at 0.75inch/19mm exact and 1.5inch/38mm depth scan, cable detection at 2inch/50mm for AC wire and 1.57inch/40mm for single-strand copper, metal detection at 4.7inch/120mm magnetic and 4inch/100mm non-magnetic. This is the SECOND distinct source for the signal proposal raised on pawdi-cas, and the one structural decision is that the obstruction is opened so the sensed thing is visible, which makes the signal's reach legible rather than asserted. Job is mechanism. A13 is engaged directly — how deep the cut goes is a claim about how far the product reaches — and this frame handles it better than any other in the drop: the depths are published specifications given in two units, attached to a named material, rather than point figures floating on a rendered section. Register is a product render composited into concrete. Ground is grey concrete, mid in value. G3 is engaged by the blue arcs. Strong: six numbers, six materials, all checkable. Weak: the arcs are identical in all three bands, so the frame draws one signal for three different physics.

The detector large on a grey wall with a cutaway at the left showing rebar, cables and timber behind it, blue signal rings spreading from the device. At the right two captioned insets sit stacked: 'MARK THE HOLES', a close shot of a pencil pushed through the device's marking aperture, and 'SAY NO TO ERRORS!', a close shot of a drill bit entering a clean hole in plaster. This is the macro-paired-with-text variant, here in a hero-plus-inset-column layout, and the insets do the thing a macro is for: they show a part and an outcome that the main frame cannot resolve. Job is spec. The marking aperture is the product's one genuinely distinctive physical feature and this is the only frame on the page that shows it being used. Register is a product render composited into a wall, with two photographic insets. Ground is grey concrete, mid in value and low in saturation. G3 is engaged by the blue rings and by the product's own indicator ring, which here shows red on the left edge and green on the right — the inverted code again. G6 is broken by the two caption bars. The second inset is the page's only image of a FINISHED result rather than a state of the tool. Strong: pencil through the hole is the whole product in one gesture. Weak: 'SAY NO TO ERRORS!' is the only exclamation on a page that is otherwise plain, and it reads as a different writer.

The detector shown large at a three-quarter angle on a grey surface, with EIGHT labels on thin right-angled blue leaders: CURRENT DETECTION MODE, PROBE SIGNAL STRENGTH, THE DISTANCE FROM THE MEASURED OBJECT TO THE DETECTION CENTER, INDICATOR LIGHT BEEP ON-SCREEN PROMPTS, METAL CABLE DETECTION, WOODEN FENCE DETECTION, POWER DISPLAY, DEPTH DISPLAY. Four of the eight point at regions of the display rather than at physical parts. This is the callout construction and a clean match, the fourth distinct source for the type in this drop. Job is spec. Eight labels is past the type's legislated band of three to six and exactly at the count its founding round tested and held, so the frame is evidence that the tested ceiling is the real one rather than the written band. The leader form is the right-angled line, one of the three ADR-066 legislated. Register is a product render on a grey ground with a small cutaway at the left edge. Ground is grey concrete, mid in value and low in saturation. G3 appears engaged and is not; the ring is the product's own indicator. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. Strong: every label points at something visible, which is the type's own binding rule and the thing twelve-label frames break. Weak: labelling four screen regions on a screen that is itself a photograph makes the frame a manual page rather than a gallery tile.

deviations.observed: the interface is the product's OWN display rather than a companion app on a phone

breakdown: A hand holds the detector against a dark blueprint-grid ground, blue signal rings behind it, and the product's screen shows a SETTINGS menu: a left column listing SENSITIVITY, LANGUAGES, VOLUME, LENGTH UNIT, SLEEP and RESET, and a right panel of sensitivity levels for each of the three modes as L, M and H checkboxes. This is the THIRD distinct source for the interface proposal — the ledger held eight observations from one source, pawdi-cas added a second, and this is the third, putting it past SPEC 6.2's evidence threshold. The one structural decision is where the interface lives: pawdi-cas argued through a companion APP on a phone, and this argues through the product's OWN screen. That is a real distinction, because a phone app is a claim about software the frame cannot verify while an on-device menu is a photograph of the thing being sold. Job is proof. It remains one of the three types A15 blocks, and this frame is the strongest argument for unblocking it: a settings menu on the product's own display is as substantiated as a printed label. Register is a product render on a dark graphic ground. Ground is dark navy, the darker third of the distribution. G3 is engaged by the blue rings. Strong: six settings visible at once answers the configurability question completely. Weak: the menu type is small enough that only the highlighted row is legible at tile size.

A yellow headline 'WALL DETECTOR SCANNER' at the right over three blue claim pills — Lithium Battery Powered, New Structural Design, Precise Positioning — with the detector at the left held against a concrete wall, a cutaway at the far left showing rebar and cables behind it, blue signal rings spreading outward and the display reading 12cm Non MAG Center 100 percent. Second claim stack on this page and a match. Job is spec. The construction is the page's default and it carries three of sixteen frames, which makes it this source's commonest tile after the macro family. Register is a product render composited into a concrete wall. Ground is grey concrete, mid in value and low in saturation. G3 appears engaged and is not; the indicator ring is the product's own code. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. What separates this from img-04 is only the setting — that one was a white studio knockout, this one is in a wall — and setting is a runtime parameter, so the two are one argument shipped twice. That is the slot-spending habit this drop has now recorded in seven of ten sources, here in its mildest form: not a colourway matrix, just the same claim set against two backgrounds. Strong: the cutaway gives the claim pills something to be about. Weak: three pills that name a battery, a design and a capability have no order and no hierarchy between them.

The same construction as img-12 with one variable changed: the product's display is a white backlit LCD showing blue graphics rather than the black OLED showing yellow. Headline, three claim pills, wall, cutaway, signal rings and framing are otherwise identical. A display variant is a runtime parameter in the same class as a colourway, which vocabulary.parameters names as a value that must never become identity, so this is absorption-ladder level one and the verdict is a match adding no type evidence. Job is spec. Register is a product render composited into a concrete wall. Ground is grey concrete. G3 appears engaged and is not. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. Recorded rather than skipped because the runbook requires one record per batch image, and because the pair is a useful instance of a variable this drop has not otherwise seen: capix-mat repeated colourways, glowy-liff repeated plug territories, fosen-ring repeated colourways, and this page repeats a SCREEN TYPE. All four are the same behaviour — a page spending a gallery slot on a cell of a product matrix — and the fourth variable class strengthens rather than dilutes the finding. Strong: the two displays are genuinely different products to a buyer choosing between them. Weak: nothing in either tile says which one they are getting.

A headline 'Multiple predictions / Safety work' with a support line 'See through walls like Superman'. Three offset white cards run down the right, each pairing a macro photograph with a text block: the lit screen with 'The screen data shows / Target depth, Arrive at the detection center, Detect material'; the glowing indicator ring with 'Indicator Light / Lights up yellow/red depending on target distance, Green light (No target)'; and a close of the device edge with red sound arcs and 'Beep alert / It will beep when a target is detected'. Macro-paired-with-text in a staggered-card layout, the fourth of six layouts this variant has shown across the drop after the checkerboard, the bands and the circles. Job is spec. The middle card is the most valuable text in this batch: it STATES the colour code in words — green for no target, yellow and red as the target nears — which confirms explicitly what img-07 showed. G3 assigns green to confirmation and red to pain, wrong or broken, so a product whose success state is RED and whose null state is GREEN inverts the library's lock completely. That is now documented in the corpus rather than inferred. Register is product macro photography on a dark grey ground. Ground is dark grey, the darker third. Strong: three sensory channels named separately. Weak: 'like Superman' is the page's only simile and it sits under a safety claim.

Two panels divided by a diagonal. The left shows the detector on a concrete wall with a pencil pushed through its marking aperture, captioned 'New Structural Design&Precise Positioning'. The right shows the device lying on a grey surface with a Type-C cable entering it and the display showing a green 100 percent battery ring, with a labelled callout 'Type-C Charging Port'. Macro-paired-with-text again, here in a diagonal-split layout — the fifth distinct layout for this variant in the drop. Job is spec. Register is product photography on concrete and on a grey surface. Ground is grey throughout, mid in value and low in saturation. G3 is engaged twice and both are the product's own: the indicator ring on the left, and the battery ring on the right where GREEN means full — which is the one place this product's colour code agrees with the library's, since green as confirmation is exactly what G3 assigns. So the same device uses green for confirmation on its battery display and green for NO TARGET on its detection ring, which means the inversion is not even internally consistent. Recorded because a reader of this ledger looking for colour evidence needs both halves. G6 is broken by the caption bars. Strong: the two panels answer two unrelated doubts without a headline. Weak: the diagonal divide crops both subjects awkwardly.

deviations.observed: a hero scene occupies the upper two thirds above a three-cell application rail

breakdown: A blue headline 'SAFE DRILLING WIDE APPLICATION'. The upper two thirds show a bearded man in a pale room looking up at a ceiling while a hand at the right holds the detector against a wall, blue signal rings around it. Across the foot runs a rail of three photographic cells: a man drilling a door frame, two men lifting a large television onto a wall bracket, a man fitting an air-conditioning unit. The argument is that one unit serves many jobs, which is the grid type's purpose, and the one structural decision is the hero above the rail — the SECOND distinct source for that layout after moisosat img-10. Job is use. Register is commercial lifestyle photography for the hero and three stock cells for the rail, with a composited product render. Ground is a pale room, light and low in saturation. G3 is engaged by the blue rings. G6 is broken by the headline. G15 is satisfied. The three applications are the page's only argument about WHO buys this, and all three are trades rather than householders, which contradicts the domestic framing of img-16's own hero. Strong: a television bracket is the single most recognisable reason to own a stud detector and the page finds it. Weak: the hero's subject is looking at a ceiling while the hand holds the device against a wall, so the two halves of the photograph are doing different things.

A man in overalls drills into a pale wall at the left while a hand at the right holds the detector up, blue signal rings around it and the display reading 12cm Center 100 percent. Across the foot a blue band carries the headline 'LET THE DRILL NO LONGER BE DANGEROUS' and six ticked items in two rows: Stud Edge, AC Wire, Metal Pipes/Rebar, Wooden Beams, Joist, Stud Center. Claim-stack construction with the claims as a ticked list along an edge rather than a stack at the side, which is the rail form recorded on gripi-mata in batch E. Third claim stack on this page. Job is spec. The tick marks are BLUE rather than green, and G3 reserves green for the confirmation badge, so six confirmation marks on this page are drawn in a colour the rule assigns to correct flow instead. Minor, and worth recording only because this page's colour behaviour is otherwise the most documented in the drop. Register is commercial lifestyle photography with a composited product render. Ground is a pale room, light and low in saturation. G6 is broken by the declared text layer. Strong: six targets named as a checklist is the clearest statement of scope on the page, and it answers the buyer's real question, which is what it will and will not find. Weak: the drill is already in the wall, so the frame shows the danger happening rather than being avoided.

A headline naming what the product locates behind walls, floors and ceilings, with the detector lying on a concrete ledge beneath it inside blue signal rings. The lower two thirds are a stacked cutaway of four wall sections, each with a different target embedded and a labelled depth: a timber batten with 'Wooden: less than or equal to 38mm', a cable bundle with 'AC wires: less than or equal to 40mm', a copper pipe with 'Metal pipes: less than or equal to 100mm', and rebar with 'Rebars: less than or equal to 120mm'. Second signal frame on this page and a match. Job is mechanism. This is the best A13 handling in the drop and the reason is the INEQUALITY sign. A13 says how deep the cut goes is a claim about how far the product reaches; glowy-liff stated 4.0mm and 4.5mm as point depths on a rendered tissue section with nothing behind them, and this states four MAXIMA, each attached to a named material and each drawn against that material in section. A maximum is a falsifiable claim; a point depth on a render is not. Register is a product render composited into four rendered wall sections. Ground is brick and concrete, mid in value. G3 is engaged by the blue rings. Strong: four materials, four limits, drawn where a buyer can see the difference between a batten and rebar. Weak: the four sections are rendered rather than photographed.

A headline 'EVERY DETAIL IS METICULOUSLY POLISHED' over a two-by-three grid of six macro photographs, each with a blue caption bar: ANTI-SLIP TEXTURE ON THE SIDE, ABS SHOCKPROOF SHELL, THROUGH-TYPE ACRYLIC PANEL, SILICONE FEEL BUTTONS, TFT HD COLOR SCREEN, TYPE-C CHARGING. This is the cleanest instance of the macro-paired-with-text variant in the whole drop and the SIXTH layout it has shown — checkerboard, bands, circles over the subject, staggered cards, diagonal split, and now a plain packed grid. Six layouts across six sources for one variant is the clearest possible statement that LAYOUT is a parameter of this construction rather than its identity, which is the question curation has to settle. Job is spec. At a square ratio a two-by-three PACKS the frame, which is what G15 asks and which three of this drop's macro frames fail. Register is polished macro product photography throughout, consistent light across all six cells. Ground is pale grey behind the cells, light and low in saturation. G3 is not engaged. G6 is broken by the caption bars. G1 binds across six layers and holds: the same object in all six. Strong: six genuinely different surfaces, none of them decorative, and the light is the same in every cell so the set reads as one product. Weak: the acrylic panel cell is dark on dark and reads as a shadow.

deviations.observed: a circular X-RAY inset showing the internal battery is added to the plain knockout

breakdown: A knockout of the detector on white, seen square-on with its display reading 12cm MAG Center 100 percent and its indicator ring lit amber and red, with soft blue signal rings spreading behind it. At the lower right a circular inset shows the device's interior with a blue-lit battery cell and circuit traces visible through a cutaway. No text anywhere in the frame. The base is the identity argument in its plainest form and the one structural decision is the inset, which is not a magnified detail but an X-RAY — it shows something the object does not present at all. That distinguishes it from clou-diaxi's operating inset in batch B, which showed the same object doing its job. Job is identity; device is pack; setting is the knockout form that needs no G7 exemption. 07-identity-pack now appears in SIX of the ten sources in this drop, which is the firmest version of the finding this drop has carried since batch C: on a direct-response product page the identity family is a SET of angles, states, contents, shipping variants and interior views, and the type as drafted legislates one frame. Register is a product render on white with a rendered inset. Ground is white. G3 is engaged by the blue rings and by the product's own indicator. G6 holds, not a word appears. Strong: a wordless tile that still says what the thing is and what is inside it. Weak: the battery inset is the fourth x-ray on a page that never states a capacity.

deviations.observed: the wrong-vs-right argument is carried by two separate stacked caption cards, Before above After, drawn as rendered dental illustration, instead of one split inset with a seam

breakdown: A smiling blonde woman cropped at the nose and chin fills the right half, her teeth and gums clean and even, gaze off-camera. Two units of the product, black and white, stand side by side in the centre on a navy band that runs along the foot of the frame. The left third carries a headline, '#1 Water Flosser For Healthy & Clean Gums', and under it two stacked rounded cards: 'Before' shows rendered teeth with brown deposits at a reddened gumline, 'After' shows the same teeth clean. The argument is step-6 relief: the healthy mouth is the state after buying, the product stands beside it, and the insets supply the wrong-vs-right proof the face cannot. That is 06-relief-hero with a vsinset, and the one structural decision is the inset form: two captioned cards in illustration rather than one split inset with a seam. The setting is a blank pale blue-grey studio gradient, not the real room the type's SETTING asks for, which is an execution of the commercial register rather than a second structural decision. G3 is honoured: red lives only on the Before gumline. G4 is not: the After card is no brighter than the Before card. G9 is served by the insets, since the smile alone would be emotion rather than evidence. G7 is strained: two units stand in a portrait they could not be in, composited rather than placed. G1 across two colourways holds, same build in both. G16 LAW row 2 is breached by '#1', a ranking with no source. Ground is light and low in saturation apart from the navy band. Strong: result, product and proof in one glance at thumbnail size. Weak: the product is present rather than used, and the headline's claim is the page's least substantiated line.

breakdown: The white unit stands on a real bathroom counter beside a basin and a chrome tap, toiletry bottles out of focus behind it, the whole frame pale blue-grey. A translucent drawn dial of tick marks arcs behind the product like a battery gauge; it is a graphic, not anything in the room. A solid navy rounded panel in the upper right carries two figure-and-label pairs: '4 hours / Full Charging Time' and '30 days / Extended Battery Use'. The argument is step-3 spec: one photograph, one baked text block, one capability — the battery. That is 03-spec-hero, and it is that type's own named failure mode: the product is merely present, nothing in the frame charges or runs, and the drawn gauge stands in for the claim the scene does not show. The words sit in an opaque panel rather than in a band the photograph leaves empty, which the type's QUIET AREA part records as the minority habit. A15 is breached twice and the page proves why it matters: the same page's FAQ says the battery lasts 'about 2-3 weeks' and its gallery slide 8 says 'Holds charge for 30-40 days', so one page gives three answers to one question and sources none of them. G3 is not engaged; the gauge and type are white on navy. G7 holds: a bathroom counter is where the product lives. G8 is not engaged. The ground is a real room, light and low in saturation, which is ADR-068's ordinary case. Strong: large legible figures and a setting that places the object. Weak: bare durations the page itself contradicts, over a product doing nothing.
notes: source file: densjet-nova__gallery-2.jpg. Densjet Water Flosser, offer.warehousetopdeals.com/products/nova-ss1-test/. In stills as pdp-dr/gallery-2.jpg; gallery slide 2 of 14 on the reference page.

breakdown: A headline '6 Reasons Why' across the top of a deep blue radial gradient. The black unit stands centred in the lower two thirds, cropped by the bottom edge through its water tank. Six white rounded pill labels ring it, three a side: 'Switchable Nozzles', '3 Custom Cleaning Modes', 'Advanced Water Jet Technology', 'Precise & Gentle', 'Good For Sensitive Gums', 'Long-Lasting Battery'. The labels are joined not to parts but to each other, by one continuous dashed circle with a small dot node at each pill — the arc joining form, observed before on hydrovia img-04 under an almost identical '5 Reasons Why' pill ring. The argument is step-3 spec by a ring of satellites around the object, which is the callout device, and the joining form is that type's declared parameter, so this is a match. The execution breaks the type's own callouts part: only 'Switchable Nozzles' and '3 Custom Cleaning Modes' sit near a part they name; the other four name a quality or a hidden component, and a label with no place on the object is A2 wearing a pill. That is the boundary with 03-spec-claimstack this frame blurs, and it is worth holding for the router-confusion test. The ground is dark and saturated — the third of the corpus that chooses it — and nothing in the product emits, so the choice is the brand's blue. G3 is not engaged. G7's arrangement exemption applies, but the tank cut by the frame edge leaves the object incomplete. Seven text clusters, all legible. Strong: six reasons read in one glance. Weak: a benefit list arranged as annotation, over a product the frame does not finish.

breakdown: A headline in navy, two weights, in the upper left: 'Removes Up To' over '29% More Plaque Than Regular Flossing'. Below and behind it, a soft 3D render of four molars on a smooth pale gum ridge. A translucent angled nozzle tip enters from the upper left, passing behind the headline, and its water stream drives into the gap between two molars and blasts dark grey debris particles out with the droplets toward the lower right. No product body appears; the nozzle tip is the only part of the object in frame. The argument is step-3 mechanism at the point of contact: the stream reaches the interdental gap and removes what is in it. That is the 03-mechanism-contact proposal, with two differences from its three earlier sources worth recording for curation: the contact is shown at the surface rather than in a tissue cross-section, and the agent is the product's OUTPUT, a water stream, rather than the product's head. G8 is honoured in a render register: the output is the primary subject. A3 is honoured: the effect is locatable at one gap. G3 is loosely honoured: debris dark grey, water clear and pale cyan, no red. A15 is breached: 'up to 29%' has no source, no n and no comparison protocol, and 'up to' is satisfied by any result — the same floor this ledger recorded on hydrovia's 'up to 30%'. The ground is pale blue-white, light and low in saturation. The page uses a clean plate of this same render, with no words, as a section image (benefit-1-gums), so on this page the gallery tile carries the words and the section carries the plate. Strong: the eye lands on the gap. Weak: the headline number, and a tile that never shows what the product looks like.

breakdown: A bold white headline '3 Powerful Cleaning Modes' in the upper left of a deep blue gradient. The white unit stands large on the right, buttons to the lens, cropped through the nozzle at the top edge and through the tank at the bottom. Down the left, three circular 3D dental illustrations each carry a mode beside it: 'Clean Mode — Suitable for daily use to remove plaque.' over a jet at the molars, 'Soft Mode — Gentle cleaning for sensitive gums.' over a gentler jet at the gumline, and 'Pulse Mode — Alternates water pulses for cleaning tight spots.' over a jet at braces. The argument is step-3 spec: three settings, subject on one side, claims on the other, which is 03-spec-claimstack. It is that type's confirmed claims-carrying-pictures form, here with rendered illustrations rather than photographs; the medium is a parameter, not a second structural decision. Claims are three, the floor of the type's count. G3 is not engaged: the roundels are pink gum and white tooth, and no colour signals. The ground is dark and saturated, the brand's blue, a choice nothing in the product earns. The only figure is the count in the headline. The three illustrations are nearly the same jet on nearly the same teeth, so what separates the modes is carried by the words alone; only the Pulse roundel's braces gives a mode a place it is for. The render family is the one gallery slide 4 uses. Strong: each claim gets a picture of where it acts, the cheapest substantiation a tile can offer. Weak: three pictures that do not differ enough to argue three modes, beside a product the frame crops at both ends.

breakdown: An extreme photographic close-up of a woman's lower face from nose to chin against a pale blue ground, lips parted over metal braces on the upper teeth. A transparent angled nozzle tip enters from the left and meets the brackets with its white tip; water beads on both lips, runs from the lower lip and drips off the chin. No hand, no product body, no text. The argument is operation: the tip reaches between brackets and wire, which answers the braces buyer's first doubt, so the job is use and the device is a close demonstration — the 03-use-demo proposal, whose earlier sources demonstrate one property in the act (press studs mating, a foot sinking into a mat). G8 is only half honoured: the water is visible but reads as spill running off the chin rather than as a jet doing work, so the output is present without being the mechanism. G9 holds: no performed expression, the physical fact carries it. G13: the subject reads as an adult and no age is stated, though braces are a youth cue a writer should not lean on. G7 holds as a real act, lips parted wider than use needs. G3 is not engaged. G6 holds: not a word in frame. On the reference page this is a SECTION image, one of three alternating image-and-text rows under 'Cutting-Edge Innovation', not a gallery slide — and it is the only one of this page's six files with no baked text, where all five gallery slides in this batch carry it. Strong: brackets and tip in one frame, legible at any size. Weak: the product cannot be identified from the tip alone, and the drips read as mess.

breakdown: A split composition with no drawn divider. On the left, two hands hold a compact black camera toward a smiling woman in a sunlit street, and the camera's rear screen shows her portrait. On the right, against a pale wall, a hand holds a smartphone whose screen shows the same portrait inside a social feed. Two drawn curved arrows run between the devices, a blue one from the camera to the phone and a green one back, with a small grey caption, INSTANT SHARE, above them. The argument is a mechanism a photograph cannot show: the camera sends the picture to the phone over WiFi, so the transfer is drawn as a path between the two devices and the result is shown on the receiving screen. That is the 03-mechanism-signal construction, a drawn signal between the product and what it reaches, in a device-to-device form; the earlier sources drew it from a device into a room or into a wall. Job is mechanism, and the page section beside it reads BUILT-IN WIFI. Register is a commercial composite, the camera sharp and the street soft. G3 is not engaged: the blue and the green mark direction, not states. G6: the phone screen carries small interface text and the one overlay word is the arrow caption. G1 appears to hold for the camera. What is strong is that both ends of an invisible link are visible and the result reads without the caption. What is weak is a screen full of interface text, which this library never has a model draw.
